Our mission is to spark a global conversation about how we value nature in our society and inspire a sense of agency in our collective efforts to protect the planet.  Tracks that credit NATURE support her conservation. At least 50% of recording royalties from "feat. NATURE" tracks and 70% of recording royalties on ‘Ecosystem Tracks’ with The Listening Planet and Vozterra are directed to EarthPercent, a registered charity in England and Wales (1188391) and 501(c)(3) non-profit foundation in the US (EIN: 86-3830611), who redistributes funds to high-impact, rights-based conservation initiatives around the world.    Sounds Right current partners include: the Museum for the United Nations - UN Live, EarthPercent, Hempel Foundation, Spotify, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark, The Listening Planet, Limbo Music, Eleutheria Group, L-Acoustics, DistroDirect, VozTerra, William Demant Fonden, 15. Juni Fonden, Aage V. Jensen Naturfond, Plot Shift Media, Concito, Vega, LD Communications, No. 29 Communications, The World We Want, Axum, and Earthrise.   More details and programme info at SoundsRight.Earth  How does that sound?

name: Chill Palm
bio: Wellness Record Label and lifestyle brand 🌴

name: Lovisa Gulli
bio: I create soundscapes in the borderland between dream and reality. Close your eyes and drift away.

name: Ruttik Dhakate
bio: Ruttik Dhakate is an ambient music producer based in Mumbai, India. His work focuses on creating calm, atmospheric soundscapes inspired by nature and stillness. Blending organic textures with minimal compositions, his music is intended to offer listeners a quiet space to reflect and unwind. With a growing catalogue of releases, Ruttik continues to explore sound as a way to slow down and reconnect.

name: Insomnian
bio: For night owls and overthinkers. Tune in, zone out, and let sleep sneak up on you.

name: Qualeis
bio: Quiet harmonies and soothing instrumental sounds for your everyday life.

name: Verdant Nook
bio: Music to quiet the mind.

name: Felix Dekker
bio: something simple and authentic in an unreal world.

name: Toni Ludwig-Graphaüs
bio: Dutch–German ambient composer Toni Ludwig-Graphaüs creates music shaped by the quiet rhythms of nature and the inner landscapes of the mind. His work blends soft drones, organic field recordings, and meditative harmonies to offer a restorative space for grounding and emotional renewal.

name: Asteeõs
bio: An ambient project from Stockholm. With love for analogue and digital soundscapes I created this electronic project to help you slow down time and space.

name: places we go
bio: Oh the places we go :) Environmental relaxing sounds courtesy of URCHN

name: Willow Skies
bio: Willow Skies is a personal project by Swedish musician Palle Hammarlund. Shaped by stillness, nature, and the spaces where sound can breathe and heal. Inspired by silence, forests, soft light, and subtle movements, the music unfolds slowly and organically. Each piece is created for relaxation, mindful breathing, and grounding - gentle music to disappear into, or return to yourself with. Save your favorites <3

name: AuraLoom
bio: AuraLoom (Jeremy Siegel) is a project that combines ambient synthesis inspired by New Age music with the organic textures of Neo-classical composition. The name itself reflects this fusion: ‘Aura’ evokes the atmospheric, intangible qualities of synth washes and ambient soundscapes, while ‘Loom’ represents the tangible, woven textures of instruments like piano and strings. Through music, Siegel creates moments of reflection, relaxation, and good vibes.

name: Quiet Point
bio: Hey! I'm a composer originally from Boston, MA currently living in Los Angeles, California. Quiet Point is an artist project I created to help listeners relax and unwind through lush ambient pads paired with peaceful (and sometimes experimental) textures.  Reach me any time at max.musicandsound@gmail.com and follow along visually @quietpointofficial on IG.  I'd love to hear from you - thanks for listening!

name: Fourth Eye
bio: Welcome to a world of smooth ambience and soft melodies, entering you into a realm of pure relaxation and solstice. Whether you’re drifting off to sleep, winding down for the evening, or needing a break from the stresses of life, Fourth Eye welcomes you.

name: Echo Veil
bio: Echo Veil is the ambient and frequency-based project of producer and instrumentalist Vicky Singh.  Built around expressive guitar textures and immersive tonal environments, Echo Veil’s music blends organic instrumentation with subtle production to create deeply atmospheric soundscapes. With an intuitive sense for tone and emotional pacing, Vicky crafts compositions that move between stillness and resonance, music designed to be felt as much as heard.  An extremely gifted musician and producer, Echo Veil is steadily building a passionate and growing listener base, with streams continuing to rise as audiences connect with the project’s calming yet emotionally rich sonic identity.

name: Halo Healing
bio: Halo Healing is the sonic sanctuary dedicated to the art of frequency music. Every track is scientifically measured before being released, to make sure that our music gives you the benefits of the numerous studies done on frequency music, so wether it’s 432Hz, 528Hz or any other frequency, you can be sure that what you’re hearing, is in the right tuning. Our innovative approach combines sound bath therapy with frequency music, so you hear the specific frequency throughout the whole track or playlist. Whether you’re seeking calm, clarity or connection, Halo Healing offers a mindful escape through music that resonates with your inner being. Breathe deep, press play, and let the frequencies guide you. Similar artists include Nu Meditation Music, Meditative Mind, Theta Realms, Healing Frequencies Music, and Jason Stephenson,  all part of a global movement making frequency-based music accessible and relevant for modern listeners.  Benefits of some of the frequencies: 432Hz: Known as the golden frequency. A universal frequency with benefits such as stress reduction, enhanced sleep, and pain reduction.  528Hz: The love frequency or the miracle tone. Linked to love, DNA repair, healing, and universal connection.  852Hz: Promotes spiritual connection, inner peace and higher consciousness.  963Hz: Promotes enlightenment, awakening and connecting with universal wisdom.

name: Van Monet
bio: The ambient project of Paris-based musician Van Monet. Painting with sound instead of light, his music transforms the subtle textures of the City of Light into expansive, dreamlike soundscapes for quiet moments.

name: Yu Su
bio: Tapping into an expansive repertoire of “fourth world” ambience and left-field dance music, Yu Su’s emotion-packed compositional punches are best described as organically groovy jazz-bient expeditions between coasts. A proficient instrumentalist who conjures up moments of natural and synthetic beauty, her delicate, dub-inflected signature balances a variety of luminous and wistful downtempo textures. As a DJ, she holds a highly unique voice, crafting evocative musical narratives which touch on a wide-range of influences and personal introspections.

name: Noah Florence
bio: Noah Florence is an ambient project filled with dreamlike sounds and immersive textures.

name: Whatever The Weather
bio: Across a remarkable run of releases in barely half a decade, London’s Loraine James has established her identity through a blend of refined composition, gritty experimentation, and unpredictable, intricate electronic programming. While titles released under her given name on the esteemed label Hyperdub, tend toward IDM-influenced, vocal-heavy collaborations, James reserves her alias, Whatever The Weather, for a more impressionistic, inward gaze. On Whatever The Weather II, rich worlds of layered textures flow seamlessly from hypnotic ambience, to mottled rhythms, to cut-up collages of diaristic field recordings. The result is a uniquely fractured beauty, born from a compelling union of organic and human elements, processed through a variety of digital and analogue methods.  James titled Whatever The Weather pieces based on an innate sense of their “emotional temperature” at the time of recording, but she notes that often, upon revisiting them, they will feel somewhere else entirely on the thermometer; such are the whims of the environment.

name: Memotone
bio: Memotone is a prolific composer and performer from the UK. Growing up in the woodlands of Wessex and now living in Wales. His music explores themes grounded in environmentalism, psychogeography and the unreliable nature of perception. Calling on jazz, classical, folk and ethnic music as well as modern production styles and electronics he builds miniature worlds, and with an extensive back catalogue, there is plenty to explore.    Memotone has releases with World of Echo, The Trilogy Tapes, Soda Gong, Sahko Recordings, Discrepent, Accidental Meetings, 12th Isle, Patience/Impatience, Folklore Tapes and many more.

name: JakoJako
bio: JakoJako is committed to exploring the spaces that emerge between the technical and emotional sides of electronic music, fostering a relationship to sound that implements both rigorous knowledge and unrestrained intuition. Engaged in a constant dialogue around the use of hardware in music, JakoJako’s artistic output is informed by the tension and release of techno, but ultimately coloured by ever-expanding forms and structures that play with the contours of the genre. As a live performer and DJ, she searches for spontaneity amongst the mathematical patterns of arpeggios and loops, locating kinetic energies that convert into moments of dancefloor catharsis. A resident at Berghain, her multifaceted approach has taken her from some of the most respected electronic music festivals in the world to institutions of great cultural significance. Forthcoming on Mute, her album Tết 41 - is an expansion on these ideas. Rhythmic fragments weave between analogue processing and melodic distillations, swirling in organic cycles of warehouse maximalism and sonic minutiae that speak to the somatic and unworldly in equal measure. Recorded in Vietnam during the Tết Lunar New Year celebrations and made with a minimal hardware setup, the album taps into a deep understanding of machine-based music illuminated by references to her heritage, reflecting on notions of rebirth, and the pursuit of a sonic core. From this simplicity emerge some of her most expansive, unworldly compositions to date.

name: Ela Minus
bio: TIEMPO DEFINIDO POR LA PRESENCIA DE LUZ.

name: Yana Couto
bio: Composer and pianist from Poland, Yana Couto blends minimalist melodies with Slavic romanticism, creating music that feels cinematic, intimate, and deeply moving.  She is composing neoclassical, minimal, film, theatre and ambient music with the use of piano, acoustic instruments, field recordings, electronics and layered textures, developing a unique sound. Her compositions are an exploration of leitmotifs and simple melodies evoking feelings and images.

name: OS.SO
bio: OS.SO is a composer, music producer, songwriter and instrumentalist that moves smoothly between musical genres, combining a love of avant-garde sounds and mainstream. Her graduate instrument is the bass guitar, but she also plays the piano, drums, gamelan (Indonesian idiophones) and sings.   She has released two original albums, “Lethe” and “Zachwyt i rozpacz” (Delight and Despair), with music composed to the poems of Polish Nobel Prize winner Wisława Szymborska.  Currently she’s working on a concept album “Isolde” with Yana Couto and is co-founding the duo MonoTony (neoclassical/minimal music) with leading Polish viola player Krzysztof Komendarek-Tymendorf.  As a full-time songwriter and producer, she has participated in many European songwriting and sync camps in cities such as Paris, Budapest, Riga, Berlin, and Warsaw writing more than 200 songs for other artists.  OS.SO also writes poems and directs music videos, combining her passion for literature and short film forms.

name: Banduragirl
bio: BanduraGirl (Anastasiya Voytyuk) is a Ukrainian singer, bandura player, songwriter & social activist.  She is the leader of the folk fusion band Troye Zillia, with whom she has released 4 LP, 2 EP and 5 singles, blending Ukrainian folk traditions with contemporary styles.  In her solo project BanduraGirl, she creates indie-folk songs featuring the traditional Ukrainian folk bandura - a delicate and rarely used instrument with a unique sound. Her music connects tradition with modern indie songwriting and reflects contemporary Ukrainian experiences.  Anastasiya is also the founder of Lviv Bandura Fest, a festival of modern bandura that creates a platform for bandura players to develop, collaborate, and share new music. She is the co-founder of Bandura App, a mobile application where users can play six traditional Ukrainian folk instruments.

name: Christina Vantzou
bio: Christina Vantzou is a Brussels based composer who deals with time expansion, atmospheres and harmonies through electronics and acoustic instruments.  Her releases include five numbered solo albums of ambient-classical music on American label Kranky, 2020's Multi-Natural LP; a foray into abstract electronics and field recording released by the Belgian label Edições CN, two full-length albums with John Also Bennett as CV & JAB, and many other solo and collaborative works.  In her latest work, Vantzou focuses on shaping ceremonial and affective spaces where voice, synthesizers, piano and electronics vaporously extend from the depths, glow in dreamlore and emerge into the light of day.

name: Okkyung Lee
bio: Korean native Okkyung Lee began her career as an experimental cellist with classical training, eventually expanding into fields of improvisation, noise, jazz, and extended technique. Lee has collaborated with many of the bigger names in the noise and experimental improvisation scenes, including performances and recording dates with standout artists like Nels Cline, Ikue Mori, Laurie Anderson, and John Zorn. While solo releases such as Ghil (2013) capture the chaotic aggression of her performances, she has also composed more delicate, reflective chamber works such as 2020's Yeo-Neun. Originally from South Korea, Lee moved to Boston in 1993. She attended the Berklee College of Music, where she graduated with a dual bachelor's degree in Contemporary Writing & Production and Film Scoring in 1998, then earned a master's degree in Contemporary Improvisation from the New England Conservatory of Music in 2000. She relocated to New York City and began recording and performing with a wide variety of improvisers, composers, and rock groups, including Assif Tsahar, Butch Morris, and Raz Mesinai (Badawi). Her first album, Nihm, was released by John Zorn's Tzadik in 2005; featured musicians included Ikue Mori, Trevor Dunn, and Sylvie Courvoisier. She also collaborated with experimental turntablist Christian Marclay on a split album with Italian improv duo My Cat Is an Alien. Lee's solo LP I Saw the Ghost of an Unknown Soul and It Said... appeared on Thurston Moore's Ecstatic Peace! in 2008. In 2010, Lee received a Foundation for Contemporary Arts Grant, which allowed her to tour and collaborate with musicians abroad. She released the Tzadik-issued Noisy Love Songs and worked with artists such as Phil Minton, Evan Parker, and Anla Courtis. In 2013, her abrasive solo album Ghil, recorded by Lasse Marhaug and edited down from hours of improvisations, was released by Stephen O'Malley's Ideologic Organ imprint. Lee also worked with Marhaug and C. Spencer Yeh on the Software-issued Wake Up Awesome. Additionally, she curated the 27th edition of the Music Unlimited Festival in Wels, Austria, with the tagline "The Most Beautiful Noise in the World." Subsequent collaborations with artists such as Mark Fell, Chris Corsano, and Bill Orcutt were released. Lee was granted a Doris Duke Performing Artist Award in 2015. She held residencies at Civitella Ranieri in Umbria, Italy, and Akademie Schloss Solitude in Stuttgart, Germany, and toured with Swans in 2016. Amalgam, a further collaboration with Marclay, was released by Northern Spy that year. Lee issued several albums in 2018: Dahl-Tah-Ghi (Pica Disk) was recorded live at the Emanuel Vigelang Mausoleum in Oslo in 2013. The Tzadik-issued Cheol-Kkot-Sae (Steel.Flower.Bird) is a long-form collaborative piece combining noise and improvisation with Korean traditional music. The Air Around Her is a collaboration with drone artist and long-string instrument master Ellen Fullman, and Speckled Stones and Dissonant Green Dots incorporates computer-generated and analog synthesizer sounds. In 2020, Shelter Press issued Lee's chamber quartet work Yeo-Neun, which became one of her most acclaimed releases. Lee's piece "Teum (The Silvery Slit)" appeared on a split-LP with Hecker, issued by Portraits GRM in 2021. ~ Paul Simpson & Fred Thomas, Rovi

name: Noémi Büchi
bio: Noémi Büchi is a Swiss/French composer and sound artist exploring the potential of cross-genre musical structures. Her music is defined by a delicate synthesis of textural rhythms and electroacoustic-orchestral abstraction. She contrasts rhythmic physicality with disruption and playfully emphasizes irregularities, creating an expansive listening experience marked by detail and elevation. Her compositions juxtapose multi-layered analog synth textures, crystal-clear tones, and brutalistic noises, evolving through structures that often recall pop song forms. Driven by an inner orchestra of countless voices, her music merges complexity and accessibility, sculpting immersive sound architectures that invite reflection on impermanence and the enduring power of sound.

name: Sandrayati
bio: Sandrayati is a singer-songwriter whose music moves between folk, ambient, alt rock, and the spaces between breath. Born into the traditions of Java and Bali and now rooted in Reykjavík, she weaves identity, nature and the body into song — music that asks us to come home to ourselves. Her second album INHABIT(2025) is an intimate look at phases both human and in nature. Sandrayati has teamed up with movement facilitators all over the world to provide workshops that allow listeners to explore both emotional and movement responses to this record called “Inhabiting Bodies”, continuing on in 2026.

name: Sarah Watson
bio: Sarah Watson is a Canadian pianist who composes and produces her own music. She lives about an hour outside of Toronto with her husband, Victor (Azure Bay on Spotify). Since first releasing Clarity in 2019, Sarah's music has been streamed over 50 million times on various online streaming platforms. Her compositions fall into the “neoclassical” and “modern classical” genres, and have been featured on several editorial playlists on Spotify including Peaceful Piano, Atmospheric Piano, Instrumental Study, Piano in the Background, and more. Sarah’s music is relaxing, uplifting, and melody-driven. You can reach out to Sarah on instagram (@sarahwatsonpiano) or at sarahwatsonpiano@gmail.com to say hello or to request sheet music. Music licensing is available on Musicbed. Thanks for listening! <3

name: Lucy Gooch
bio: Lucy Gooch's debut album ‘Desert Window’ is out now on Fire Records

name: Yasmin Williams
bio: Yasmin Williams is an innovative guitarist and composer known for her unique compositional approach and expansive instrumental style. Her latest album Acadia, released on Nonesuch Records, showcases her evolution from solo performer to collaborative artist, featuring partnerships with notable musicians like Aoife O'Donovan and Immanuel Wilkins. Williams' distinctive creative process involves "ruminating" on single notes until compositions naturally emerge. Beyond traditional fingerpicked guitar, she demonstrates mastery of multiple instruments including kora, harp guitar, banjo, and electric guitar. Her music, while rooted in folk traditions, transcends conventional structures to incorporate elements of progressive rock and experimental composition. Following her acclaimed 2021 album Urban Driftwood, Acadia represents a significant artistic expansion, featuring three distinct sections that move from traditional folk influences to atmospheric soundscapes and experimental arrangements. Williams' approach emphasizes sustained tones and intricate articulation, creating music that balances technical precision with ethereal, floating melodies,  simultaneously. She also incorporates instruments like the kora, harp guitar, and banjo. Despite her use of folk instruments, she resists being categorized within the genre, valuing creative freedom over conformity. Her latest record, Acadia, is out now via Nonesuch Records.

name: Darlingside
bio: Something new....is coming soon.

name: Gollden
bio: Gollden is the ambient music project of Collette Andrea, singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and producer from Toronto, Canada. Since 2016 Collette has been combining music and wellness through the art of sound healing, movement, and meditation. Her music combines ambient guitar, field recordings captured from her favourite places, crystal singing bowls, synths, and airy vocals.  She specializes in creating music for rest,  sleep, and mostly for dreams.  For more visit gollden.ca  |  for all collaborations: golldenmusic (@) gmail dot com

name: Bendik Giske
bio: Now on the cusp of his third solo album, Norwegian saxophonist knows himself well. With his new, self-titled record, he is in his prime as an artist: confident in his voice and abilities, buoyed by critical acclaim from all corners – including two Norwegian Grammy nominations – and a surge in audiences everywhere. With the intriguing choice of Beatrice Dillon as album producer – clearly the British electronic musician is a fellow traveler in the practice of original aesthetic expression – her distinctly spare influence is immediate and keenly felt.

name: Hania Rani
bio: Hania Rani’s music grabs you — its gravitational pull sucks you into a hypnotic trance, regardless of your will. Pianist, composer, and vocalist, she has emerged as a genre-blending nonconformist who nevertheless has made a name for herself weaving classical, jazz, and electronic influences.  Born in 1990 in Gdańsk, Poland—a city renowned for the Solidarity resistance movement— Hania began playing the piano at age seven. She eventually trained as a classical pianist in Warsaw and later studied in Berlin, where she explored electronic music. Recently, she has settled in London.  Rani is a quiet star, more interested in connection than fame or spectacle, and constantly seeks the new in her work, challenging herself and her audience in an active process of renewal and regeneration. It’s a driving quality she has brought to bear on a series of extraordinary albums for Gondwana Records including solo piano albums like 2019’s Esja and 2023’s more electronic Ghosts, award-winning film and theatre scores, duo recordings with cellist and friend Dobrawa Czocher, art installations and most recently Rani has composed and recorded the score for Joachim Trier’s film Sentimental Values.  Her latest recording, Non Fiction: Piano Concerto In Four Movements (November 14 Decca Records) was recorded at Abbey Road Studio 2, with Hugh Tieppo-Brunt conducting an expanded 45-piece Manchester Collective, led by violinist Rakhi Singh and featuring guest performers Jack Wyllie and Valentina Magaletti.

name: Ah! Kosmos
bio: Başak Günak is a sound artist and composer, internationally known as AH! KOSMOS in the field of electronic music. Her work includes sound art, performance, sound installation, composition for theater & contemporary dance.   She released 3 solo LPs from Subtext, Compost Records & Denovali Records, 2 collaborative LPs and numerous EPs.  Günak’s work unconsciously defies being tied to a genre, tapping into something beyond an immediate surrounding or experience to communicate something more transcendental. Günak uses test equipment, acoustic instruments and found sounds to build a sonic realm.   In addition to her compositions with AH! KOSMOS, Günak pursues her sound experimentations as a sound artist, composing soundscapes for theatre, contemporary dance, film and visual art projects, and realising site-specific performances. Her works have been featured worldwide in several festivals and institutions, such as Dutch National Opera, Barbican Theatre (UK), Martin-Gropius Bau(DE), Royal Theater Carré (NL), Berlin CTM Festival (DE), Rotterdamse Schouwburg (NL) and Prague Quadrennial (CZ). She has done composition for Martin-Gropius Bau, Berlin State Museums, Kunstmuseum Basel, Your Data Mirror which was awarded for 2 Webby Awards in Activism.   She has been invited to artist residencies at INA GRM Paris, Callie's Berlin, EMS Stockholm, Bijloke Academy, and HELLERAU – European Center for the Arts. Most recently, she was  invited for a sound installation by Sharjah Biennial 16.

name: Ekin Fil
bio: Turkish artist Ekin Üzeltüzenci records softly swirling drone-folk under the moniker Ekin Fil. Mainly using guitar and her own voice as well as minimal electronics, her sparse yet heavily immersive recordings (such as 2013's Ekin Fil and 2018's Maps) bring to mind shoegaze without the distortion, or ethereal darkwave without any trace of goth. Before starting her Ekin Fil project, Üzeltüzenci sang and played keyboards in several bands based in her hometown of Istanbul, including the post-rock trio Proudpilot, who formed in 2000 and released Monsters Exist in 2009. Ekin Fil's self-released debut CD-R, Soon, also appeared that year, and the cassette Language followed on Root Strata in 2011. She sang on a 2013 EP by Root Strata co-founder Jefre Cantu-Ledesma, and her self-titled LP was released that year by Students of Decay; label boss Alex Cobb was introduced to her through Grouper after Ekin Fil opened for her in Europe. Soon after, Fil released cassettes on labels like Bathetic Records and No Kings, as well as a limited 2015 7". She began releasing music on Helen Scarsdale Agency starting with the 2016 LP Being Near. Following 2017's Ghosts Inside, Fil's soundtrack to Ceylan Özgün Özçelik's film Inflame was issued on cassette, and the Maps LP was released in 2018. ~ Paul Simpson, Rovi

name: Amina Hocine
bio: Amina Hocine (b.1991) is Swedish composer, sound artist, and instrument creator. She writes acousmatic, electro-acoustic and notated music for musicians, focusing on longform pieces, exploring minimal harmonic movements and static rhythmic gestures. Her recent work has been centered around a self-made organ embodied from HVAC components, which produces mesmerizing drones with profound psychoacoustic effects. Drawing inspiration from spiritual sciences, she weaves detailed timbres which encourages deep listening in her compositions.

name: Karen Vogt
bio: Karen Vogt is an Australian artist who uses her voice primarily to create atmospheric compositions.  Mostly known for her ethereal, shimmering vocals with Australian dream-pop band Heligoland, that she co-founded in 1999 (produced by Robin Guthrie).  She also makes experimental/ambient solo works, does guest vocals and collaborations.  Her duo GALÁN/VOGT makes emotive, neoclassical music infused with elements of dark ambient and shoegaze.  She is currently based in Paris, France.

name: Zuzanna Całka
bio: Zuzanna Całka is a clasically trained pianist and composer.  Her debut EP, Late Night Takes is meditative piano ballades built around the idea of boketto which in Japanese means the art of daydreaming; gazing into the distance, lost in thought which is the artist's way of slowing down and being present in the modern world. Zuzanna decided to release this album under her own label LNT.wav established in Warsaw in 2023.   Coming up in April 2025 Late Night Takes expands to synthesizers, exploring the beauty of electronic keyboards and sound design. Minimalist sketches contrast with complex structures, creating intriguing, and sometimes even hallucinatory, trance-like melodies. Major role in the process is improvisation which emerges each show in a different way.  Zuzanna has been playing the piano since she can remember. Awarded with Ist prize on Transatlantyk Instant Composition Contest for composing music for two short movies, with Oscar winning head of the jury Jan AP Kaczmarek.

name: Chihei Hatakeyama
bio: Chihei Hatakeyama is a Tokyo-based ambient musician and mastering engineer who creates chiming, shimmering soundscapes with acoustic instruments (including guitar, vibraphone, and piano) and laptop processing. His works often evoke scenes from nature, and appropriately include an abundant amount of field recordings and other organic sounds. Since the release of his well-received debut album, Minima Moralia (Kranky), in 2006, he has been remarkably prolific as both a solo artist and collaborator, and his work has always maintained a consistently high quality. He has issued numerous recordings through labels like Room40, White Paddy Mountain, Gearbox, and Constellation Tatsu (who released Unconsciousness Silence in 2026). Hatakeyama originally began making music as part of various hardcore and metal bands, and his interests gradually drifted toward experimental rock and classical music. He formed a duo called Opitope in 2002 with Tomoyoshi Date. Kranky issued Hatakeyama's solo debut in 2006, and Opitope released their first full-length, Hau, on Spekk the following year. Hatakeyama's second solo album, Dedication, appeared on Magic Book Records in 2008. From 2009 on, his release schedule was relentless, with albums on Hibernate (The River), Room40 (Saunter, Mirror), Home Normal (A Long Journey), and numerous other ambient/experimental labels. In 2010, he began releasing music digitally through his White Paddy Mountain label, including volumes of his Void series of live recordings; gradually, the label began issuing CDs by other artists (such as Celer, Machinefabriek, and Aaron Martin), which were mixed and mastered by Hatakeyama himself. He continued to release albums on other labels, including Rural Colours, Small Fragments, and Airplane Label, in addition to collaborations with artists like Asuna, Hakobune, and Federico Durand. Hatakeyama released six albums in 2015 alone, including Frozen Silence (a collaboration with Sakana Hosomi), Mist, Five Dreams, and his third album for Lawrence English's Room40 label, Moon Light Reflecting Over Mountains. In 2017, Hatakeyama returned to Room40 with Mirage. Recorded over a five-year period, the album found him exploring the relationship between architecture and music. Other releases during the year included Far from the Atmosphere (Hiss Noise Records) and collaborations with Durand and Tamaru. In 2018, Hatakeyama released Solitary Universe (with Eraldo Bernocchi) and FTS002, a 12" EP with Vida Vojić. His solo efforts during the year included the Constellation Tatsu cassette Scene and White Paddy Mountain CDs Butterfly's Summer and Vanished and Afterimage. Erroribus Humanis et Antimony, a collaboration with Ken Ikeda and Tetuzi Akiyama, was issued by Otooto in early 2019. Jodo (with Stijn Hüwels) and Ghost Woods both appeared on White Paddy Mountain later in the year, and Room40 released Forgotten Hill. Hatakeyama collaborated with Tetuzi Akiyama and Ken Ikeda for the album Erroribus Humanis Et Antinomy. 2020 brought Black Frost, Hatakeyama's second collaboration with Dirk Serries. Late Spring, his first album for Gearbox Records, appeared in 2021. He collaborated with Michael Grigoni and Stephen Vitiello for the release Earth Awhile. Hachirogata Lake was released by Field Records in 2023, and the soundtrack Life Is Climbing appeared on Gearbox. In 2024, Hatakeyama released the solo album Thousand Oceans, and collaborated with Hakobune, zakè, and From Overseas for the release Live Improvisations. He also began issuing a series of Magnificent Little Dudes releases with Shun Ishiwaka. Lucid Dreams was released by First Terrace Records in 2025, with guest appearances by Cucina Povera and Nailah Hunter. Hatakeyama returned to Constellation Tatsu with 2026's Unconsciousness Silence. ~ Paul Simpson, Rovi

name: Drum & Lace
bio: Drum & Lace, aka Sofia degli Alessandri, is a Florence-raised, London-based musician and composer. Her music takes inspiration from the natural world and is scattered with field recordings, so while the work is largely electronic there is a grounding and organic nature to every track. Her debut album Natura (PITP) found inspiration in soil and in rolling hills, while 2023's Frost EP captured the quiet beauty of winter. Her second LP ONDA (Fabrique Records) is inspired by the ocean, with motifs of shells, sand and sisterhood present throughout. The release of ambient vocal works EP Tempora and track ‘Marmo’ (LATTICE003) followed in 2025. In early 2026, Mesh announced D & L joining their roster with EP Terra, which comprises a collection of meditations on human existence, tapping folkloric traditions and the breadth of electronic music. Using Italian lyrics for the 1st time, Drum & Lace considers the ancient lands she grew up in, and the complex lore that overlooks nature, history, and technology. She has shared the stage with luminary artists such as William Basinski, Suzanne Ciani, Kaitlyn Aurelia Smith, black midi, Sqürl and Hans-Joachim Roedelius, while the stages she's performed on include revered London venues like Café OTO & EartH; Moogfest, Public Records NY, Zebulon and Slingshot Festival in the US & Festa Dell’Opera in Italy. As a film composer, she's worked on films and series such as ‘Dickinson’, ‘Rosaline’, ‘Cobweb’, ‘Good Girls’ & ‘Red, White & Royal Blue’.

name: Hainbach
bio: Based out of Berlin, Germany, electronic music composer and performer Hainbach creates shifting audio landscapes THE WIRE called "One hell of a trip". His music has been released on Opal Tapes, Seil Records, Spring Break Tapes, Limited Interest and Marionette. He has been fascinated with sine tones, noise and FM since he discovered the dial on the radio. Never losing his childhood wonder, he still searches for the sounds in between on modular synths and other devices. Through his YouTube channel Hainbach brings experimental music techniques to a wider audience.

name: Rebecca Foon
bio: Composer and cellist Rebecca Foon has been a fixture of the Montréal and NYC music communities for two decades, performing and recording in a wide array of contexts, most notably as co-founder of the modern chamber post-rock ensemble Esmerine, as a member of Thee Silver Mt Zion Memorial Orchestra (2001-2008) and Set Fire To Flames (2001-2004), and more recently at the helm of her electro-acoustic songwriting project Saltland. With these four entities, Foon has performed around the world and released over a dozen albums on various imprints. Esmerine’s 2013 album Dalmak won the Canadian music industry’s Juno Award for Best Instrumental Album, the band’s 2015 album Lost Voices was a finalist in this same category along with winning the award for Best Album Package, and won Best Instrumental Album in 2022 for their most recent album, Everything Was Forever Until It Was No More. Foon regularly plays with her sister Aliayta Foon-Dancoes along with Richard Reed Parry and Sarah Neufeld, releasing albums in 2024 and 2025 with these beautiful Neo-classical projects. Foon began working on new solo music featuring a heightened emphasis on vocals and piano, with her first eponymous release in February 2020 and now releases her most dream pop album to date Black Butterflies. Foon is also a co-founder alongside with Jesse Paris Smith of the climate action non profit Pathway to Paris.

name: Sarah Neufeld
bio: Canadian violinist and composer Sarah Neufeld is best known as a member of Arcade Fire and co-founder of the post-rock band Bell Orchestre. Her first solo album, ‘Hero Brother’, was recorded in Berlin by engineer and co-producer Nils Frahm. In 2015 Neufeld released the Juno award winning ‘Never Were The Way She Was’ with celebrated saxophonist and collaborator Colin Stetson, and in 2016 Neufeld released her acclaimed second solo album, ‘The Ridge’. New LP ‘Detritus’ was inspired by a collaboration with legendary dancer/choreographer Peggy Baker and features the work of Arcade Fire bandmate Jeremy Gara, Bell Orchestre bandmate Pietro Amato, and long-time collaborator Stuart Bogie.

name: Richard Reed Parry
bio: The first volume of Quiet River of Dust was released on the autumn equinox of 2018; this second volume, out on the summer solstice of 2019, was created at the same time. (It was supposed to come out on the spring equinox, but got bumped because Parry and designer Tracey Maurice had to wait for salt crystals to grow on the artwork to create wave caps and mountaintops—do not underestimate Parry’s attention to detail.) Both volumes bleed into one another, by design. “It feels like a multi-sided window to me,” says Parry, “a different view into this prismatic song world.” Japanese folk myths, death poems and British folk music are tributaries flowing into a river of late-20th century avant-garde composition and traditional song craft, written and performed by a member of a Grammy-winning rock band. This is a meditative, widescreen musical experience with Beach Boy harmonies and a hypnotic pulse. Layered songs that move in a linear fashion, following a current rather than circular composition.

name: Maya Shenfeld
bio: Berlin composer Maya Shenfeld’s music is as powerfully evocative as it is strikingly intimate. Through a mastery of sound sculpting and visionary approach to composition Shenfeld has established herself as one of the most vital voices in Berlin’s New Music scene. Her work exists in liminal spaces, collapsing the boundaries between electronic synthesis and organic sound as it draws equally from classical tradition and underground experimentalism. Each aspect of her output, from site-specific sound installations to works for new music ensembles and even playing guitar in punk bands, combines an astute technical prowess with an authentic, tangible expression of soul.   Shenfeld’s debut solo record In Free Fall, out 22 October via Thrill Jockey Records merges the grand vision of orchestral music with the granularity and intimacy of deep listening, exploring a tension between immaculately structured compositional architecture and the sheer joy of noise, grain and feedback.

name: Veryan
bio: Veryan is an elusive female electronic musician based in Scotland. She composes and produces abstract, ambient-tinged instrumentals that are deliberately minimalistic and experimental in nature.  In 2020 Veryan self-released her debut album 'Ebb & Flow', which she shortly followed with a four track digital EP 'Hireath', before releasing her second album 'HERE' on Cue Dot Records in 2021.  Veryan's music has been described as lush tonal electronica infused with warmth which, in turn, creates a sense of space within the soundscapes she composes.

name: Alice in Freefall
bio: An Ambient Electric Harp and Drone project from Australian harpist Mary Doumany, using  harp effects to create lush textures, combined with pianos, synths and voices. Alice in Freefall takes inspiration from liminal landscape, inner states and deep space.... Go to www.marydoumany.com and join our mailing list for all the info on Alice.

name: Cheryl B. Engelhardt
bio: Cheryl B. Engelhardt is a 2x GRAMMY®-nominated artist & composer who writes New Age music, pieces for choirs, scores for commercials, and music for meditation apps, orchestras, and other media.  Cheryl began her career as an advertising & film composer in NYC, scoring several national commercials before hitting the road with her pop band. Her music has been placed in numerous TV shows, meditation apps, & airlines.  She composes for social justice choirs & has been featured in People & Forbes for her collaboration with Donzaleigh Abernathy, Martin Luther King’s goddaughter, on the song “The Listening.” Her seventh album, the GRAMMY®-nominated project The Passenger, made her the first person to create a full album on a cross-country Amtrak train journey in 2022. Her second nomination is for her 2025 release, According to the Moon.  A certified trauma-informed coach, Cheryl empowers musicians & creatives through her mastermind program, Amplify, and her platform, In The Key of Success. She leads workshops and retreats focused on sustainable systems, nervous system regulation, and aligned careers.  A Cornell University alumna with advanced orchestration training from Juilliard, Cheryl is a sought-after speaker, moderator, and advocate for artists. She also serves as a key advocate for musicians through her roles as Governor of The Recording Academy’s New York Chapter and as Chair of Contemporary/Commercial Repertoire for the American Choral Directors Association Eastern Region.

name: Aasma
bio: Mira Aasma writes, produces and performs experimental music inspired by the elements under the artist name Aasma. Residing in deep forests, misty mountains, flowing rivers and the vast ocean, Aasma presents odes to nature while creating spaces for clear mind and presence. Totemically transforming waves, wind, rocks and root systems into narrative stories and characters, their work shimmers between the textural lines of dream-pop, ambient and experimental.  Based between Bohuslän and Berlin with Swedish/Estonian heritage and a childhood shaped by choir-singing and drums, Aasma’s multi-instrumental approach weaves voice, gongs, bowls, field recordings and flute into deeply meditative sound healing sessions. This record for Sources is part of her ongoing ‘Elemental Odyssey’ project, exploring how sound can bridge nature and humanity through the four elements.

name: Clariloops
bio: Clariloops is the project of Australian neo-classical/electronic artist Ruby Ester Mae. Combining the sound of her clarinet with effects pedals and synthesised sound, Ruby experiments with electronics to create music that is unique yet familiar, existing between genres. The project started as a way of bringing stillness and creativity into Ruby’s classical music practice. The resulting sounds are rhythmic and calming, providing accompaniment to people’s movements and thoughts without intrusion.

name: Claire M Singer
bio: Claire M Singer is a composer and performer of acoustic and electronic music, film and installations. Known for her experimental approach to the organ her work draws inspiration from the dramatic landscape of her native Scotland, exploring rich harmonic textures and complex overtones that create ever-shifting melodic and rhythmic patterns disappearing almost as soon as they emerge. Her three critically acclaimed releases on Touch feature Singer playing both organ and cello (‘..each piece is timeless and genuinely magical’ – The Quietus). Performances include Queen Elizabeth Hall; Glasgow Cathedral; Tate Modern; Westerkerk opening for Low and the Barbican opening for Stars of the Lid. The Guardian wrote ‘Claire M Singer really knows how to wring the best out of this magnificent instrument, creating moments of sustained rapture’  Most recently in December 2021 her solo organ work The Molendinar featured in The New York Times '5 Minutes That Will Make You Love the Organ'.  Awards include the Oram Award in 2017 for her innovation in sound and music and the Festival Castell de Peralada Award for best film score in 2019 (Tell It To The Bees). In 2020 her work Gleann Ciùin was nominated for an Ivor Novello Award, which was commissioned by the London Contemporary Orchestra. Recent projects include a collaboration with Chris Watson for organ, field recordings, orchestra and choir premiering at her festival Organ Reframed at Union Chapel in 2022.   www.clairemsinger.com

name: Salamanda
bio: Salamanda is a Seoul-based Leftfield Ambient music producer/DJ duo of Uman Therma (Sala) and Yetsuby (Manda). Salamanda believes every sound has beauty, and loves to collect and experiment with all kinds of sounds from the world around them.     *Releases 2019.10 Our Lair EP [Tonal Unity (KR)] 2020.04 Glass Cage EP [Self-Release] 2020.12 Allez LP [Good Morning Tapes (FR)] 2021.09 Sphere LP [Small Méasures (UK)] 2022.06 ashbalkum LP [Human Pitch (US)]   *Links soundcloud.com/8salamanda8 8salamanda8.bandcamp.com instagram.com/8salamanda8

name: Noveller
bio: As Noveller, guitarist Sarah Lipstate employs loops and an intricate web of effects to create textural, expansive instrumental soundscapes. Lipstate's background in filmmaking informed the cinematic elements of her ambient guitar compositions. Noveller's sound progressed from slow-moving drones to filmic science fiction-themed pieces, eventually growing from solo guitar arrangements to incorporate synthesizers and rhythmic elements on 2017's A Pink Sunset for No One. While attending college in Austin, Texas, between 2003 and 2006, Lipstate played guitar in an experimental duo called One Umbrella with synth/electronics partner Carlos Villarreal. Noveller was devised as a guitar-based solo moniker in 2005 when Lipstate contributed songs to a few different noise compilations, as well as self-releasing two 3" CD-R EPs, Vasovagal and Nerves and Endings. Her heavily processed guitar loops resulted in an icy wash of distant sounds, spare and unsettling by turns. In 2007, a move to the East Coast brought Noveller into the realm of live performance, starting with a spot at Washington, D.C. experimental festival Sonic Circuits. Various shows in the New York area followed, which led to a meeting with sound artist Carlos Giffoni. Giffoni issued the first two Noveller full-lengths, Paint on the Shadows and Red Rainbows, on his No Fun Productions label. Both records saw release in 2009. The same year, Canadian label Divorce released Colourful Disturbances, a split LP between Noveller and Aidan Baker. In 2010, Lipstate started her own imprint, Saffron Recordings, releasing her third solo full-length, Desert Fires, as well as a split LP with unFact. Her fourth proper full-length, Glacial Glow, was released jointly through Saffron and Weird Forest in May 2011. In the interim between albums, Lipstate kept very busy with one-off festival performances as well as regular shows in Manhattan and Brooklyn and tours of Europe and the U.S. for each new record. She also collaborated frequently, performing at times as a member of Cold Cave and Parts & Labor. In addition, Lipstate acted as a player in Rhys Chatham's Guitar Army and Glenn Branca's 100-guitar ensemble, among other duo improvisation dates with fixtures of N.Y.C.'s experimental scene. Following a limited 2012 tour-only CD-R titled Artifact, the proper full-length No Dreams saw release in 2013 on the Important Records label. Reveries, a collaboration with Thisquietarmy, appeared on French label Shelter Press in June 2014. Noveller then signed to Fire Records, which issued Fantastic Planet, an album of decidedly more cinematic soundscapes, in early 2015. Following the LP's critical success, the label subsequently reissued No Dreams and Glacial Glow. Around this time, Lipstate gained a new fan in Iggy Pop, who not just took Noveller on tour as an opening act but eventually began to collaborate with her on writing new material. Noveller's eighth set, A Pink Sunset for No One was released on Fire Records in 2017, finding Lipstate's cinematic solo guitar compositions expanding to include percussion and other more structural elements. Lipstate continued her affiliation with Iggy Pop, collaborating with him and trumpet player Leron Thomas on his subdued and reflective 2019 album Free. At this point, Lipstate was stationed in Los Angeles and had officially joined on as a guitarist in Pop's touring band, but she also continued work on Noveller. Her next solo album, Arrow, was released in June 2020, preceded by several singles that continued Lipstate's expansion from her early sheets of sound into more compositionally complex territory. ~ Fred Thomas, Rovi

name: Meg Bowles
bio: Meg’s newest release (December 2022), Voices from the Ethereal Forest, features contemplative ambient-choral soundscapes inspired by the life-sustaining beauty and mystery of forests past and present. Her previous release, Pilgrimage (May 2022), explores a more cinematic ambient-orchestral style that incorporates spacious atmospheric textures evoking meteorological phenomena and other poetic elements that form an accompanying dreamscape along the path of a journey towards wholeness.   These recordings follow Evensong: Canticles for the Earth (2018), and The Shimmering Land (2013), both of which were voted ZMR’s Best Ambient Album for their respective years. For the past several decades Bowles, a synthesist, has been a leader in the ambient music genre with all her recordings which also include Inner Space, Solstice Dreams, Blue Cosmos, From the Dark Earth and A Quiet Light.

name: Jefre Cantu-Ledesma
bio: Creating sounds based in both patient ambient exploration, experimental clatter, and the textural expressiveness of shoegaze, Jefre Cantu-Ledesma applies his distinctive voice to a wide range of instrumental styles, from the distorted ambient haze of his 2010 debut Love Is a Stream to the slowed-down beats and tape experiments of 2015's A Year with 13 Moons. Along with solo work, Cantu-Ledesma collaborates frequently, bringing in a host of contributors on his 2019 high-water mark album Tracing Back the Radiance, and working with like-minded musician Ilyas Ahmed on the 2021 joint effort You Can See Your Own Way Out. In 2025, he released a new album of minimal, naturalistic ambient compositions entitled Gift Songs. Born and raised in Texas, Jefre Cantu-Ledesma delved into abstract music around the same time he was studying sculpture and visual arts in San Francisco in the mid-'90s. Developing an ambient approach to the spacy indie rock and slowcore of the time, Cantu-Ledesma co-founded the highly influential instrumental act Tarentel, worked with experimental rock trio the Alps, and ran the well-respected drone/ambient label Root Strata. Prolifically collaborative, Cantu-Ledesma worked with Grouper's Liz Harris in a duo called Raum, as well as with filmmaker Paul Clipson and in Alexis Georgopoulos' ARP project. For a short time he worked solo under the name Colophon, and released music under his own name. A more official solo debut came out in 2010 with the beautifully damaged shoegaze tones of Love Is a Stream, released on Type Records. Some copies of the record included the companion EP Love Is a Dream, featuring collaborations between Cantu-Ledesma and Type founder John Twells' Xela project. Following several years' worth of limited cassette and vinyl releases, a proper follow-up came in 2015 with A Year with 13 Moons. Named after a Fassbinder film, the collection of dreamy guitar textures, modular synth noise, and distant drum-machine rhythms was put together during a residency at the Headlands Center for the Arts in the San Francisco Bay Area. The album was released early that year on Mexican Summer. In 2016, Shelter Press released Comme un Seul Narcisse, a collaborative LP by Cantu-Ledesma and Félicia Atkinson (aka Je Suis le Petit Chevalier), and Geographic North released Cantu-Ledesma's solo cassette In Summer. Also that year, the Czech label Pre-Echo issued vinyl editions of Songs of Remembrance and Songs of Forgiveness, two previously cassette-only albums from 2014. In 2017, he returned to Mexican Summer with On the Echoing Green, a clearer, more accessible album than his previous efforts. 2019 marked another step away from well-traveled territory with the more subdued, experimental, and chamber instrumentation of Tracing Back the Radiance. In 2021 Cantu-Ledesma collaborated with Portland musician Ilyas Ahmed on duo album You Can See Your Own Way Out, as well as continuing his work with French acoustic composer Félicia Atkinson on their joint album Un Hiver En Plein Été. The following year, the seldom-seen Raum duo released Daughter, their first new material since 2013. Completely solo recordings around this time took different paths, with 2023's Poverty getting into experimental electronics and programming while 2025's Gift Songs was pastoral, minimal, and reliant largely on organic instrumentation. ~ Fred Thomas, Rovi

name: Poemme
bio: Poemme is the ambient project of Angela Klimek, who first began creating music in 2016 to supplement her husband’s sleep music radio station, Ambient Sleeping Pill. Since discovering her passion for creating dreamy soundscapes, she hasn’t been able to stop recording tracks for sleep as well as brighter, more daytime-oriented drones from her home studio in Ohio, USA.

name: The Seven Fields Of Aphelion
bio: The Seven Fields of Aphelion is the stage name of Maureen "Maux" Boyle, keyboard player for Pennsylvania-based experimental indie rockers Black Moth Super Rainbow. A native of Pittsburgh, Boyle joined the group in the early 2000s. Her solo work, which largely eschews the ramshackle chaos of BMSR for a more ambient/neo-folk approach, was first made public in 2010 with the arrival of Periphery, which was released via Graveface Records. Boyle's sophomore long-player under the Seven Fields of Aphelion moniker, the Rad Cult-issued Keep the Ocean Inside, followed in 2017. ~ James Christopher Monger, Rovi

name: Ana Roxanne
bio: Ana Roxanne is an American musician based in New York. Her self-released EP was later reissued by Leaving Records before signing with Kranky for her official full-length debut, 2020's Because Of A Flower.  Working at the interzone of electric meditation, dream pop, and ambient songcraft, her inspirations span the secular (R&B divas of 1980's and 90's) and the spiritual (Catholic choral traditions in which she was raised), synthesized into a uniquely intuitive sonic language, equal parts atmospheric and ancient, healing and hermetic.

name: Faten Kanaan
bio: Composer, musician, and producer Faten Kanaan uses counterpoint as a narrative tool to create music that is mysterious, smudgy, and deeply melodic. From the repetitive structures of modern minimalism and early music/baroque influences, to more languid textural ebbs & tides, there's a warmth in her use of synthesizers that gives her work a curiously timeless feel. Composing intuitively, her music creates its own world... one that isn't easily categorised.  In symbiosis with electronics is an appreciation for the vulnerability of human limitations and nuances, and her live performances highlight her use of the piano keyboard. Recent concerts have included ones supporting Alessandro Cortini, Colin Stetson, Blonde Redhead, and William Basinski.  Bio: Syrian-Palestinian-Jordanian-Lebanese.  b. Walsrode, Germany

name: Echo Collective
bio: “Post-classical”, “neo-classical”, “non-classical” : nobody knows what to call this music – but Neil Leiter and Margaret Hermant, aka Echo Collective, don't mind one bit. Orchestral instrumental music from outside the classical establishment has become huge over the past few years, and Leiter and Hermant have witnessed the evolution and extraordinary rise of this movement right up close. They've worked with some of the most important players, both in the recording studio and for concerts worldwide. And though the Echo Collective members themselves very much do come from within the classical music establishment, they don't care which side of the fence they are seen to be on.   Echo Collective essentially came together around A Winged Victory For The Sullen: the duo of Adam Wiltzie and Dustin O'Halloran. During this time they were also playing in related projects: with Wiltzie's much revered other duo project Stars Of The Lid, with O'Halloran's solo work, with Icelandic composer Jóhann Jóhannsson.   The ability to flow easily from black metal to Erasure, Radiohead to Stars Of The Lid shows exactly what kind of musicians Echo Collective are. Without prejudice, without over-reverence, without particularly caring about genre boundaries - but always with utmost seriousness - they take on challenges set by others and put their own mark on them, they dig for the musical motifs that work for them.

name: Grand River
bio: For the last decade, Berlin-based Dutch-Italian composer and musician Aimée Portioli, aka Grand River, has been circling the perimeter of electronic music and sound art, crafting heady electroacoustic soundscapes for acclaimed labels like Spazio Disponibile, Editions Mego, Caterina Barbieri's light-years, Ghostly International, Tresor and Umor Rex while simultaneously devising ambitious multichannel installations and rupturing the boundary between the gallery and the performance space. Most recently, she debuted Symphony for Endangered Birds, a 7-channel sonic examination of vulnerable bird species, at Essen's Museum Folkwang.  Portioli is set to return to Editions Mego in fall this year with Temporary, her most expansive and focused album yet. Painting over the musical outlines she displayed on its predecessor she meticulously seeks out more nuanced shades, balancing her billowing electronic textures and buzzing arpeggios with vivid melodies and thunderous rhythms. It's surprisingly direct, highlighting the interplay between Portioli's guitar work and advanced synthesizer processes.

name: Penelope Trappes
bio: On April 4th, Brighton-based Australian vocalist, producer, and multi-instrumentalist Penelope Trappes will release her fifth full-length album ‘A Requiem’. It comes alongside news of her signing to London imprint, One Little Independent Records. Formally trained in opera and jazz in her youth, Penelope swaddles her voice and poetics in brooding atmospherics underpinned by subterranean drone. She released her acclaimed trilogy, ‘Penelope One’, ‘Two’ and ‘Three’, on Fabric’s Houndstooth label. In between instalments of her ambitious trilogy, Penelope released a clutch of both experimental and more dreampop-oriented EPs. She demonstrated her versatility in the extended 25-minute deep-listening composition ‘Gnostic State’, and the arpeggiated electronics and minimalist songwriting on the ‘Eel Drip’ EP. She also released an album of reworks, ‘Penelope Redeux’, with contributions by Cosey Fanni Tutti, Mogwai, Félicia Atkinson and Nik Colk Void, and the cassette, ‘Mother’s Blood,’ a vocal-free meditative reinterpretation of 'Penelope Three’. Penelope’s fourth album, ‘Heavenly Spheres’, was released in 2023 on her own Nite Hive imprint, was composed using just piano, voice and an old reel-to-reel tape deck during a two-week artist residency for Britten Pears Arts in Aldeburgh, Suffolk.    “Summoning the great ghosts of vintage 4AD and Kranky, the Australian singer and producer makes inky dream pop that’s as heavy and welcoming as a weighted blanket.” - Philip Sherburne (Pitchfork)

name: normal the kid
bio: "don’t worry, i feel the same way lovely <3"  normals highly anticipated release “Salt,” is OUT NOW!  Liam Sass (Also known as normal the kid) isn’t just an artist. You experience his music as much as you hear it. With over 100 million streams, billions of short-form video views, and a rapidly growing global fanbase, he’s built a career that proves connection goes far beyond sound.  What makes his story truly extraordinary is that he’s created all of this while being almost entirely deaf.  Instead of relying on traditional listening, normal the kid approaches music through feeling, vibration, emotion, and instinct. That relationship with sound shapes everything he creates. The result is music that cuts deeper, resonates longer, and reaches people in a way that feels almost physical. His songs aren’t just heard, they’re felt.  His catalog reflects that difference. Each track is crafted to create space for clarity, for emotion, for reflection. Whether it’s helping someone slow down during chaos, process something they can’t quite put into words, or simply breathe for a moment, his music serves a purpose beyond entertainment. It’s intentional. It’s grounding.  While many artists chase trends, normal the kid has built his own lane entirely. His limitations became his advantage, forcing him to create without the noise of the industry both literally and figuratively. That perspective is what gives his art its signature depth and honesty.  inquiries@normalthekid.com

This project was given the name, “Cosmazul” which is a mix of “cosmos” and “azul” - the color blue.

name: Joey Michels

name: Jonah Heather

name: Marino Calle
bio: The music of Marino Calle lives somewhere between memory and stillness — warm, spacious, and deeply calming.

name: Camilo Branca
bio: A genius of musical world-building, is appreciated globally for her beautiful guitar music. Though in fact, she is a pseudonym of composer Jackson Fitzgerald. Predominantly known in other fields, Fitzgerald enjoys adopting different personas fluent in other genres to best express himself in a wide variety of settings.

name: Finlep
bio: Rooted in classical tradition and shaped by contemporary serenity,  Finlep is guitarist Marcio Philomena’s alter ego. In this project, he crafts lyrical melodies and ethereal soundscapes that reflect his calmer side.

name: Sven Simons
bio: New York City based classical guitarist and composer.

name: Fabian Lombardi
bio: Fabian Lombardi makes peaceful music for the moments when you need the world to feel a little softer.

name: Riley Howe
bio: Riley Howe is a neoclassical project by composer Jackson Fitzgerald.  A master of musical world-building on the guitar Fitzgerald enjoys adopting different personas in other genres to best express himself in a variety of musical traditions.

name: Jonka Ebony
bio: Jonka Ebony is the moniker used by the Guitarist, composer from Sweden Jonas Kahnberg for his calm and sensitive guitar pieces. Thanks for listen and please follow. Jonka Ebony also has playlists of guitar music Soft Acoustic Guitar

name: Jules Navarro
bio: Instrumental glimpses for calm mornings, tired evenings, and the moments where everything gets a little quieter.

name: Hayden Phoenix
bio: The sound of Hayden Phoenix is rooted in calm repetition, subtle movement, and the beauty of simplicity.

name: Davide Di Sierra
bio: Davide Di Sierra, aka David Albornoz, is a versatile classical guitarist born and raised in Maracaibo, Venezuela. With a Bachelor’s degree in Music from Venezuela, David’s journey in music began early, both as a student and as a musician in various bands. Over the past decade in the United States, he has expanded his horizons, working as an elementary music teacher and performing live in the Houston area for both public and private events.  David’s music is a rich tapestry that blends Venezuelan folk traditions, Spanish influences, and classical guitar techniques. His instrumental compositions have gained considerable recognition, amassing around 100,000 monthly listeners across his various projects.  As a performer, David captivates audiences with his expressive guitar playing, bringing a soothing and evocative atmosphere to every performance.

name: Jasper Lynx
bio: Jasper Lynx is the acoustic alter ego of guitarist Simon Löfstedt. Best known for his expressive work on the electric guitar, Löfstedt created Jasper Lynx as an outlet for a more intimate and contemplative musical voice.

name: Maude Clonet
bio: Peaceful, acoustic guitar side project from Nate Harrison.  contact@nateharrisonmusic.com for any inquiries

name: Marcio Philomena
bio: Hailing from Porto Alegre in Southern Brazil but now based in Brooklyn, New York, jazz guitarist and composer Marcio Philomena creates music that reflects his experience as an international troubadour. ‘Trails’ is Philomena’s debut album and contains nine instrumental tracks that are a refreshing blend of jazz, Brazilian music, rock and soundscapes that also showcase his love of melody.  The album sees Philomena perform eight pieces with a traditional jazz quartet that includes Julian Shore (piano), Rick Rosato (upright bass), and Roberto Giaquinto (drums), with ‘Vibraçöes' steering towards the Brazilian tradition and featuring Hélio Alves (piano), Peter Slavov (upright bass) and Rafael Barata (drums).  Philomena first picked up an acoustic guitar at the age of 11 after seeing Green Day perform on MTV. By 13, he had discovered a love of jazz after seeing his music teacher play through a book of Pat Martino transcriptions. “I didn’t know you could sound like that on the guitar, and it looked challenging, so that inspired me to learn jazz.” Receiving a scholarship to Berklee College of Music in 2009 to study guitar and production, he was shortly thereafter selected as a semi-finalist in the Montreux Jazz Festival Guitar Competition. After a period in Brazil, he settled in Brooklyn, where he has become a fixture in NYC’s music scene.

name: Leo Ask
bio: Leo Ask creates music rooted in simplicity and quiet emotion. Gentle instrumental pieces move softly in the background, bringing a sense of calm to everyday moments and giving the mind room to wander.

name: Allan Soderbergh
bio: Allan Soderbergh creates calm, intimate instrumental music built around the warmth and simplicity of acoustic guitar. His gentle melodies and understated arrangements invite the listener to slow down, breathe, and find a moment of stillness.  Music for quiet mornings, peaceful evenings, and everything in between.

name: Philip Grass
bio: Transcendent guitar music that was written throughout my travels

name: Odyssey Quartet
bio: Odyssey Quartet is a Stockholm-based band formed in 2020, though its members have been playing together in various constellations for over two decades. United by a shared passion, they create music that feels familiar, welcoming, and soothing—equally suited for focused listening and for setting a warm, atmospheric backdrop.

name: Robert Nilsson Trio
bio: Robert Nilsson Trio is an instrumental jazz trio based in Stockholm, Sweden. Inspired by the Nordic jazz tradition, the trio creates spacious, melodic music that values restraint as much as expression.

name: Hudson Harris & Haim
bio: Artist enquiries - getintouch@musician.org

name: The Soulful Strut
bio: Based in Stockholm, we are a jazz band brought together by a deep love for jazz, improvisation, and the feeling of musicians creating something together in the moment.  In our everyday musical lives, improvisation is not always at the center of what we do. The Soulful Strut gives us a different kind of space — a place to explore a side of our musical expression that we rarely get the chance to fully embrace. To listen, react, take chances, and let the music find its own way.  Our music is warm, relaxed, and rooted in the jazz tradition. We want it to feel equally at home in the foreground or quietly filling a room. Something you can put on, slow down to, close your eyes, and simply let the music take over for a while.  Jazz has always fascinated us, and this project is our way of getting closer to it — with curiosity, freedom, and a lot of love for the music.

name: The City of Birches
bio: Welcome to The City of Birches, an alter ego of Andreas Gidlund. Andreas started his musical journey as a child growing up in the north of Sweden playing all sorts of instruments from an early age. Maybe it was the cold and long winters of the north that developed a love for the melancholic and sentimental expressions in music and jazzballads in particularly. Here, you'll find simple and elegantly restrained compositions...yet with plenty of passion and subtle nuance. Welcome again and thanks for listening!

name: Noel Duvall Trio
bio: Noel Duvall Trio plays soft jazz rooted in the classic American tradition. Focused on space and tone, the music unfolds naturally with a calm vibe to it.

name: Zach Dawson
bio: Zach Dawson draws inspiration from the European jazz tradition, blending elegance with singable, lyrical melodies. His piano playing values clarity, phrasing, and emotional restraint. The music feels conversational, melodic, and rooted in classic jazz storytelling.

name: Nathan Hill Trio
bio: Acoustic piano trio from Sweden. Calm melodies and warm harmonies with a Scandinavian touch.

name: Night Current
bio: Night Current delivers sophisticated jazz performances blending soulful harmonies, expressive improvisation, and late-night atmosphere.

name: Trio Rosa
bio: Trio Rosa is a New York City–based jazz group led by bassist Rick Rosato. Blending classic and contemporary jazz influences, the trio delivers a sophisticated sound that has captivated a growing global audience. Their music has amassed over 20 million streams and continues to attract an expanding base of monthly listeners across streaming platforms.

name: Gus Anderson
bio: Jazz infused with global colors and singable themes. Warm textures, natural flow, lasting resonance.

name: Eddie Harper
bio: Welcome to the sounds of Eddie Harper. I hope you enjoy the music.

name: Oliver Bade
bio: Oliver Bade is an acoustic guitarist creating music for calm, reflective moments. Centered entirely around the six strings, his compositions are intimate, warm, and deeply expressive. Through gentle melodies and subtle dynamics, Oliver Bade crafts a sound that invites stillness and quiet reflection.   Each piece unfolds with simplicity and care, offering listeners a space to slow down, breathe, and reconnect with the moment. Rooted in the natural voice of the guitar, his music captures the beauty of restraint -where every note matters, and silence becomes part of the experience.

name: Dan Lauften
bio: Dan Lauften is an acoustic guitarist known for his warm and soothing sound. From an early age, he developed a deep connection to the acoustic guitar-a bond that continues to shape his music today. With a focus on tone, melody, and feel, Dan Lauften creates compositions that are calm, inviting, and easy to settle into. His playing carries a natural flow, where each note is placed with care, forming a sound that feels both comforting and sincere. Rooted in a lifelong love for the instrument, his music offers a gentle listening experience-simple, melodic, and quietly expressive.

name: Eric Nilson
bio: I’m Eric Nilson, based in the south of Sweden. I write soft guitar tunes with a hint of Swedish melancholy. I love composing, recording, mixing, and playing my father’s old Levin guitar. Glad you found your way here. Hope you like the songs.

name: Dorian Skye
bio: Rooted in classical tradition yet shaped by contemporary pop, guitarist Dorian Skye offers a moment of tranquility amid the ceaseless motion of modern life.

name: Jorge Huksos

name: Marée Claire
bio: Marée Claire creates delicate classical guitar music featuring graceful melodies, intricate fingerstyle, and warm acoustic tones. Her sound is intimate, expressive, and timeless.

name: Oaktree Melodies
bio: Drawing inspiration from life in its entirety, embracing both pain and beauty. The music is genuine, sensitive, and intimate.  Oaktree Melodies began playing the guitar at an early age,  and the creative process has always been an integral part of his musicianship.  He loves finding ways to convey emotions and thoughts through music and with the guitar in particular.  Inspiration can stem from a word, an image, or a film,  but Oaktree Melodies always envisions something visual when creating.  The music is organic, often featuring ambient electric guitars or acoustic guitar as the primary elements.

name: Noah Lorne
bio: Noah Lorne creates calm, peaceful  neo-classical guitar music, weaving delicate melodies with gentle harmonies. His compositions offer a serene escape, perfect for deep focus, relaxation, and quiet moments of reflection.

name: Ivan Pirman
bio: Built around warmth, stillness, and understated melodies, Ivan Pirman makes music for slowing down. Each track offers a peaceful backdrop for reflection, concentration, or simply letting the day unfold.

name: Nico Harper
bio: Built on patience and quiet introspection, the music of Nico Harper is crafted for unwinding and clearing the mind. These slow-moving textural tracks drift seamlessly into the background of your evening.

name: Lex Quirk
bio: In threads of sound the stillness flows. A hush of strings, a breath, a gleam. Like dawn unfolding in a dream.

name: Cecil Noss
bio: Cecil Noss creates atmospheric guitar music that invites calm, reflection, and presence. Through gentle melodies and harmonious arrangements, he crafts soundscapes that are equally suited for relaxation, focus, meditation, or simply a quiet moment in everyday life

name: Charlie Oakfield
bio: With roots in both classical and pop music, Charlie Oakfield records both covers  and original compositions on steel- and nylon-string guitars.  Beauty and fragility are key elements in Charlie Oakfield’s music, there must be emotional intensity and presence in every phrase and note.  The goal is to move the listener, not to impress,  authenticity matters more than perfection.  There is nowhere to hide behind the guitar, making every phrase crucial.

name: Carl Eksmo
bio: Carl Eksmo grew up in Gothenburg and started playing classical guitar at an early age. In the years that followed he switched to electric guitar and piano in various bands, in several genres. After graduating from the Academy of Music, today he works as a musician, music creator and music producer.  In January 2021, he released "Over Treetops" which is an instrumental EP. The music is written with inspiration from nature and as with all his music, Carl starts with a picture or a scene he wants to convey in his music creation.

bio: Basil M Jose is a pianist, composer, and producer dedicated to crafting intimate, cinematic soundscapes. Blending the emotive purity of solo piano with soft orchestral textures and organic ambient sound design, his music invites listeners into a space of reflection and stillness.  Drawing inspiration from the nuances of contemporary classical and modern minimalism, Basil creates compositions that feel both vast and deeply personal. Whether through delicate felt piano melodies or layered atmospheric pads, his work explores calm, hope, and emotional storytelling.

name: Huma
bio: HUMA is an ambient duo formed by Xalo Gayoso and Helga Blanco, composers and pianists with an extensive career across contemporary music, electronics, and composition for visual media.  The project is conceived as a conceptual body of work in which literature, city, and memory intertwine to shape fragmented sonic narratives: an intimate listening space where piano converses with electronic textures to explore stillness and contemplation amid the noise of the present. Their music moves between classical tradition and contemporary production, blending acoustic and digital elements into emotionally charged soundscapes. Huma sits within the lineage of the most intimate and restrained strains of ambient — with clear nods to works such as William Basinski's The Disintegration Loops and the albums of Stars of the Lid — offering a space for deep listening where emotion, always held in reserve, surfaces more as echo than as presence.

name: Fred Russ

Our selection of music is carefully curated to bring out the best of this genre.   Enjoy the journey of pandora. and explore the dreamscape with us.  Contact: pandora@unionentertainment.co

bio: Primary Sense is about returning to the basics. Born in the 1980s and active as a producer since the early 2000s, I focus on removing rather than adding. Slow piano, subtle electronics, pads and an intuitive workflow shape music inspired by small, everyday moments of calm.

bio: Nobuhiro Okahashi is a Japan-based electronic musician working with ambient and drone sound.  His music unfolds through sustained tones, slow modulation, and near-static movement. Built from layers of electronic signals and restrained gestures, the sound emphasizes duration over event, density over melody. Subtle changes emerge gradually, inviting deep listening and a heightened awareness of time, space, and resonance.  Based in the Osaka area, Okahashi releases music through the Tokyo label purregoohn and performs in Japan and abroad. He also organizes Naniwa Ambient, a gathering dedicated to immersive listening and experimental sound.

Beyond her musical training, Michelle is a Reiki Master, who practices yoga and meditation.

The Stockholm producer, composer and guitarist came up through classical and folk, and it shows in how he treats tone and room - solo tracks like "Run Like River Runs" and "Walking Through Walls" pair a vulnerable lyric with production that leaves plenty of air around it. He also writes and produces for other artists, among them Maybe, Zorro, Roof and Vicki Vox, moving between indie pop, acoustic fingerstyle and something closer to score. name: Florence Beatrice Price
bio: The first African-American woman whose music was played by a major symphony orchestra, Florence Price was a pioneering figure in 20th century American music. In the 21st century, her music has been performed increasingly often, especially since a large cache of her compositions was rediscovered in 2009. Price was born Florence Beatrice Smith in Little Rock, Arkansas, on April 9, 1887. Her father was a dentist, and her mother was a music teacher. She and her two siblings all took music lessons, and she emerged as the prodigy of the group, giving her first performance at age four. Price and African American composer William Grant Still attended the same elementary school. By the time she graduated as valedictorian of her segregated Catholic high school class, she had already published her first compositions. She attended the New England Conservatory of Music in Boston, studying piano and organ with the plan of becoming a music teacher. She also took composition lessons from George Whitefield Chadwick, who believed with Dvořák that the music of African Americans could form the basis of an American national school of composition; he encouraged her. Graduating in 1906, she returned to Arkansas, teaching for several years and then moving to Atlanta to head the music department at historically Black Clark Atlanta University. There, she married lawyer Thomas J. Price. The couple and their son fled the South in 1927 for Chicago, where Price took more composition lessons from Leo Sowerby, William Dawson, and the popular song composer Will Marion Cook. After Price and her husband divorced, she experienced several lean years, and she moved in with her student Margaret Bonds, making a living by writing jingles for radio commercials. Things picked up in 1932 when she took several honors in the Rodman Wanamaker Competition, and the following year, her Symphony No. 1 in E minor was performed by the Chicago Symphony Orchestra under conductor Frederick Stock. This was the first performance of music of an African American woman by a major orchestra. Price performed her Piano Concerto in D minor with the Chicago Women's Symphony in 1934. She wrote a large body of choral music that was performed on Chicago radio, as well as chamber music, keyboard music, and songs. In the late 1930s, soprano Marian Anderson performed her setting of Langston Hughes' poem cycle Songs to the Dark Virgin. Price's compositions rarely quote African American spirituals directly, but they use structural devices such as call-and-response that are characteristic of African American music. Price wrote three more symphonies and a suite for strings that was commissioned and performed by conductor John Barbirolli.
