name: Rex Orange County
bio: Alex O’Connor, known globally as Rex Orange County, is a multi-platinum singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, and producer. To date, he has amassed over 5 billion career streams and earned 4 RIAA platinum certifications.  Rex was just 16 when he self-released his debut album, bcos u will never b free. The project caught the attention of Tyler, The Creator, sparking a foundational collaboration that featured Rex on two tracks for Tyler’s acclaimed album Flower Boy.  From there, Rex’s solo career skyrocketed. His sophomore album Apricot Princess (2017) cracked the Top 10 of the US Billboard Independent Albums Chart, while 2019’s PONY reached #3 on the Billboard 200. By 2022, his fourth album WHO CARES? reunited him with Tyler, The Creator and went straight to #1 on the UK album chart, while hitting #2 in Australia and #5 in the US.  Always evolving, Rex's recent work bridges the gap between indie-pop sensibility and heavy-hitting collaborations. His 2024 album, The Alexander Technique, featured artist and producer James Blake. That same year, his feature on Ravyn Lenae's "Love Me Not" (produced by DJ Dahi) earned a VMA nomination for "Song of the Summer."  Stepping into 2025, Rex continues to push boundaries, releasing two celebrated collaborative tracks with Daniel Caesar ("Rearrange My World" and "There’s A Field"), alongside songwriting contributions from Mustafa and Devonté Hynes, followed by the Pharrell Williams-produced standout single "Take A Drive."

name: M.O.T.H.E.R.
bio: Conceived as an open, evolving project driven by Robbie Furze rather than a fixed band, M.O.T.H.E.R. is built around a shared creative history, with contributors shaping the music as it unfolds in the spirit of iconic groups such as N.E.R.D., UNKLE, and Massive Attack. This first release captures an initial moment of collaboration, while future installments are set to expand and shift — with different voices, line-ups and directions still to come. With contributions from longtime friends Jamie Hince (The Kills) and Jamie T, the four-track EP sees Furze fuse anthemic pop songcraft with supersized hooks and sharp-edged sonic invention, resulting in a singularly exciting approach all its own.  “M.O.T.H.E.R. is a project that responds and adapts to what’s happening in the moment,” says Robbie Furze. “This EP came from losing my mother, and everything around it grew out of that, a band of brothers coming together. The next release will be a completely different color and approach.” - Robbie Furze

name: Wednesday
bio: Bleeds is not only the best Wednesday record—it’s also the most Wednesday record, a patchwork-style triumph of literary allusions and outlaw grit, of place-based poetry and hair-raising noise. Karly Hartzman—founder, frontwoman, and primary lyricist—credits Wednesday’s tightened grasp on their own identity to time spent collaborating on previous albums, plus a tour schedule that’s been both rewarding and relentless. “Bleeds is the spiritual successor to Rat Saw God, and I think the quintessential ‘Wednesday Creek Rock’ album,” Hartzman said, articulating satisfaction with the ways her band has sharpened its trademark sound, how they’ve refined the formula that makes them one of the most interesting rock bands of their generation.   Just like Rat Saw God, one of the defining rock & roll records of the 2020s so far, Bleeds came together at Drop of Sun in Asheville and was produced by Alex Farrar, who’s been recording the band since Twin Plagues. Hartzman with bandmates—Xandy Chelmis (lap steel, pedal steel), Alan Miller (drums), Ethan Baechtold (bass, piano), and Jake “M.J.” Lenderman (guitar)—worked as a team to bulk-up the compositions with the exact right amounts of country truth-telling, indie-pop hooks, and noisy sludge. More than ever, the precise proportions were steered by the lyricism—not only its tone or subject matter, but also the actual sound of the words, as well as Hartzman’s masterfully subjective approach to detail selection.

name: Interpol
bio: This Mirror Weighs a Ton, finds the band turning inward while continuing to move forward. Across the record, reflection, distortion and perception become a lens through which familiar shapes are refracted into something slightly alien, as if seen through a different kind of light.  Synthesizers, strings, acoustic guitars and percussion are integrated into the fabric of the songs, expanding the palette while revealing colors already latent within it. Nothing feels imposed. Instead, the additions deepen the band’s language of restraint, atmosphere and tension. The result is an album that feels expansive, uncanny and alive with forward motion, not a reinvention but an evolution that allows Interpol to continue transforming without losing their identity.

name: Beck
bio: Californian alternative icon and pop polymath Beck experiments with genres and has an approach to style so fluid that the only thing one could expect from a new record is that it would be different from the last. The ubiquity of his 1994 lo-fi rap/folk slacker anthem "Loser" pointed toward one-hit-wonder status, but those predictions were punctured by the boundary-pushing work that quickly followed. Far from the short-lived novelty act his early success might have suggested, Beck continued down his unique and ever-winding path for decades, taking on new forms with every release. He had a creative breakthrough with 1996's Odelay, a co-production with the Dust Brothers that touched upon his obsessions with crate-dug samples and synthesizing elements of funk, soul, hip-hop, blues, lounge music, and all other manner of found sounds. Odelay served as a cultural keystone for the fading '90s while telegraphing all of Beck's future moves, from the soul prankster of Midnite Vultures to the melancholy troubadour of Sea Change. He moved between the extremes of satire and sincerity throughout the 21st century, sometimes fusing the two emotions, as on 2008's Modern Guilt. Achievements like his 2015 album Morning Phase taking home the Grammy for Album of the Year underscored Beck's presence in the music industry, and he continued pushing creative boundaries in collaborations with everyone from Jenny Lewis to Paul McCartney, and on solo albums like 2019's Pharrell Williams-assisted Hyperspace. In 2026, Beck continued the mode of his sad, reflective albums with the Nigel Godrich-produced Ride Lonesome. Fittingly, Beck came from a distinctly artistic background, the son of string arranger/conductor David Campbell and Bibbe Hansen, the latter a regular at Andy Warhol's Factory whose father was a pivotal contributor to the Fluxus art movement. Adopting the Hansen surname after his father left, Beck grew up in Los Angeles, dropping out of school in the tenth grade to play as a street busker and attend poetry slams. Bashing out blues and folk, Beck wound up assembling a home tape called The Banjo Story before departing for New York, where he operated on the margins of the anti-folk scene without ever breaking into it. He returned to Los Angeles, where he continued to play clubs, eventually gaining the attention of Bong Load Records, an independent operated by Tom Rothrock and Rob Schnapf. All parties agreed to pair Beck's fledgling folk with hip-hop beats assembled by producer Karl Stephenson, whose kitchen provided the studio for their first efforts, including "Loser." These tapes remained unreleased as Beck recorded an album's worth of material with Calvin Johnson for the latter's K label, but the first release Beck had was the Flipside single "MTV Makes Me Want to Smoke Crack" and Sonic Enemy's cassette release of Golden Feelings. However, what really broke the doors open was Bong Load's 12" single of "Loser," which garnered considerable play in L.A., coinciding with increased underground attention. Soon, Beck signed with Geffen, striking a deal that allowed him to release on independent labels. One of these immediately followed -- Fingerpaint released the 10" record A Western Harvest Field by Moonlight in January 1994 -- before the Geffen debut Mellow Gold appeared in March of that year. Naturally, "Loser" was the lead single from Mellow Gold and it turned into an instant smash, boasting a hook that worked as an ironic underground rallying cry and a novelty crossover. Despite many positive reviews, Beck worked overtime to dispel the notion he was a novelty, quickly releasing two indie albums in succession: the noise-skronk Stereopathetic Soul Manure and One Foot in the Grave. Stereopathetic made few waves, but the stripped-back, folky One Foot in the Grave acted as a counterbalance to the gonzo Mellow Gold, illustrating the depths of his talents. After a furious 1994, Beck laid relatively low in 1995, touring with the fifth Lollapalooza in between working on a new album with the production team the Dust Brothers, who had collaborated with the Beastie Boys on their landmark 1989 Paul's Boutique. The resulting album, Odelay, appeared in June 1996, preceded by the lanky, funky single "Where It's At," which would go on to win the Grammy for Best Male Rock Vocal. Odelay piled up acclaim and hits -- "Devil's Haircut," "Jack-Ass," and "The New Pollution" all charted around the world -- and the record went double platinum, becoming a touchstone of '90s alternative rock. An outtake from the album, "Deadweight," appeared on the soundtrack to Danny Boyle's 1997 film A Life Less Ordinary, and then Beck set to work on his next album with producer Nigel Godrich, who had just worked with Radiohead on OK Computer. Their collaboration, originally slated for an indie release but moved to Geffen, thereby setting a precedent that no future Beck LP would be released on an indie (something worked out in the courts the following year), traded futuristic rock -- either the joyous collage of Odelay or the dystopia of OK Computer -- for a quiet, pulsating, psychedelic folk-rock album called Mutations. Riding high on Odelay, the record charted well without turning out any major hits, although it did garner a Grammy for Best Alternative Music Performance. Beck made another abrupt change in musical direction in 1999 with Midnite Vultures, a garish party record that was part satire and part salute to soul and funk, particularly Prince. Reviews were divided between ecstatic and skeptical, but the album had some real hits with "Sexx Laws" and "Deborah," and in some ways it was the apex of Beck's hipster prankster phase, a persona he shed with his next album, 2002's Sea Change. Recorded in the wake of a romantic breakup, Sea Change was another Godrich production, but it was gentle and mournful, lacking some of the gritty underpinnings of Mutations but retaining the psychedelia -- and that psychedelic edge was brought out in the supporting tour when Beck hired the Flaming Lips as his supporting band. The tour was well-received, but there were some tensions, as reported by Lips leader Wayne Coyne later. After an extended break -- the longest he had taken between albums to date -- Beck returned in 2005 with Guero, an album that reunited him with the Dust Brothers and consciously evoked Odelay. Guero launched a few hits, including "E-Pro" and "Hell Yes," and was followed within months by Guerolito, a remixed version of the entire album. Beck continued in this direction the following year with The Information, but its Nigel Godrich production kept the album streamlined and emphasized the darker undercurrents in the songs. Some of that darkness could be heard on his eighth LP, Modern Guilt, a 2008 release produced by Danger Mouse, marking the first time in 14 years that Beck worked with a producer who wasn't the Dust Brothers or Godrich. Modern Guilt performed respectably -- it debuted at eight on the U.S. Billboard charts and received strong reviews -- but he spent the next several years relatively quiet. In 2009, Beck began actively pursuing a career as a producer, collaborating with Charlotte Gainsbourg on her acclaimed IRM album; two years later, he produced Thurston Moore's Demolished Thoughts and Mirror Traffic by Stephen Malkmus & the Jicks. He also dipped his toe back into solo recording on the soundtrack to the 2010 Edgar Wright film Scott Pilgrim vs. the World. Still, between 2009 and 2010, much of his studio energy was devoted to his Record Club, where he and a loose collective of friends covered classic albums in their entirety; the albums covered included The Velvet Underground & Nico, The Songs of Leonard Cohen, and INXS' Kick. Beck returned to original material in 2012 via Song Reader, a collection of sheet music featuring 20 new, unrecorded songs; although he didn't record versions of these songs, he did appear at Song Reader concerts featuring other musicians (and a collection of those live performances was eventually released under his name). In 2014, Beck released Morning Phase, his first new album in nearly six years and first record for Capitol. Described by the singer/songwriter as a "companion piece" to 2002's Sea Change, it appeared in February 2014, preceded by the singles "Blue Moon" and "Waking Light." Critical reception was largely positive, and the set won three Grammy Awards, including Best Rock Album and Album of the Year. Beck returned the following year with the lively single "Dreams," and the like-minded "Wow" arrived in 2016. During that year, he continued working with producer Greg Kurstin and also made guest appearances on work by Fun.'s Nate Ruess, the Chemical Brothers, M83, and Flume. Beck finally released Colors, his collaboration with Kurstin, in October 2017. It peaked at number three on the Billboard 200, and topped the modern rock and alternative albums charts. Colors won the 2019 Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album, along with the trophy for Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical. In 2019, Beck contributed the song "Tarantula" to the soundtrack album Music Inspired by the Film Roma, which accompanied director Alfonso Cuarón's acclaimed work. That November, Beck released Hyperspace, an album largely produced by Pharrell Williams. Initially, Williams invited Beck to contribute to a N.E.R.D album, but the collaboration proved fruitful, resulting in the core of the record that became Hyperspace. In 2019, he also collaborated with Jenny Lewis and tourmates Cage the Elephant. The next few years brought more collaborations, as Beck worked with Gorillaz on their 2020 song "The Valley of the Pagans," singer/songwriter Natalie Bergman on a 2021 cover of Lion's deep cut "You've Got a Woman," and Paul McCartney on "Find My Way," a hit single from the 2021 album McCartney III: Imagined. Beck released a cover of Neil Young's "Old Man" in 2022, and an original titled "Thinking About You" in 2023. In 2026, as more time had passed without a new studio album, Beck released Everybody's Gotta Learn Sometime, a short compilation with eight previously released cover songs, assembled into the format of a mini-album. Only a few months later, however, his next proper studio album, Ride Lonesome, arrived. This album continued the style of heartbroken orchestral folk that Beck had first broken ground on with Sea Change, and returned to with Morning Phase. The similarities in the three records were emphasized by Beck reuniting with the same personnel who had helped him realize those albums, including the original backing players and producer Nigel Godrich. ~ Stephen Thomas Erlewine

Modest Mouse released their highly anticipated new album, The Golden Casket, on June 25, 2021 via Epic Records. The Golden Casket heralds another new chapter in the GRAMMY® Award-nominated multi platinum band’s unpredictable evolution. Produced with Dave Sardy and Jacknife Lee in Los Angeles and in Modest Mouse’s studio in Portland, the album hovers in the liminal space between raw punk power and experimental studio science, frontman Isaac Brock explores themes ranging from the degradation of our psychic landscapes and invisible technology, to fatherhood. The twelve tracks behave like amorphous organisms, undergoing dramatic mutations and mood swings that speak to the chronic tug-of-war between hope and despair that plays out in Brock’s head.

name: Jack White
bio: Jack White is one of the 21st century's great rock conceptualists. He came to fame as the leader of the White Stripes, the Detroit-based garage-punk duo who unexpectedly became one of the biggest rock acts of the 2000s. The White Stripes established White as a roots rocker -- he made sure they covered blues chestnuts from Son House -- to such a degree that his modernist art instincts were somewhat overshadowed during the band's peak. These dueling, sometimes complementary instincts, fueled White's myriad artistic pursuits both within and without the confines of the White Stripes. Almost immediately after White Blood Cells gave the duo a blockbuster in 2001 he started working outside of the group, producing Loretta Lynn's Van Lear Rose and forming the Raconteurs with Brendan Benson as well as the Dead Weather with the Kills' Alison Mosshart. Once the White Stripes called it a day in 2011, his voracious musical appetite and strict work ethic flourished, as White divided his time between his Third Man Records empire, the Raconteurs and Dead Weather, and a solo career that grew increasingly idiosyncratic with each album. Blunderbuss (2012) and Lazaretto (2014) stayed near the territory he covered with the White Stripes, but the proggy oddity of 2018's Boarding House Reach didn't prove to be a detour, as the twin 2022 albums Fear of the Dawn and Entering Heaven Alive proved: the noisy rock of the former was complemented by the quiet, introspective adventure of the latter. On 2024's Grammy-nominated No Name, he reconnected with bluesy, high-octane rock -- a path he continued with 2026's Frozen Charlotte, which arrived a year after White's induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. John Anthony Gillis was born in Detroit on July 9, 1975. The youngest of ten siblings, he began playing drums at an early age and took inspiration from the world-weary blues of Son House and Blind Willie McTell. A fascination with guitar followed in his teenage years. After launching his own upholstery business in Detroit, White began to infiltrate the city's music scene as the drummer for Goober & the Peas, a local cowpunk band that split in 1995. While continuing to play drums for other groups, he crossed paths with a bartender named Meg White, and the two were married in 1996. Jack took Meg's surname, and the pair formed the White Stripes after a Bastille Day jam session showed promising results. With their color-coded image and raw, punky sound, the White Stripes became a key component of the garage rock revival of the late '90s. In addition to their music, the bandmembers stirred public interest by claiming to be siblings, a declaration that seemed slightly less incestuous when Jack and Meg White divorced in 2000. Despite the split, the White Stripes only grew in popularity as the decade progressed, eventually winning three consecutive Grammy Awards and issuing several platinum-certified albums. Following the release of Elephant in 2003, Jack White took a break from the group to produce Loretta Lynn's Van Lear Rose. A critical smash, the album helped endear Lynn to a new generation of fans, thanks in part to White's credibility as a rock artist. He then returned to the White Stripes for the release of Get Behind Me Satan, which saw him expanding his instrumental range with piano and marimba. Shortly thereafter, he launched a concurrent group, the Raconteurs, with friend Brendan Benson and two members of the Greenhornes (who, incidentally, had served as backing musicians on Van Lear Rose). The Raconteurs made their debut with 2006's Broken Boy Soldiers and toured in support of the album, while White publicly stressed that his work in the band should not be seen as a side project or a diversion from the White Stripes. Thus, he began juggling his responsibilities to both groups, partnering with Meg White once again for the White Stripes' 2007 release Icky Thump before returning to the Raconteurs for 2008's Consolers of the Lonely. While touring in support of the latter album, White suffered from bronchitis and often lost his voice, prompting singer Alison Mosshart (from the Raconteurs' touring partners the Kills) to climb on-stage and contribute her own vocals. The chemistry between Mosshart and the Raconteurs proved alluring, and the musicians opted to form a separate group named the Dead Weather. With Jack White now handling drums, the band retreated to the studio and recorded an energetic debut, Horehound, in a matter of weeks. Released in 2009, the album was well-received on both sides of the Atlantic, cracking the Top Ten in America and peaking at number 14 in the U.K. Encouraged by such success, the Dead Weather began working on their second album, 2010's Sea of Cowards. In the meantime, White secured enough free time to appear in a movie -- the guitar-themed It Might Get Loud -- and produce an album, The Ghost Who Walks, for his then-wife, songwriter Karen Elson. The first solo outing from White, the bluesy, typically idiosyncratic Blunderbuss, arrived in April of 2012. Named for a muzzle-loading firearm that was a precursor of the shotgun, it promptly debuted in the American charts at number one, the first White-associated album to do so. Certified gold in the U.S., the U.K., and Australia, and certified platinum in Canada, Blunderbuss also earned several Grammy nominations, including Album of the Year, Best Rock Album, and Best Rock Song for "Freedom at 21." White's second solo album, Lazaretto, followed in June 2014, preceded by the single "High Ball Stepper." Earning positive reviews, it also debuted at number one on the U.S. 200 Albums Chart and reached the Top Five on the charts in eight other countries. The Dead Weather released their third album, Dodge and Burn, in September 2015, and a year later White issued Acoustic Recordings 1998-2016, a double-disc compilation of acoustic numbers from his various projects. In April 2017, he released a surprise instrumental single called "Battle Cry." A lifelong baseball fan, it was announced that the song would be used as the walk-up music for Detroit Tigers infielder Ian Kinsler, with whom White co-owns the baseball bat company Warstic. In March 2018, the strange, sprawling Boarding House Reach was released, peaking at number one on the Billboard 200 and topping the charts in Canada. The following year, he was back with the Raconteurs for the group's third album, Help Us Stranger. In November 2021, White returned with "Taking Me Back," a single released in two versions: a noisy, gnarled rock incarnation and a softer acoustic variation. The rock spin on "Taking Me Back" heralded April 2022's Fear of the Dawn, a nervy, noisy record that found White experimenting with digital effects. The album debuted in the Top Ten of the U.S. charts, as did Entering Heaven Alive, a quieter but still restless record anchored by the jaunty acoustic revision of "Taking Me Back (Gently)." Entering Heaven Alive appeared that July, while White was in the middle of a lengthy and eventful tour that saw him getting married onstage and playing Saturday Night Live for the fifth time. White surprised fans on in July 2024 with the release of a bares-bones, blues-influenced album titled No Name. It was packaged like a white-label promo with only the words "No Name" stamped on the sleeve and was given away to customers at Third Man records locations for free. It topped the U.K. Independent Albums chart, cracked the Billboard 200, and finished the year with a Grammy nomination for Best Rock Album. A pair of concert EPs, No Name Live and Live at Ford Field, appeared in 2025, the latter one featuring a collaboration with fellow Detroiter Eminem during the Detroit Lions halftime show. Late that year, White was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame for his work with the White Stripes. In April 2026, ahead of his sixth appearance on Saturday Night Live, White released the singles "G.O.D. and the Broken Ribs" and "Derecho Demonico." Ever busy, that May he appeared on the Michigan public access show Only In Monroe with Stephen Colbert following the cancellation of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and launched These Thoughts May Disappear, a major exhibition of his artwork, at London's Newport Street Gallery. Imagery from the exhibit, as well as "G.O.D. and the Broken Ribs" and "Derecho Demonico," featured on White's seventh full-length Frozen Charlotte. Appearing that July, the album continued in the tight, garage-blues vein of No Name. ~ Andrew Leahey & Stephen Thomas Erlewine, Rovi

name: Taba Chake
bio: Taba Chake is an Indian finger-style guitarist, multi-instrumentalist, and multilingual singer-songwriter. Known for his soulful blend of folk, indie, and contemporary sounds, he rose to prominence with tracks like “Aao Chalein,” “Shaayad,” and “Walk With Me” from his acclaimed debut album Bombay Dreams (2019). Writing in multiple languages, including his native Nyishi dialect, Hindi, Assamese, and English—Chake is celebrated as the first artist from Arunachal Pradesh to compose and release Nyishi songs on global streaming platforms.  Chake began his independent career in 2012, releasing his first EP Bond With Nature in 2016. His breakthrough came three years later with Bombay Dreams, a 10-track project that established him as one of the most original voices in India’s indie music scene. Over the years, he has graced some of the country’s most prestigious stages, including Ziro Festival of Music, NH7 Weekender, Axean Festival, Royal Enfield Motoverse 2023, and the Arunachal GI Mahotsav 2025 in New Delhi, inaugurated by Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein.  His music is deeply philosophical, often weaving themes of introspection, self-realization, and interconnectedness with nature and the universe. With poetic lyrics and minimalist yet profound melodies, Chake’s compositions invite listeners to rediscover forgotten aspects of the inner self while creating a space for emotional resonance and reflection.

name: Parvaaz
bio: Parvaaz brings a constellation of rooted stories and textured sounds that embrace the winds of folk, blues, rock, and psychedelia. Their discography is a repository of Kashmiri and Urdu poetry, weaving words of longing, tenacity, and transcendence. Their soundscapes feel at once familiar and elusive, intimate and boundless.  Parvaaz took shape in Bangalore in 2010 when friends Khalid Ahamed and Mir Kashif Iqbal came together to make music that can be their own. Soon after, Sachin Banandur on drums and Fidel D’Souza on bass joined in, and the quartet began weaving a sound that would quietly carve out its place in India’s independent music scene. Their early work — Dil Khush (2011), the EP Behosh (2012), and the single Khufiya Dastaan (2013) - carried the first echoes of what was to come, hinting at a journey that was only just beginning. Their debut album Baran (2014) arrived like a landmark - a haunting conversation where poetry met sound. With the live album Transitions (2016) and later their magnum opus Kun (2019), the band extended their voice to wider audiences while expanding their sonic philosophy.  Following the departure of co-founder Mir Kashif Iqbal in 2021, Parvaaz welcomed Bharath Kashyap on guitar. The band has been touring with renewed energy, while letting new ideas take root; a new chapter that will find its fullest expression in their forthcoming third album, slated for release in late 2025.

name: Neyhal
bio: Meet neyhal, an independent artist whose music lives somewhere between existential reflection, nightlife euphoria and emotional surrender. Born and raised in Nagpur he left home at 16 and got acquainted by loneliness, heartbreak and self-discovery early on, he began making music as a way to understand both himself and the world around him. Blending indie songwriting with electronic textures and cinematic emotion, Neyhal’s work feels intimate yet expansive - songs built for train rides, crowded nights, memory haze and moments of emotional release. His upcoming EP Naya Daur is “A retro-futuristic Hindi disco EP about loneliness, surrender, love, mortality and liberation. It feels like the modern world collapsing while he plays his song drunk in the juice of existence, grateful for life. Dancing in a post apocalyptic world while he can, staring right in the eyes of chaos and still choosing ecstasy. name: Saahel
bio: Saahel is a singer-songwriter crafting contemporary Hindi pop with heartfelt storytelling and modern, genre-fluid production. Known for his warm melodies and emotionally resonant songwriting, his music explores themes of love, longing, nostalgia, and human connection in ways that feel both personal and relatable.  Writing, composing, and producing much of his own music, Saahel has steadily built a loyal audience through releases such as Tera Pata , Zulfe, and Baarish Mein Phir. Following the success of Tera Pata, he was featured on Spotify's Times Square billboard as part of the RADAR India program. Today, his music resonates strongly with listeners across India, with Mumbai, Delhi, and Bengaluru emerging as his top streaming cities.  No matter where his listeners are in the world or what music they listen to, Saahel's songs feel like coming back home. Familiar, comforting, and deeply personal, his music creates a connection that stays with listeners long after the song ends.

name: Khatth
bio: Khatth (meaning ‘letter’) is an independent band from Bhubaneshwar, Odisha, formed in the summer of 2019 by Aditya Atmakuri, Ashutosh Verma, and Satyam Nayak.  The trio, based out of different cities and known for a sound that ranges from acoustic love ballads to disco-inspired pop numbers, merges their differences to craft music that is emotionally resonant, sonically diverse, and unmistakably their own. Their emotionally resonant music videos further strengthened their growing fanbase and visual identity.  Blending introspective songwriting with layered production, Khatth draws influence from Jon Bellion, Sufjan Stevens, and Strings.   Despite being in different countries, they meet annually in a chosen city and studio to record three songs, then perform live shows there to immediately test and reflect on their work through audience reactions.

name: The Local Train
bio: The Local Train is a Hindi Rock Band from New Delhi. The band launched their debut album 'Aalas ka Pedh' in 2015 and their second album ‘Vaaqif’ was released in January 2018. Both the albums went on to  become one of the most streamed independent albums in India. The band is known for their explosive concerts and massive sing along hits.  They’ve had a cult following since then and are perhaps one of the few rock artists in the country that have achieved mainstream popularity.

name: Shruti Prakash Dash
bio: Shruti Prakash Dash is a music producer and composer from Odisha, creating sounds that blend emotion, melody, and atmosphere.  He has produced music for films like Daman, Parab, Bigul and releases his produced tracks with Khatth. That includes 'Woh ft. Sthiti' under the label of Sony Music India.  His style brings together folk influences, modern production, and cinematic moods to make music that feels personal and honest.

name: Ramil Ganjoo

name: Mansa Jimmy
bio: Mansa Jimmy is a singer-songwriter hailing from the serene town of Nainital. With over a thousand live performances to her credit, she has carved a distinct space for herself in the Indian music landscape. Her work spans writing lyrics for films across the country, contributing to acclaimed projects such as Coke Studio Bharat, Merchant Records’ SoundCheck, and a wide range of jingles and musical collaborations.  Known for her genre-fluid approach, Mansa resists being boxed into a single musical style. While she embraces versatility in her sound, she holds a special affinity for Sufi, folk, and rock influences. Her original compositions are deeply lyric-driven, ranging from grand cinematic arrangements to minimalist storytelling, with a thread of melancholia weaving through them all.

name: Samad Khan
bio: Meet Samad Khan, a  singer and songwriter whose musical journey is a beautiful blend of classical elegance and contemporary expression. With roots in Gurugram and a current home in the vibrant city of Mumbai, Samad's melodies resonate with the poetic essence of the Urdu language.  Embarking on his musical journey at the age of 8, Samad has matured into a multi-instrumentalist , playing instruments such as the piano, guitar, and drums, adding layers of depth to his music.  In 2020, at just 20, he made waves by releasing his debut EP in collaboration with UK-based artist Max Cooper, contributing to the soundtrack of Jacob Jonas's film, "Weakness of the Flesh," based in Los Angeles which went on to be picked by various international radio platforms and featured in international film and music festivals around the world.  Samad is not merely a recording artist; he's a dynamic performer. Since the tender age of 10-12, he has been gracing stages, leaving audiences spellbound in iconic venues like the JLN Stadium in Delhi and even on international stages like Budapest, Hungary.  Samad is currently exploring new horizons by delving into genres like Pop and R&B experimenting with Indian Music and taking it to the global stage.

name: Rovalio
bio: Rovalio also known as Rommel Yazdan is a Billboard Chart topping producer from Gilgit, Pakistan. He started making music when he was 15 years old, he created his niche in Hip Hop working with artists like Talha Anjum and Talhah Yunus. He later produced the debut album for Shamoon Ismail, "Scars & Screws " He has collaborated with artists in South Asia like Young Stunners, Talha Anjum, Talhah Yunus, Hasan Raheem, Umair, Annural Khalid, Maanu, KR$NA & Bayaan to name a few. In 2022 he made his name with Bikhra & Iraaday with Abdul Hannan, charting Spotify Pakistan's number 1 position for over 150 days & staying in the top 10 for 379 days straight. Iraaday & Bikhra have amassed over 200 million views on Youtube & crossed 300 million Streams on Spotify. In 2024 Rovalio & Umair produced Hisaab for Karan Aujla & DIVINE on their Street Dreams Album. It charted No. 22 on the Billboard Hot 100 charts & peaked at No. 7 on the Spotify debut global albums, The album charted in 36 countries & was the No. 1 album on Apple Music in India, Canada & Australia. In 2024 Rovalio collaborated with Bayaan and Hasan Raheem on Maand which crossed 50 million streams & was No. 1 in Pakistan, No. 5 in India & also charting in the top 10 Global Viral Hits. With over 700 million streams combined, the influence of Rovalio's signature sound can be seen on Hip Hop & Pop music all over South Asia.

name: Marshall Ahmad
bio: Marshall Ahmad, sometimes affectionately known as Marshi, escaped corporate slavery to pursue his career in music. Started off as a vocalist in an underground pop-rock band called Arsenic in his early years, he accumulated a smaller fanbase of friends and family and decided to release his own music under his name, so learned to produce himself. Marshall released his first self-produced single Waaday (feat. Maliha J. Khan) Waaday being especially unorthodox for the time in terms of production brought attention from the industry, allowing him to further his craft by learning through his peers, collaborators and their belief in his projects. Cheese , Take Me Home and Bygones were instantly popular as fresh sounds in the scene, featured multiple times on the Fresh Finds Playlist by Spotify. Take Me Home's unique lyric-less falsetto chorus dubbed him lovingly as the falsetto queen, says he has 'crazy falsetto-y tracks in the vault', still marinating. Later releasing fan favourite tracks like Paas, All Mine (featuring Annural Khalid), and recently, Different (written by Hasan Raheem). His recent EP MADEMEN with Shahmeer Raza Khan, comes from, in his own words, 'his Guy Ritchie era', borrowing grungy and absurdist themes for the world of the EP, juxtaposing them with his unique take on R&b, house and pop. \\socials: @marshallahmadd\\

name: maahi
bio: Music is Maahi’s heartbeat. At the young age of 9, he followed his heart and decided to pursue music. Since then, he has dedicated himself to honing his craft, training, experimenting, and relentlessly learning. With a strong emphasis on meaningful lyrics and an unwavering love for pop music, Maahi has embarked on a journey to connect with audiences.   His debut song, “Sorry,” has already garnered over 15 million views and counting on YouTube and captured many hearts, becoming a favorite track for many. His second release, “Jaadugari,” has been warmly received since its recent release and is on track to becoming one of the most loved romantic songs. Amidst other achievements, Maahi was one of the Saregama Talents that performed at the Cannes Film Festival 2024 at Hotel Majestic, representing India at a young age. As his journey unfolds with promise, each verse echoes his core truth: his heart beats to the rhythm of his music.

bio: Suzonn is an independent singer-songwriter hailing from Guwahati, Assam. With a musical style that traverses the realms of Indie folk, Indie pop, Indian indie, and Indian Pop, Suzonn is a genre-defying artist who captivates listeners with his emotionally charged compositions. Suzonn's musical journey began at his teenage when he discovered a profound connection to music as a means of expressing his myriad of feelings and emotions. Each of his songs is a unique and heartfelt expression of his innermost thoughts, making him stand out as a remarkably versatile artist. Among his notable works, tracks like Farq hai , Sun Lo Na (Raw) , Rihaee and Tu Jo Paas have caught the hearts of many, resonating particularly with the younger audience. The ability to craft such diverse and relatable music has earned him a loyal following, with fans drawn to his distinctive approach to storytelling through song. Driven by an independent spirit, Suzonn has been a trailblazer in the music industry, charting his own path and remaining true to his artistic vision. Through his tireless efforts and DIY approach, he has carved a niche for himself in the music scene, gaining recognition not only in India but also beyond its borders.

bio: Adnan Dhool is a renowned Pakistani singer and songwriter, known for his remarkable contributions to the music industry. He is also a composer known for his composition of the song Awari from the film Ek Villain and also Mast Malang from the movie Malang.  He gained fame as one half of the music duo "Soch," which rose to prominence with their hit songs Bandeya and Nery Nery vas He also performed in Coke Studio and Nescafe basement. Adnan's soulful voice and emotive performances have earned him a devoted fan base in both Pakistan and India. With his talent and passion for music, Adnan continues to leave a lasting impact on audiences across the globe. Currently, Adnan is working on his solo material and has released many solo tracks including Chalo Choro, Jan E Man, and Saddiyan his latest track is Pardes Katenda is trending due to its soulful lyrics and groovy beat.

name: Abdul Hannan
bio: Abdul Hannan has revolutionised what it means to take the music industry by storm as a singer-songwriter. A software engineer by profession, he pursued music simultaneously and gained attention with his debut single "Faaslay" in 2020 while working full-time. The song was well received and signaled the arrival of a new icon in Pakistan's music scene.  Hannan’s subsequent releases however, “Bikhra” and “Iraaday” cemented him as a global icon in the making. Both tracks dominated the Pakistani top 10 charts for over 100 weeks straight while also making a mark on international charts. "Bikhra" clinched the number one spot, while "Iraaday" followed closely at number two for several months. One of his next releases, "Siyah," also secured a place in the top 10 charts in Pakistan, making it the third of his songs. Being consistently ranked in the top 10 most streamed artists on Spotify in Pakistan, his music has remained on the charts since 2022.  His song “Iraaday" achieved international recognition by making it onto the US Secretary's playlist of the year, showcasing Hannan's global appeal.   In 2024, Abdul Hannan made a remarkable appearance on the globally renowned music platform Coke Studio for Season 15. His song "O Yaara” became the season's highlight, receiving widespread acclaim and high streaming numbers from all over the world.  Abdul Hannan's discography has accumulated hundreds of millions of streams, making him one of the most-listened-to artists in Pakistan.

name: Ritviz
bio: Ritviz is an Indian sonic architect, effortlessly blending the traditional and the contemporary. His music is a vibrant tapestry woven from traditional Indian melodies, electronic beats, and introspective lyricism.  Born into a middle class Indian family, Ritviz's artistic journey began early. Exposed to the rich world of Hindustani classical music from the young age of 6 years, thanks to his mother Mrs. Anvita Bharti, an Indian classical singer and Performing Art HOD. In 2017, Ritviz's career took a meteoric rise with his infectious single, "Udd Gaye." This explosive blend of hip-hop and electronica, infused with traditional Indian elements, became an anthem propelling Ritviz to national & international fame. Since then, he has carved his own niche in the Indian music scene, churning out chart-topping hits like "Jeet", "Sage", "Liggi", “Baaraat” & “Aaj Na” each one a testament to his ability to seamlessly blend genres and create music that resonates with the soul.  Ritviz's music is more than just a sound; it's a cultural tapestry, a bridge between generations and traditions. He is a torchbearer for India's sonic evolution, a testament to the power of creative fusion, and an artist who continues to push boundaries and redefine what Indian music can be.

name: Zeeshan Ali
bio: Zeeshan Ali is a classically trained vocalist and musician from Lahore, widely recognised for his command over ghazal, Sufi, and semi-classical forms. Grounded in traditional South Asian vocal discipline, his work balances technical precision with emotional restraint, leaving space for both heritage and personal expression. He first came into wider recognition through NESCAFÉ Basement (Season 4) with his rendition of Tere Jeya Hor Disda, a performance that established him as a vocalist of depth, control, and sincerity. This momentum was further strengthened by his critically acclaimed rendition of Saadgi, presented with minimal piano and vocals. Zeeshan’s interpretation resonated with listeners globally and led to collaborations with respected platforms such as Sufi Score and Coke Studio Pakistan. Pushing his exploration of sound further, Zeeshan went on to form the band Surkhwaab fusion project that brings classical thumri sensibilities into dialogue with jazz and blues-influenced arrangements. More recently, he has performed at the Darbar Festival, including events for London’s Barbican Centre, situating his voice within a broader global South Asian music landscape.

name: Umair
bio: Umair is an alternative R&B and Hip Hop producer known for his distinctive, genre-bending sound. Born in 2003 in Karachi, Pakistan, as Muhammad Umair Tahir, Umair began making beats in his bedroom at just 13 years, inspired by producers like Boi-1da, 40,  Mike Dean & WondaGurl, he gradually developed a sound that blends atmospheric textures with hard-hitting hip-hop sensibilities. Umair initially explored house music in 2016 before transitioning into hip hop. His breakout moment came in 2019 with the debut single “Asli Hai” alongside Young Stunners, which made waves across the subcontinent and peaked at #1 on the Pakistani YouTube Charts. The release marked the beginning of a run that would help redefine the sonic direction of modern Pakistani hip hop. Since then, Umair has collaborated extensively with leading artists including Talha Anjum, Talhah Yunus, Hasan Raheem, Karan Aujla, Shamoon Ismail, Faris Shafi and many others contributing to several influential records that have played a significant role in shaping the country’s contemporary music scene. Expanding his vision beyond borders, Umair has also been instrumental in facilitating international collaborations, notably Smino & Kenny Mason and more projects that broadened his artistic identity worldwide. With millions of streams and a rapidly growing global fanbase, Umair has established himself at the forefront of South Asian hip hop.

name: Prateek Kuhad
bio: Lauded by Rolling Stone India as “one of the country’s leading singer-songwriters,” Kuhad’s cinematic songwriting reminds us that great music can often make intimacy feel expansive. A pair of early EPs put Kuhad on the map, followed by his full-length debut in 2017, In Tokens and Charms, which earned Kuhad Indie Album of the Year honors from iTunes. In 2018, his EP “cold/mess” debuted at #1 on Spotify India. He maintained this momentum with “Kasoor” in 2020, which became the first independently released track in India to claim the #1 spot on Apple Music’s all-genre chart. Released in 2022, The Way That Lovers Do earned new fanfare, with “Co2” now becoming his most-streamed track on Spotify. Kuhad has headlined festivals like Lollapalooza India and sold out headline tours across North America, Europe, UK, Asia, and the Middle East. 2026 marks the arrival of Kuhad’s third studio album, Full Moon Chamber, via Atlantic Records. Created between New York and Los Angeles, the project explores themes of love, identity, and emotional transformation — capturing a period of both personal and artistic evolution.

Her journey began in 2016 when a viral cover at just 11 years old introduced her remarkable vocal talent to the world. In 2024, she was selected as Spotify’s first EQUAL Pakistan Ambassador, marking a major milestone in her career.  Her debut single “Beqadra” emerged through Spotify’s Fresh Finds program, achieving a 2852% listener surge and crossing 7 million streams worldwide. Known for her soulful storytelling, emotional honesty, and cinematic indie-pop sound, Nehaal continues to captivate audiences with every release.  She has also contributed several OSTs for Pakistani dramas and web series, solidifying her reputation as a dynamic, genre-bending artist shaping the next wave of South Asian music.

name: AUR
bio: Karachi-born, emotion-engineered. AUR turns heartbreak into slow-burn anthems—soft, cinematic, unapologetically desi.  Since 2022, Usama Ali, Ahad Khan, and Raffey Anwar have scored timelines with memories: viral spark “Tu Hai Kahan,” sing-alongs “Chal Diye Tum,” “Long Time No See,” “Shikayat,” and the ballad-heavy EP Par Ab Jo Aayegi Tu (May 2025). name: Talal Qureshi
bio: Pakistani music producer and composer, Talal Qureshi, stands as a dynamic artist renowned for pushing boundaries in the electronic and experimental music realm. Seamlessly melding traditional Pakistani music with contemporary electronic sounds, he's become a vanguard of innovation.  TQ’s sonic palette spans bubblegum and synth-pop, a blend that defies norms and resonates globally. His groundbreaking and first-of-its-kind collaboration with Naseebo Lal birthed "AAG," a track which catalysed a new era in Pakistani music. Bridging East and West, he crafted music that found its way to Marvel’s hit TV series ‘Ms. Marvel’ and even became an anthem for the Pakistani feminist movement Aurat March.  Now a mainstay and collaborator in Coke Studio, Talal’s collaborative spirit knows no generational bounds. Artists like Atif Aslam, Hasan Raheem, Maanu and  Faris Shafi have all harmonized with his vision.  His international footprint extends from performances in the USA with Diplo to collaborations with acts like Elliphant, Coolio, Rae Sremmurd.  The next step on Talal Qureshi's trailblazing journey leads to his 2023 debut album "TURBO." With an innovative, futuristic blend of tradition and modernity, he cements himself as a sonic pioneer, etching sounds that resonate across time and culture.

name: FLYIN
bio: Introducing FLYIN aka Karl Flykt, a musical virtuoso, whose journey into the world of music began at an early age, captivated by the allure of instruments. From the tender age of a kid, FLYIN wielded the guitar with an innate passion that would become the cornerstone of his artistic expression.  Born and raised in a world of melody, he honed his musical prowess within the walls of a music-oriented high school, where his journey into composition and production took flight in his late teens. Despite initially exploring the realms of rock and metal during his formative years, FLYIN underwent a transformative musical evolution that saw him seamlessly transition into the vibrant and dynamic world of pop music.  A mere year after bidding farewell to high school, FLYIN made the decision to elevate his musical pursuits beyond the realm of a mere hobby. With an unwavering commitment to his craft, he delved deeper into the art of songwriting and production, weaving together a rich tapestry of pop melodies infused with funk rhythms and soulful influences. His journey is a symphony of passion, dedication, and the relentless pursuit of musical innovation, inviting audiences to join him on a melodic odyssey that transcends genre and resonates with the heart and soul of every listener.

name: Cushy
bio: Cushy is the alias of Seamus McNamara, a producer working out of the Bay Area. His tracks are built on hard-hitting percussion and melodies that lodge themselves on first listen - trap and electronic production with enough pop instinct to carry a real hook. The songwriting is what makes them stick: these are beats with structure, not just impact. That combination has carried the catalogue a long way, with more than 97 million streams across different streaming platforms and tens of billions of views on YouTube and TikTok, where creators have used the music in over 687,000 videos.

Niclas Gustavsson grew up in Gothenburg on the club records of Tiesto and Armin van Buuren, then taught himself to produce on midi controllers, trusting his own melodic instinct from the start. He still lives in Gothenburg, with a wife and two young children he calls the most honest critics of his music, and he spends his days building houses and his nights masterminding house tracks. The catalogue has passed 117 million streams across different streaming platforms and 9.2 billion track views on YouTube.

Auxjack’s holistic style of lofi draws both on his upbringing playing in pop-punk and emo bands as a teenager and on his thousands of hours sitting in the engineer’s chair; he earned a Grammy nomination for his work as a vocal and horns engineer on J Cole’s album “2014 Forest Hills Drive," and he works closely with acts like New Jersey indie pop artist, joe p, and Boston rapper, Sammy Adams.

name: Travis Scott
bio: Houston-born rapper and producer Travis Scott's psychedelic trap style makes him one of the more distinctive talents to have risen to the height of mainstream commercial popularity. His heavily processed, half-sung/half-rapped style set him apart early on, and he grew from affiliations with Kanye West's GOOD Music and T.I.'s Grand Hustle in the early 2010s to chart-dominating popularity before the close of the decade. After his first studio album, 2015's Rodeo, debuted in the number three position, Scott followed with a pair of number one full-lengths, Birds in the Trap Sing McKnight (2016) and Astroworld (2018), all the while assisting on platinum singles headlined by the likes of Rihanna ("Bitch Better Have My Money"), SZA ("Love Galore"), and Drake ("Portland"), and working extensively with Quavo as Huncho Jack. He also launched his own Cactus Jack Records, topping the Billboard 200 with the 2019 label compilation JackBoys. Whether leading or supporting, Scott's presence was unmistakable, and he quickly accumulated Grammys, endorsement deals, and appearances on more than 80 charting songs. By the 2020s, Scott was one of the most successful living artists on the planet. This level of fame played into both extreme success and profound tragedy, with Scott being at the center of controversy surrounding the deaths and injuries of hundreds of fans at his 2021 Astroworld Festival before he released his genre-crossing, Grammy-nominated fourth album, 2023's UTOPIA. He was then featured on a variety of tracks with 21 Savage, Metro Boomin, Asake, and others, before topping the Billboard 200 with his second label compilation, JackBoys 2. Born Jacques Webster, Travis Scott grew up in a suburb of Houston and began making music as a teenager. He formed a duo called the Graduates with Chris Holloway, and they released an EP in 2009. The following year, he formed another duo, the Classmates, with OG Chess. Scott produced the pair's two full-lengths, Buddy Rich and Cruis'n USA, but they broke up near the end of 2011. After dropping out of college, Scott moved to Los Angeles and began recording music on his own. He met T.I. and eventually Kanye West. Scott was hired as an in-house producer for GOOD Music, and appeared on the label's Cruel Summer compilation in 2012. Scott's debut, Owl Pharaoh, was originally scheduled to be released as a free mixtape in 2012, but as his profile grew (including a placement in XXL Magazine's Freshman Class of 2013), and sample clearance issues, the album wasn't released until May 2013. Featuring guest appearances by T.I. and 2 Chainz (on the single "Upper Echelon") as well as Toro y Moi and Justin Vernon of Bon Iver, Owl Pharaoh eventually garnered a nomination for Best Mixtape at the 2013 BET Hip Hop Awards. The buildup to Scott's first proper studio album involved the Days Before Rodeo mixtape, promoted with the singles "Don't Play" and "Mamacita," and the March 2015 U.S. Rodeo Tour, headlined by Scott and supported by Young Thug and Metro Boomin. Several of the dates sold out. The same month, Rihanna's Scott-produced hit single "Bitch Better Have My Money" was released. "3500" and "Antidote" were issued ahead of Rodeo, Scott's second full-length, which followed in September on Grand Hustle/Epic and debuted at number three on the Billboard 200. Toward the end of the year, "Antidote" peaked at number 16 on the Hot 100 and became Scott's first platinum single. Chatter regarding a follow-up, along with numerous delays, ensued throughout much of 2016. Meanwhile, Scott extended his commercial presence with featured spots on Wiz Khalifa's "Bake Sale," Rihanna's "Woo," and Kanye West's "FML," as well as a collaboration with Young Thug and Quavo, "Pick Up the Phone," a mid-year hit issued as the lead single of Young Thug's JEFFERY. Three months later, after "Bitch Better Have My Money" earned platinum certification, Scott's second proper album arrived. Titled Birds in the Trap Sing McKnight after one of Quavo's lines in "Pick Up the Phone," the woozy, mostly midtempo set featured that hit and contributions from the likes of André 3000, Kid Cudi, and Kendrick Lamar. It went straight to the top of the Billboard 200. Leading up to his third LP, Scott was featured on a slew of tracks, including platinum singles headlined by SZA ("Love Galore"), Drake ("Portland"), Miguel ("Sky Walker"), 2 Chainz ("4 AM"), and Trippie Redd ("Dark Knight Dummo"). Scott's own "Butterfly Effect" arrived during this torrent of hits in May 2017 and promptly went platinum as well. Seven months later, Huncho Jack, Jack Huncho, a collaborative full-length with Quavo, entered the Billboard 200 at number three. The following May, Scott released "Watch," a non-album track featuring Kanye West and Lil Uzi Vert, and within three months released Astroworld, which he considered the true follow-up to Rodeo. Featuring "Butterfly Effect," the album -- named after a demolished Houston amusement park -- debuted at number one and was supported with a second single, "Sicko Mode." Scott closed out 2018 by appearing on multiple tracks of Metro Boomin's Not All Heroes Wear Capes album. After collaborating with Young Thug and J. Cole on 2019's "The London" and being featured on Ed Sheeran's "Antisocial," Scott issued his own solo single, "Highest in the Room." JackBoys, a brief compilation showcasing artists from Scott's Cactus Jack Records label, appeared at the end of the year. The release subsequently became the first number one album of the 2020s. Another Young Thug collaboration, "Franchise," also featuring M.I.A., debuted in September 2020 on top of the Billboard 200. In January 2021, Spanish DJ HVME released a deep house reworking of Scott and Kendrick Lamar's song "Goosebumps," eventually topping Billboard's Hot Dance/Electronic Songs Chart. Two more tracks appeared that November, with both "Escape Plan" and "Mafia" arriving concurrently and hitting the Top Ten of Billboard's Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart. On November 5, 2021, there was a fatal crowd crush during Scott's performance at his third annual Astroworld Festival in Houston, Texas. The event resulted in the death of 10 people with over 300 being treated for injuries. The rapper apologized and the rest of the festival was canceled. Scott and others involved in the festival were investigated, though a Texas grand jury ultimately declined to indict them. In May 2022, Scott performed at the Billboard Music Awards, his first live appearance since the Astroworld Festival tragedy. He also contributed to four tracks on Metro Boomin's Heroes & Villains album. In July 2023, he released his fourth studio album, UTOPIA. An ambitious, genre-crossing concept album in the vein of Kanye West's Yeezus, it featured a bevy of producers, including Scott, James Blake, WondaGurl, and others. Also featured were many guests, such as Bad Bunny and the Weeknd on the lead single, "K-pop," and Beyoncé and Bon Iver on "Delresto (Echoes)." UTOPIA topped both the Billboard 200 and R&B/Hip-Hop Albums charts and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Rap Album. Scott's work throughout much of 2024 largely consisted of features on records by 21 Savage, Future and Metro Boomin, Mustard, and Asake. A Cactus Jack Records sequel compilation, JackBoys 2, arrived in July 2025, featuring appearances by Don Toliver, Playboi Carti, Future, GloRilla, and others. It topped both the Billboard 200 and the rap/hip-hop albums charts. In 2026, he contributed the track "Rhyno" to the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album soundtrack. ~ Paul Simpson & Andy Kellman, Rovi

Since making his mark he has only gone from strength to strength with his first official project ‘Double Tap Diaries’ peaking at #11 in the UK charts and its lead single ‘No Diet’ a now renowned drill classic gaining a top #20. name: Morrisson
bio: Morrisson is a British rapper & songwriter from East London.   Born in Newham, he is one of four brothers raised on the William Morley estate, hailing from a traditional family brought up in a true multi cultural hub. Due to his environment, Morrisson experienced a few brushes with the law in his early years.   Morrisson began his road to music in 2008 with a tape called “Currently Getting Currency” - this was was cut short due to his incarceration. Reappearing in 2011 with select freestyles on SBTV, Link Up TV and GRM Daily that generated millions of views, he again disappeared from the scene. Despite his absence his name continued to always carry weight in the UK. He dipped in and out of the music scene during the 2010s but then towards the end of the decade and going into 2020, he really started to take his career seriously, taking a more commercial route for his music. He has collaborated with artists such as Aitch, Tion Wayne, Tom Zanetti, Steel Banglez, Bugzy Malone and more. Accumulating over 55 million views on his YouTube channel and over 80 million global streams on Spotify alone. Morrisson has 3 UK Top 75s and has spent 6 weeks in the official charts. Going into 2024 Morrisson has big plans to release more consistently and cement his name in the current greats of UK Rap.

name: 163Margs
bio: 163Margs is carving out a distinctive lane in UK music, combining sharp lyricism, melodic instinct and an uncompromising creative vision. With every release, he continues to blur the boundaries between genres, delivering music that is as reflective as it is impactful. As his catalogue and audience continue to grow, 163Margs is establishing himself as a defining voice of a new generation, proving that his story has always been more than rhyme.

name: JAE5
bio: The summer-heralding sound of afroswing has warmed up the past half decade worth of shoobz in the UK and beyond, via melodic tracks like Dave and Burna Boy’s “Location”, J Hus’ anthemic “Did You See” and NSG's sleek club tune “Options”. The man behind those tracks is British Ghanaian producer JAE5 – the scene’s genre-shifting pioneer.  His unique blend of rap production, layered minimalism and afro-beat instrumentation has won him mainstream awards (Best Producer – MOBOs 2020), nominations (Best Contemporary Song – Ivor Novello 2020; plus multiple BRIT and Mercury nods) and platinum records along the way.   With his partner in crime J Hus – who he has a classic producer-artist relationship with in the vein of Dre and Snoop or Timbaland and Missy – JAE5 helped open the door for heritage-embracing British African artists. Now, with two Hus albums in the bag, he’s about to go solo, featuring a room full of dial switching acts – leading with debut single “Dimension”, featuring UK rap heavyweight Skepta and afropop hotshot Rema.   Having galvanized artists across several continents with his afrobeat tinged sound, there’s plenty more music en route. Think – big superstars and homegrown acts, combined in the JAE5 way, with his melodics, his smoothness. He’s released some of the biggest songs in modern British history. With all the accolades under his belt, it’s now his turn to lead. Get the BBQs out and the drinks poured – summer is coming again and JAE5 is ready.

name: Marnz Malone
bio: Rapper Marnz Malone is one of the hottest prospects in music . Born and raised in Spanish Town Jamaica, he moved to England around the age of 6 years old, more specifically Birmingham Newtown.  His Jamaican roots influenced his music heavily and he was constantly surrounded by music “Vybz Kartel & Movado's clash at Sting was probably the first time I realised the impact of music because the whole gaza vs gully thing was massive where I’m from.” Moving to Newtown in Birmingham, the rap scene there begun to influence him, and this is where he realised the power of music.  His love and enjoyment for music and the emotions it makes you feel made Marnz Malone take that step further and begin recording his own tracks, realising it could change his life and the lives of those around him.  Releasing a steady number of projects with his debut Trenchfoot in 2022, Maktub in August 2023 and Tina’s Boy at the beginning of 2024, all representing different times and feeling throughout his journey, allowing him to say things he struggles to say.   Drawing from personal experiences and struggles, Marnz Malone creates an emotive, raw, vulnerable and honest sound that connects to his listeners on a profound level and captures them.  His story, music and artistry has been building with accolades as a huge ‘one to watch’ artist from the likes of Complex, Mixtape Madness, Clash Magazine and many more.

name: J Hus
bio: Bouff Daddy. Juju J, Hustler, Hitman Likman. Lead Militarian of the Jamba Boys. The Fisherman, The Farda. He goes by many names, but there is only one J Hus.    A true homegrown star with global appeal – the man born Momodou Jallow rocketed from SB:TV to GQ cover star, east London to the O2 Arena, with the mega success of 2017’s Mercury, BRIT and MOBO Award nominated debut album Common Sense. Delivered with Hus’ inimitable charisma, the album’s eclectic voyage into the world of dancehall, rap, afrobeat and grime inaugurated the then 21 year-old as the voice of young black Britain.     Common Sense went Top 10 on release, while Hus’ recent 2019 collaborations with Skepta, Stormzy and Dave kept his presence hot and his seat warm at the table of UK music’s upper echelon. Having inspired a generation of diaspora teens to “Lean & Bop”, cementing a new wave of festival bookings, Hus is the prescient top boy of the charts, the dance and the streets. So what next?   Big Conspiracy, released Friday 24 January, 2020, is the next chapter.   After a well-documented fall from grace that included a stint in prison in early 2019, Hus studied up, became grown. The cheeky east Londoner introduced on songs like “Friendly” matured. As he elaborated to Wonderland in their 2019 cover story, "you’re gonna hear a more grown up Hus” on Big Conspiracy. “You’re gonna hear music with more meaning.”    Common Sense was Hus’ introduction, defining a sound – Big Conspiracy defines the mission.

name: Skillibeng
bio: Becoming a major player in dancehall with his debut single "Brik Pan Brik," Jamaican musician Skillibeng built an international audience in the early 2020s with his trap-focused approach to the genre. "Crocodile Teeth," from his 2021 album of the same name, became a breakout hit and he continued to impress with 2024's "Jump" featuring Tyla and Gunna, as well as collaborations with a range of artists including Popcaan, Mura Masa, WizKid, and more. In 2025, Skillibeng released his third solo album, International. Born Emwah Warmington in St. Thomas, Jamaica, Skillibeng first started making music in high school before beginning his solo career while working at his father's company. A near-death encounter convinced the vocalist to commit to music full-time: Early tracks released in 2015 and 2016, "Skilli She Love" and "Bruk Up Party," took an electronically led approach to the genre. But it was the 2019 hit "Brick Pan Brick" that would prove the artist's breakout moment. Encouraging hustling with its money-centric verses, the multi-million-streamed track found immediate success in Warmington's home country. From there, Skillibeng had a relentless release schedule, dropping 43 singles in 2020 along with his debut album The Prodigy. Among the highlights were his second major hit, "Mr. Universe," the Quenga collaboration "Not," and his third smash hit, "Crocodile Teeth," which got a remix by Nicki Minaj. In 2021, Skillibeng continued the rapid release pattern with 38 more singles, second album The Prodigy: Ladies Only, and third album Crocodile Teeth LP. As well as hits like "Coke" and the "Crocodile Teeth [Remix]," the artist took promising new directions alongside collaborators including Sleepy Hallow ("2 Sauce [Remix]"), Unknown T ("Wollan"), and Popcaan/Rich the Kid ("Rocket Launcher.") Over the next few years, Skillibeng bolstered his reputation with highlights like 2022's gritty "Whap What" with F.S., 2023's trap-inspired "16CHOPPA" featuring Nardo Wick, and 2024's hit Tyla and Gunna collaboration "Jump." These helped build anticipation for his next full-length, International, which arrived in 2025 and featured a guest list of stars like Ty Dolla $ign, Young Nudy, and Major Lazer. That same year he and Shenseea took part in a popular remix of Moliy and Silent Addy's hit "Shake It to the Max." ~ David Crone

name: Nines
bio: Nines first shot to notoriety with 2012 mixtape Church Road To Hollywood, a fiery, compelling body of work that spawned a string of street anthems, seeing Nines play out his role as North West London’s Robin Hood – a rapper intent on giving back to his local community. The release was later followed by the 2013 mixtape Gone Till November which earnt him the People’s Choice Award at the 2013 BBC 1Xtra Mixtape Awards. Sequentially came the 2014 release Loyal To The Soil and One Foot In the following year, which saw him nominated for Best Hip Hop Act at the 2015 MOBO Awards.  A pioneering and differentiated young polymath, few artists are able to retain the artistic vision and credibility that Nines has spent the last 10 years uncompromisingly building. In 2017, Nines released his debut album One Foot Out which thrust him into the limelight as a raw, honest and richly inventive artist like no other, this was followed by his 2018 sophomore offering Crop Circle -which debuted at number 4 in the UK album chart and went on to be the biggest selling UK rap album of 2018- the album featured lead single I See You Shining, the track is currently sat at over 20M YouTube views and has recorded over 300,000 sales. Continuing to solidify his reputation as a singular British creative force like no other, in 2020 he released his most recent album Crabs In A Bucket (which is now certified Gold) securing his first number 1 album and 3rd consecutive album in the UK Top 5.

name: Skrapz
bio: North-West London rapper Skrapz has 2 distinct sides to his music: one that focuses on harder, road rap & the other is melodic & calm. Skrapz has become known for music which reflects his life & the patchwork of his experiences. Early in his career, Skrapz was a part of garage & grime rap group SLK. Now, he is most known for his close association with long term friend & rapper Nines the two are part of the same collective entitled Ice City Boyz. 2010 saw the release of Skrapz's debut album, Skrapz Is Back, followed by 2013’s Shutdown Season. Toward the end of a short sentence, Skrapz was granted day releases, which he used to record his sophomore album, 2014's Skrapz Is Back 2. Later the same year, he released the 80's Baby mixtape, showcasing his calmer, melodic side for the first time. The following year he released his first album, 2015's The End of the Beginning, which combined both his darker & lighter styles. Most notably, this project included track ‘They Ain’t Ready’ which was later used by six time heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua for his ring walk against Wladimir Klitschko. The year 2017 saw the release of his second full-length album, 2017's Different Cloth, which featured guest appearances from the hottest in the UK. After a 4 year break, Skrapz returned to gift his fans with 2021 project ‘Be Right Back’. 2023 is set to be an pivotal year for the rapper, with a new project on the horizon & lots more to come - Skrapz is back & he’s better than ever.

name: Chy Cartier
bio: Hailing from North London, Chy Cartier represents the best and brightest of today’s emerging UK talent. Using her North London upbringing as a catalyst for her art, Chy is a vivid storyteller who is redefining what it means to be a young female artist in the male-dominated field of British rap.  At just 21, her razor-sharp rhymes speak for themselves. Despite her young age, Chy has already received a host of credible co-signs – Stormzy, DJ Semtex, Youngs Teflon, Wretch 32, Digga D and Potter Payper are all early champions and big fans of her sound.  Chy’s lyrics are filled with conviction, and through her tracks she offers an unselfconscious, first-hand take on what it is like growing up in austerity Britain. Her words provide an eloquent commentary on the social issues, disparities and injustices one can face when growing up in an inner-city environment – all delivered with an easy air of quick wit and relatability.  Of dual Sierra Leonean and Jamaican heritage, the music played at home when Chy was growing up heavily influenced her subsequent journey as an artist. With early exposure to R&B, Dancehall, Hip Hop, Reggae, UK Garage and House, the shift between listening to creating music came naturally. Almost as soon as she could talk, Chy was rapping – memorising Lil Kim, Nicki Minaj, Vybz Kartel and Mavado lyrics and counting bars until she was old enough to write her own.

name: D-Block Europe
bio: Essential collection of tracks from D-Block Europe. Platinum-selling collective D-Block Europe announced their 3rd album ‘Rolling Stone’ for January 12th 2024 with new single ‘I Need It Now’ on 30th November 2023, alongside the announcement of more historic nights at the O2 Arena, London. To date they’ve achieved a staggering 10+ Gold & 6 Platinum singles, 6 Gold mixtapes, over 5 billions global streams, and 30 x top 40 singles, including a #2 single with ‘Prada’ featuring Raye and produced by Casso. Meanwhile their cult classics ‘Overseas’, ‘Darling’ and ‘Make You Smile’ have transferred them from their home in Lewisham to worldwide reputation, outlined by features from the likes of Offset, Ed Sheeran, Central Cee and more.

name: French Montana
bio: Moroccan-American rapper French Montana is one of the world's most successful African-born artists, with several platinum certifications and collaborations with numerous major hip-hop figures. He rose from the New York mixtape underground in the 2000s and built an indie empire with his Cocaine City imprint, then emerged as a pop-savvy hip-hop act in the 2010s. Starting with his 2013 debut album, Excuse My French, he became known for his high-profile collaborations and a handful of chart hits including the diamond-certified "Unforgettable" from his 2017 sophomore LP, Jungle Rules. 2019's double album Montana was another showcase for big-name guests that featured the hit singles "No Stylist" and "Writing on the Wall." He retained his tried-and-true formula in 2021 for another guest-heavy effort, They Got Amnesia, before collaborating with Harry Fraud on 2022's Montega and DJ Drama on 2023's Coke Boys 6. Continuing another mixtape series, Mac & Cheese 5 arrived in 2024, followed by singles like "One More Chance, and the 2026 Max B collabs Coke Wave 3.5: Narcos and Wave Gods 2: Cosmos Brothers. Born Karim Kharbouch in Morocco, he immigrated to the U.S. while in his teens. He set up shop in the Bronx and began releasing his Cocaine City series of DVDs in 2002, mixing interviews with established hip-hop artists and unsigned talent. In 2009 he began releasing his own mixtape CDs with DJs like Evil Empire, DJ Drama, and Big Mike as his hosts. That same year, he would be signed to Akon's Konvict Musik label, but in late 2011 it was announced that they had parted ways and that Montana was signing to both P. Diddy's Bad Boy and Rick Ross' Maybach Music imprints in a unique joint venture. His 2012 single "Pop That" would be the first release for the united labels, while 2013 saw the arrival of his debut album, Excuse My French. A series of mixtapes, each with an increasing R&B influence, brought Montana to 2016, when he released Casino Life 2: Brown Bag Legend. The mixtape included the hit single "Moses" featuring Chris Brown and Migos. A full LP -- MC4 -- was slated for the end of the year, but after the album was leaked by a retailer months before its official release, Montana scrapped the rollout entirely and issued it as a mixtape. MC4 (aka "Mac & Cheese 4") featured appearances by the Weeknd, Drake, Jeezy, A$AP Rocky, Kodak Black, Miguel, Nas, Kanye West, DJ Khaled, Beanie Sigel, Jadakiss, Styles P, the Alchemist, Max B, and Chinx. The following year, Montana returned with his official sophomore effort, Jungle Rules. The record included guests like the Weeknd, Travis Scott, Pharrell Williams, Quavo, Future, T.I., and Young Thug. Lead single "Unforgettable" with Swae Lee became a hit, topping the Billboard rap chart and climbing into the Top Three of the R&B and main singles list. The album itself, certified gold in the U.S., debuted at number three on the Billboard 200. In 2018, Montana joined Diplo, Lil Pump, and Zhavia Ward for the bombastic single "Welcome to the Party" from the Deadpool 2 soundtrack, which returned him to the Hot 100. Additional singles "No Stylist" with Drake and "Slide" with Blueface and Lil Tjay were also chart hits, carrying Montana into 2019. Those latter tracks landed on his third effort, which was issued toward the end of the year on the same day he was released from hospitalization in the ICU. A double album, Montana, boasted an impressive cast of guests, including Juicy J ("50's & 100's"), Swae Lee (on the "Unforgettable" sequel "Out of Your Mind"), and Post Malone and Cardi B ("Writing on the Wall"). Upon release, the LP debuted at number 25 on the Billboard 200. The next year, he returned to his mixtape roots with Coke Boys 5. 2021 saw the release of Montana's fourth full-length, They Got Amnesia, which featured guests such as John Legend, Rick Ross, Ty Dolla $ign, Doja Cat, and many more. In 2022, Montana teamed up with Harry Fraud on the joint project Montega, which included the singles "Drive By," "Blue Chills," and "Brick & Bags." Coke Boys 6, with DJ Drama, appeared in 2023 and reached the Top 20 of the Billboard 200. Mac & Cheese 5, another installment in a mixtape series running since 2009, was released in 2024. The ambitious effort was issued in a comprehensive "Versions" edition including sped-up, slowed-down, a cappella, and instrumental versions of every song. Montana continued issuing singles and collaborations, including "Skyami" (with Skilla Baby), "To the Moon" (with Fivio Foreign and Fabolous), and "One More Chance." Both "Outta Here"(with Trippie Redd) and "Nissan" (with MC Tyson) appeared in 2025. Two collaborations with Max B, Coke Wave 3.5: Narcos and Wave Gods 2: Cosmos Brothers, both arrived in 2026. That year Montana also teamed up with British duo, D-Block Europe WORLDWIDE WAVE. ~ David Jeffries, Rovi
