name: Becky G
bio: Singer, songwriter, actress and activist Becky G was born for the spotlight and her multifaceted career is shaping up to be nothing short of iconic. The 24-year-old global superstar’s achievements include two number one hits on the Billboard Latin Airplay Charts (“Mayores” & "Sin Pijama”), a starring role in "Power Rangers," and guest-starring in Fox TV’s Emmy-winning “Empire" series.  She has toured alongside Katy Perry, Demi Lovato, J Balvin, and Fifth Harmony and has recorded collabs with Daddy Yankee, Maluma, Anitta, Natti Natasha, ZAYN, Bad Bunny, Ozuna & Pitbull among others.  Becky accepted the Agent of Change award at the 2020 Premios Juventud for her activism & using her platform to inspire positive change. She has also been honored by the Latin Recording Academy as one of the Leading Ladies in Entertainment (2018) and has been recognized as one of Rolling Stone’s “18 Teens Shaking Up Pop Culture” and one of Billboard’s “21 Under 21”.  She hosted & produced her “En La Sala" podcast - live from her living room during the lockdown. With every episode, Becky donated $10K to a charity of her choice, and spoke to high-profile guests from Vice President-elect Kamala Harris about politics to reggaetón star J Balvin about mental health.  Becky recently launched her very own beauty brand. Treslúce Beauty creates, celebrates and supports Latinx heritage and culture, with high-performance, conscious, vegan-friendly formulations that deliver high impact artistry.

name: Los Tigres Del Norte
bio: Los Tigres del Norte are an internationally successful norteño group from Mexico based in California. Since the late 1960s, this family band has detailed the struggles and triumphs, romances, and heartbreaks of working people, families, immigrants, outlaws, politicians, and farmers. Over more than 70 albums -- including 22 number ones -- they turned norteño, an accordion-based polka music indigenous to Northern Mexico, into commercially viable pop music, infusing the tradition with boleros, cumbias, rock rhythms, waltzes, and sound effects. Their 1974 breakthrough single, "Contrabando y Traición," about a drug deal and love story gone bad, sold on both sides of the border, establishing them in the U.S. 1984's Jaula de Oro was their first chart-topper. The following year's A Ti Madrecita marked their first million-seller. 1989's Corridos Prohibidos kicked off the modern narcocorrido movement, paving the way for the 21st century's alterna-movimiento. 2011's MTV Unplugged is among the series' most successful volumes, and 2014's number one Realidades discussed the harsh realities of immigrants. In 2019, Los Tigres del Norte were the first musical act since Johnny Cash to film a concert at Folsom Prison. In 2021 they issued Y Su Palabra Es La Ley: Homenaje A Vicente Fernandez and followed it with La Reunion in 2022. The group is centered on lead vocalist and accordionist Jorge Hernández (the oldest of 11 children), who is joined in Los Tigres by his brothers Hernán (bass, vocals), Eduardo (accordion, saxophone, bass, vocals), and Luis (bajo sexto, vocals) -- he replaced older brother Raul Hernandez who'd left to pursue a solo career during the 1990s -- and cousin, Oscar Lara (drums). Their parents were campesinos, small farmers who worked the land with ox-drawn plows. The Hernandez family lived and worked in Rosa Morada, a tiny village located in the municipality of Mocorito in Sinaloa. Jorge still insists that the day his grandmother brought home a Philco radio changed the course of his family's lives. It was the only electronic device of its kind. Amid the region's hilly terrain it managed to pull in just one radio station -– a 150,000-watt powerhouse from Harlingen, Texas -- that played pure norteño music exclusively. Jorge heard the music of major norteño artists including Freddie Gómez, Los Donneños, and Los Dos Gilbertos, for the first time. The acts were already making money across the border, and were known only in the United States at the time. During festivals, locals would set up a Victrola with a bullhorn for a speaker. At these parties, the Hernandez brothers were introduced to other top norteño acts including Los Alegres de Terán, and national mariachi stars including Pedro Infante. Aside from commercial music, they picked up songs from the oral traditions older men in town taught them. They taught the boys the revolutionary-era corridos about bandits and rebels, horses and heroes. The youngsters memorized verse after verse about historic and folkloric figures including Pancho Villa and learned to play as a band. These songs truly inspired Jorge, who desperately wanted to become a professional singer and songwriter. In 1966, their father, D. Eduardo Hernández, suffered a tragic accident causing a serious back injury that left him unable to walk. The youngsters, still young teens, started playing local gigs at night to earn money for their father's medical bills. Pressed by financial necessity to earn even more, they moved to the border town of Mexicali and worked its bar and restaurant circuit quite successfully. They eventually hired a manager and bought a van so they could work all across town from noon to dawn. In Mexicali they caught the break that would change their lives -- and ultimately, norteño music. One day, a telegraph worker Jorge knew form sending money home, told him that a promoter in San Jose, California, had put the word out that State officials were looking for Spanish-language acts to entertain Mexican inmates at Soledad prison. The gig didn't pay, but it provided exposure. With a 90-day visa, they could look for additional gigs in the U.S. After an audition, the Hernández brothers were hired as part of a revue brought in for the prison show. While filling out their visas and working papers, a U.S. immigration agent asked what the group's name was, but they didn't have one. The border officers affectionately referred to boys who exhibited a "go-get-em" attitude as “little tigers.” Since they were headed north, the agent dubbed them the "Little Tigers of the North," then eliminated the diminutive so they wouldn’t outgrow the name and Los Tigres del Norte were born. After the Soledad performance they got stranded in San Jose, but it proved a fateful break. They played clubs and cantinas, and even on radio station KOFY. They were discovered by Englishman, producer, and promoter Art Walker. Los Tigres del Norte became the first act signed to his Fama Records, which grew to become the leading Spanish-language record label on the West Coast. Walker, a local impresario, first heard the group on a live radio presentation recorded at the local Parque de las Flores on Keyes Street in San Jose and, impressed with what he heard, decided to make them Fama's core band. With his guidance, Los Tigres adopted an electric style, trading in their traditional acoustic sound for one incorporating bass, drums, and electric guitar. The group also adopted a modern approach to songwriting, emphasizing contemporary social themes common to Mexican-Americans. They cut the single "De un Rancho a Otro," and in 1968 issued their debut long-player, Juana La Traicionera/Por el Amor a Mis Hijo. While it got local airplay in San Jose, and in Sinaloa, it didn't sell many copies. Neither did 1969's Sufro Porque Te Quiero/La Cochicuina or 1970's Si Si Si: Chayo Chaires. That said, the continued wave of releases presented them with opportunities to tour. In late 1971, Jorge and Walker heard a corrido singer in Los Angeles play "Contrabando y Traición" about a drug-smuggling couple whose exploits end in betrayal and murder. It hit at radio and eventually charted in both the U.S. and Mexico, creating the modern narcocorrido subgenre. The followed with "La Banda del Carro Rojo," about a drug-smuggling gang in a red car. It too charted. Both songs became sizable hits in Southern California and in Mexico. They issued Contrabando y Traicion, their first charting album (and sixth overall) in 1974. Between 1976's Pueblo Querido and 1980's En La Plaza Garibaldi, they cut eight albums for Fama, but were paid for none of them. Los Tigres del Norte made their money playing live and by selling wholesale copies out of their van. While their recordings did reasonably well and kept concerts full, the band saw its profile grow exponentially when they appeared in the 1976 films La Banda Del Carro Rojo and La Muerte Del Soplon -- both were based on their corridos. The band sued Walker and won their freedom from Fama as well as the rights to their recordings. For several years they recorded for a variety of labels including EMI Pops, Profono Internacional, and Golondrina. Beginning with 1984's Jaula de Oro, the group would regularly score big on the Regional Mexican album chart stateside, and this success was acknowledged in 1987 when they won their first Grammy Award for Best Mexican-American Performance, for Gracias America...Sin Fronteras (1986) topping the Mexican Regional charts. They signed with Fonovisia in late 1987, and released their label debut, Ídolos Del Pueblo in 1988. They also appeared in three films based on their songs: La Puerta Negra (1986), La Jaula De Oro (1987), and Tres Veces Mojado (1989). 1988's Gracias! ... América ... Sin Fronteras topped the charts and spent more than 73 weeks on the charts; it earned Los Tigres del Norte their first Grammy award. In 1989 they issued two Grammy-nominated albums that reached the upper rungs of the charts, Mi Buena Suerte went to number three, while Los Corridos Prohibidos went to number one. Their first album with saxophonist brother Eduardo Hernandez, it marked the flowering of the narcocorrido movement. Despite an intense recording schedule, they never stopped touring or consciously building their fan base. Not only did they play across Mexico and North America, they made inroads to the rest of Latin America as well, consciously keeping ticket prices low. The next two decades saw Los Tigres del Norte tour for 1991's Para Adoloridos and Incansables -- both albums made the Top Five -- while 1993's La Garra De went Top 20. Tragedy was in the offing, however: Brother and percussionist Freddy Hernandez died after a heart attack suffered in a hotel room on tour. 1994's now historic Los Dos Plebes went to number two, largely based on its single "Muerte Anunciada," a legendary narcocorrido about the life and death about Colombian drug kingpin Pablo Escobar. 1995's El Ejemplo reached number two at Mexican Regional Albums but more change was in the air: Bajo sexto player Raul Hernandez announced his departure for a solo career after completing the support tour. He later revealed that part of the reason for leaving was feeling that tracks such as "Muerte Anunciada" and other narcocorridos glorified drug traffickers; none of the group's other members shared that opinion. Throughout the '90s, the band's fortunes multiplied. They were playing larger venues and touring abroad. They sold out concerts across Central and South America while playing football stadiums in Mexico and concert halls in the United States as the hits kept on coming. The appeared in four more films including Amor a la Medida, a romantic musical drama directed by Raúl Araiza. 1996's Unidos Para Siempre topped the Mexican Regional Albums chart. 1997's Jefe de Jefes followed it but also became their first entry in the Top 200. The album also topped the Latin Albums chart and earned a Grammy nomination. The following year's more romantic Asi Como Tu became their third straight number one at Mexican Regional Albums. Los Tigres del Norte closed the century with Herencia de Familia. It not only topped the Mexican Regional charts but fought its way into the top half of the Top 200. The band's popularity only grew in the 21st century. In 2000, De Paisano A Paisano became their fifth consecutive number one at Regional Mexican Albums; it also cracked the front half of the Top 200. 2001's Uniendo Fronteras reached the top spot on the Mexican Regional list. The title track of 2002's La Reina del Sur (Queen of the South) was based on Spanish author Arturo Perez-Reverte's novel about Teresa Mendoza, a Mexican woman who becomes a trafficker and emigrates to Spain where she becomes one of the most feared and respected gangsters of all time. The track met with great resistance from Mexican radio as the country's government censors pressured Latin radio stations in Mexico and the U.S. to refrain from playing it. Ultimately it made no difference. It topped Latin albums and Mexican Regional charts and went to number 54 on the Top 200. The single reached number nine on Hot Latin Songs. The full-length was nominated for a Grammy award. Further, both the song and the novel inspired the 2011 Netflix series of the same title, starring Kate del Castillo in the lead role. The group were honored with El Mas Grande Homenaje a Los Tigres del Norte (2001), a tribute album featuring many of the biggest names in Mexican music including Julieta Venegas and Molotov. Furthermore, beginning in 2003 Fonovisa began to compile a series of greatest-hits compilations titled Herencia Musical. The first, Herencia Musical: 20 Corridos Inolvidable, unsurprisingly, went to number one. 2004's Pacto de Sangre also reached the top spot on the Mexican Regional albums chart and the upper half of the Top 200; it was followed by the cumbia offering Cumbias Y Algo Mas.... that peaked at three. Throughout their long and storied career, Los Tigres maintained a respectable image, never glamorizing the drug trade nor any other criminal activity. They refused to be photographed with so much as a gun in sight. This air of respectability helped expand their audience demographically and internationally. During the new century's first decade, Los Tigres global concerts more often than not reflected the diversity of their fan base. Amid all of the touring and recording activity, they continued releasing albums on an annual basis and branched out into cinema as well, with DVD videos becoming a regular addition to their music releases. In 2006, Fonovisa reissued some of the band's films on DVD, including La Banda del Carro Rojo and La Muerte del Soplon -- with thematic compilations of Los Tigres favorites. That same year they issued the covers album Raices. It topped the Latin albums and Mexican Regional charts and went to number 68 on the Top 200. It also won the Grammy for Best Norteño Album. Two years later the band made the film La Misma Luna, a 2007 bilingual Mexican-American drama directed by Patricia Riggen about the plight of a mother and son after illegally entering El Norte. The band also took home another Grammy for the live audio/visual offering Tu Noche Con Los Tigres Del Norte. 2009's La Granga, offered a balance of songs about immigration, romance, and narcocorridos,. It topped the Mexican and Latin albums lists and went to number 45 on the Top 200. Certified multi-platinum, it became Los Tigres del Norte's highest-charting album. In 2011, Diego Torres, Zack de la Rocha, Andrés Calamaro, and others would assist the group in celebrating their long career on the spirited MTV Unplugged: Los Tigres del Norte and Friends. One of the best-selling volumes in the series, it topped various charts and won a Grammy for Best Banda or Norteño Album. After a four-year break from studio recording, Los Tigres del Norte issued the full-length Realidades in October of 2014. It was their 23rd album to reach the Top Ten on the Top Latin Albums chart, tying the record originally set by Los Temerarios. The album entered at number three. It won a Grammy for Best Regional Mexican Music Album (including Tejano) two years after its release. On November 13, 2015, the group released the single "Tu Carcel," written by Marc Antonio Solis (who appears on it), an artist Los Tigres consider the "poet of the century." It was followed three weeks later by the live album Desde al Azteca. In 2016, Los Tigres del Norte, like many musicians before them, submitted a request to perform at California's Folsom Prison. It took two years to get permission, but on the 50th anniversary of the norteño legends playing their very first show in the United States at Soledad prison, they received said permission to play Folsom. They played the show in mid-April 2019, marking the first time a major act performed at the prison since Johnny Cash took its stage nearly half-a-century before. Los Tigres made it special for the inmates, and even brought one of them on-stage to play accordion on their reading of the Cash classic, "Folsom Prison Blues." Both album and film were released in September 2019. The following year, Los Tigres del Norte released Y Su Palabra Es La Ley: Homenaje a Vicente Fernández, a 15-song tribute to the legendary mariachi and ranchera singer. They combined ranchera, mariachi, and corrido styles in reading 14 songs closely associated with the great vocalist, and added the unpublished corrido "Un Consentido de Dios," composed especially for him. Fernandez died the following year at age 81. Los Tigres del Norte released the six-track La Reunion EP digitally in 2021, followed by a deluxe edition that doubled its track length and received a physical release in May 2022. The band kept the momentum going with the singles "Pan Y Miel" and "She Is Wow," both of which appeared on the 2024 EP Aquí Mando Yo. More songs followed, including the streaming hits "Tus Últimas Palabras" and "Al Diablo Tu Ausencia" ahead of the release of the EP La Lotería in 2025. ~ Jason Birchmeier & Thom Jurek, Rovi

name: Midland
bio: Footloose and free, working hard and drinking harder, always riding into the sunset or sunrise, GRAMMY-nominated trio Midland makes country music feel viscerally alive and timeless, with songs for people to drink, swing, love and, yes, lose to. Name inspired by a Dwight Yoakam song, the Dripping Springs, Texas-born trio channels a distinctly 21st century post-modern traditionalism, recapturing a classic country essence through thick harmonies, steel guitars and a worn-in cool that has made their music a dive bar staple worldwide. Honed in barrooms, it’s a sound that’s been imitated but never duplicated since 5X PLATINUM, No. 1 “Drinkin' Problem.” For Mark Wystrach, Cameron Duddy and Jess Carson, music isn’t just something to play in your car. It envelopes their aesthetics, from the Nudie Cohen-inspired rhinestone suits, their Insolito Tequila and Kingsmaker cigar line to their album-focused musical explorations and lean, song-forward live presentation. From head-turning debut On The Rocks through the Billboard Top Country Album Let It Roll and into The Last Resort: Greetings From and Barely Blue, Midland has built a catalog that bridges conceptual ambition with roots-driven songwriting. Alongside “Drinkin' Problem,” their catalog also includes PLATINUM-certified “Burn Out” and GOLD-certified favorites “Cheatin’ Songs,” “Make A Little” and “On The Rocks.” The band's commitment to the sounds, stories and places that define country music persists in Stages, out now.

name: Frank Ray
bio: Blessed with a smooth country vocal, BBR Music Group/BMG Nashville artist Frank Ray is a long road singer-songwriter who built his career on medicinal-strength performances, making the world a slightly-happier place, one night at a time. But with a new understanding of his “duty,” the hit-making former police officer has gone back to his roots. Growing up amid the intense collision of cultures in border towns Laredo, Texas and Columbus, New Mexico, everything from Tracy Lawrence and Rascal Flatts to Tejano, Ranchera, and Norteño music formed his musical foundation, with service in his blood. Spending 10 years as a law enforcement officer in Las Cruces, New Mexico, Ray wrote tickets by day and worked honky tonks by night, until a battle of the bands scored him a gig opening for Keith Urban. A bright fusion of organic honky-tonk pop and smooth Latin twang led to two Texas radio #1s, while the R&B-inflected “Country’d Look Good on You” reached the Top 20 of Billboard’s Country Airplay chart in 2022. Ray’s good-time credentials were solidified on nationwide tours with Luke Combs, Kane Brown, Luke Bryan, and more, and he was hailed by TIME Magazine, Good Morning America, Rolling Stone, Country Radio Seminar, and beyond. A 2023 album debut played up his vibrant Tex-Mex flavor. But on the new EP, Good For The Soul, sunny honky-tonk tones from the ‘90s and 2000s combine with epic balladry and mood-boosting vocals, in a sonic prescription for the good life.

name: Joss Favela
bio: Two-time Latin GRAMMY nominated Regional Mexican artist and composer Joss Favela and his songs have reached great popular success among those who love Regional Mexican music. Artists like Julión Álvarez, Alejandro Fernández, Banda El Recodo and Gerardo Oritz, among many others, have recorded and performed his songs.  Joss Favela began writing when he was only 12 years-old and now counts with two 2016 Latin GRAMMY® nominations for Best New Artist and Best Norteño Album for his debut album “Hecho A Mano” leading him to compete with great artists like Intocable, Tigres del Norte, Pesado, among many others. In 2016, Joss Favela was also recognized by ASCAP as the Songwriter of the Year, making him the youngest songwriter in obtaining this award.   Joss Favela represents the very best of this new era of Regional Mexican music.<br>

name: Dustin Lynch
bio: Dustin Lynch has “built one of the most consistent recording careers in modern country music” (Billboard), earning 10 number ones, four Top 5 albums, 12 RIAA-certified singles and more than 5 BILLION global streams. His seventh studio album, Clean Slate, is out now via BBR Music Group/BMG Nashville. Across 12 tracks, Lynch explores love, heartbreak and second chances, blending his signature country sound with fresh influences. Highlights include “Made In A Bottle,” “How You Been” with Ashley Cooke, the title track and “Home To You” with MC4D. Lynch recently celebrated his chart-topping run with Setlist Staples - 10 #1's, alongside new RIAA certifications for “Small Town Boy” (5X PLATINUM), “Thinking ’Bout You” (4X PLATINUM), “Ridin’ Roads” (2X PLATINUM) and “Chevrolet (feat. Jelly Roll)” (PLATINUM). He has headlined packed venues and toured with Kane Brown, Luke Bryan, Brad Paisley and Blake Shelton. In 2025, he became Wynn Nightlife’s first country artist in residence, returning in 2026 and expanding his sound through genre-blending collaborations and his Club Set Remixes EP. Since his 2012 PLATINUM breakout “Cowboys and Angels,” the Tennessee native has joined the Grand Ole Opry and earned nominations from the ACM, American Music, Billboard Music, iHeartRadio Music and CMT Music Awards.

name: Adriel Favela
bio: El  cantante, compositor, productor y multi-intrumentista hoy hace mancuerna con la compañía más grande y representativa en el Género Regional Mexicano, Fonovisa Records sello que pertenece a la gran familia de Universal Music Latin Entertainment, logrando concretarse una ambiciosa y prometedora alianza en la que se impulsará la creatividad sin límite del joven nacido en San Francisco, California. Esta unión no solo es como artista sino se abre la puerta a un grupo de jóvenes que el mismo Adriel está produciendo bajo su propia marca Esperanto Music Group donde Favela escribe, produce y dirige a estos nuevos talentos.    “Me siento bendecido y agradecido por poderles mostrar fragmentos de mi vida de la forma más pura y honesta posible a través del lenguaje universal que es la música, estoy orgulloso del equipo que se está creando porque hay  talento, visión, paciencia e inteligencia para ese ajedrez musical”, afirma el joven cantante.   Hoy esta joven promesa impulsado por un corazón y una energía positiva, continúa escribiendo su historia y además se suma a impulsar los sueños de otros nuevos talentos convirtiendo a Esperanto Music Group, en una fábrica de éxitos y semillero de artistas.

name: Jay de la Cueva
bio: Jay de la Cueva  multinstrumentalista, cantante, productor y compositor mexicano , nominado al Grammy Latino por el disco «Malditos Pecadores» de Moderatto; así mismo ha logrado varias nominaciones a los premios MTV VMA, Billboard, Lo Nuestro, Premios Juventud, entre otros. Jay de la Cueva ha desempeñado un importante papel en el desarrollo de la industria musical mexicana. Es considerado uno de los músicos más prolíficos y el frontman con más presencia y fuerza de México.  Inicia su carrera a los 6 años tocando la batería como Baby Rock junto a su papá,  a los 9 años fue invitado a ser parte del grupo Microchips tocando el Bajo, en esa etapa aprendió a tocar otros instrumentos y obtuvo una disciplina que lo ha llevado a lograr el éxito.  En 1995, junto a Micky Huidobro y Tito Fuentes fundó una de las bandas más influyentes del rock mexicano: Molotov,  colaboró en la composición del disco «Donde Jugaran Las Niñas». En 1997 se integra como baterista de una de las bandas más importantes del país: Fobia, con la cual toca hasta la actualidad.    Desde 1999 hasta el día de hoy sigue siendo miembro de  Titán, con la que ha recorrido gran parte de los continentes Europeo y Americano. Desde el 2001 hasta el momento, bajo su álter ego  «Bryan Amadeus» ha sido líder fundador y guitarrista principal del grupo Moderatto, con el cual ha cosechando sus mayores éxitos; ventas multi-platino, extensas giras por todo México, Latinoamérica , Estados Unidos, España, Francia y Japón.

name: Javier Molina
bio: A native of Texas, Tejano singer Javier Molina first surfaced as a member of Hombres G; with backing group Eldorado, he made his solo debut in 1998 with Cowboy Cumbia, followed a year later by Mi Nena. ~ Jason Ankeny, Rovi

bio: 8 SEGUNDOS es hoy por hoy el Grupo de Música Country en Español mas importante de México y Latinoamerica

name: Kat & Alex
bio: For as much as Kat & Alex embody classic country stylings and values, the Nashville-based duo also rewrite the rules altogether with a Latin twist. The husband-and-wife pair shake up country with full-bodied soulful delivery, engaging live instrumentation, and bilingual lyrics, introducing themselves as Nashville’s most compelling outliers. Kat is a Miami native and first-generation American from a Cuban family. Alex, who is of Puerto Rican descent, grew up in Northwestern Georgia and moved to Miami by middle school. Their paths crossed after Kat witnessed Alex singing one day at their church, and the two quickly forged an eternal bond after meeting up to collaborate. They appeared on American Idol individually before returning home to focus on writing and recording original music as a duo, and then made their way to Nashville in 2020, igniting a life-altering couple of years. Kat & Alex released their debut single “How Many Times” and its accompanying Spanish version in the fall of 2020. The following year the couple tied the knot, made their Grand Ole Opry debut, and released several new tracks to critical acclaim including “Heartbreak Tour,” which The New York Times dubbed as “an earnest power country slow-burner.” The duo is set to make waves this year with their scorching signature style while resolutely representing Hispanic culture in country music with a sound that’s rich and soulful with velvet harmonies, pop-like vocal riffs, and hooky lyrics.

name: Squeezebox Bandits
bio: State Fair Records recording artists, playing Honkytonk Country w/ a Tex-Mex flavor. Winners of Best Texas Music for The FW Weekly Music Awards-2019 New album coming out May 5, 2022.

name: Camila Cabello
bio: Camila Cabello is a diamond-certified, GRAMMY®-nominated Cuban-born singer, songwriter, actress, and activist. She has notably emerged as the first Hispanic woman to reach RIAA Diamond status with her Billboard Hot 100 #1 smash “Havana” [feat. Young Thug]. She’s garnered dozens of awards, including two Latin GRAMMY® Awards, five American Music Awards, and a Billboard Music Award. In 2018, her full-length debut album, Camila, bowed at #1 on the Billboard Top 200 and eventually went platinum, receiving a GRAMMY® nomination for “Best Pop Vocal Album”, with “Havana (Live)” nominated for Best Pop Solo Performance. With the success of the triple-platinum single “Never Be The Same,” she made history again as “the first artist ever to land two multi-format number one singles with the first two singles from a debut album.” In  2019,she teamed up with Shawn Mendes for “Señorita,” scoring a GRAMMY® nomination for “Best Pop Duo/Group Performance”. Her sophomore full-length, Romance, ascended to platinum status and her third full-length album, Familia was nominated for a Grammy and has over 500 million streams, making her the first female artist since Adele to triple up atop Billboard’s Hot 100, Top 200, and Artist 100 charts.  Most recently, Camila released her critically acclaimed fourth studio album C,XOXO which represents an evolution for the singer-songwriter tapping into genres that extend beyond just pop and drawing inspiration from her Miami roots.

name: Teo & Diego
bio: Originarios de Monterrey, N.L.,los hermanos Teo y Diego, productores, compositores, y músicos, han superado toda expectativa desde que aparecieron a través de las redes sociales. Su estilo característico y propio, les ha permitido conquistar los corazones de todos sus seguidores que los apoyan día con día.  Arrancando su carrera de manera profesional, Teo y Diego nos presentan “Qué Loco”, primer sencillo promocional de su álbum debut “Sueños”. En esta melodía en la que a ritmo pop, logran lucir la potencia de su voz y la fuerza de su personalidad.  Es un placer anunciar que Teo y Diego son parte de la familia Latin Power Music, donde su creatividad y pasión por la música brillarán aún más.

name: Paul Wall
bio: An esteemed figure in Texas hip-hop, Paul Wall is known most for his equally affable and boastful rhymes delivered with a thick drawl best suited for the syrupy rhythms he favors. Also a DJ who fell under the spell of the pioneering DJ Screw, Wall came up with Houston's Swishahouse label, recording in tandem with Chamillionaire. Wall made local and regional moves before reaching a larger audience through Mike Jones' "Still Tippin'," a platinum hit that set him up for crossover solo success with The Peoples Champ (2005), a Billboard 200-topping release. Wall kept rolling with a featured role on Nelly's "Grillz" -- a number one pop hit nominated for a Grammy, it was good for Wall's custom mouthpiece business -- and Top Ten follow-up album Get Money, Stay True (2007). After a couple more albums with Swishahouse, Wall went independent and for the most part has stuck with street music tailored for leisurely drives and hedonistic parties. He has likewise remained prolific with a combination of over two dozen subsequent solo albums, duo albums, mixtapes, and EPs. Among Wall's frequent collaborators is Termanology, with whom he made Start 2 Finish (2022) and Start Finish Repeat (2023). Born Paul Slayton, Paul Wall grew up as a hardcore disciple of fellow Houstonian DJ Screw and became so familiar with the pioneering DJ's woozy, slowed-down style of remixing that he had to adjust to hearing hip-hop at any other tempo. Wall started rapping and DJ'ing in the late '90s. Before his nationwide breakthrough, he was involved with promotional street teams, spun records at parties, put together underground mixtapes, and was half of the Color Changin' Click with Chamillionaire. He recorded 2002's Get Ya Mind Correct with Chamillionaire and then followed that with the 2004 solo effort Chick Magnet, his first album. Later in 2004, Mike Jones released a version of "Still Tippin" -- featuring Wall and Slim Thug -- that would reach number 60 on the Billboard Hot 100 and eventually go platinum. During its ascent, Controversy Sells, another disc billed to Wall and Chamillionaire, hit the streets and set up the September 2005 release of Wall's Atlantic-distributed second album, The Peoples Champ. Appropriately titled, the album went to number one on the Billboard 200 and featured a pair of gold singles with "Sittin' Sideways" and the Top 40 crossover hit "Girl." It was around the same time that Wall was featured on another big single, Nelly's number one pop hit "Grillz," a track also nominated for a Grammy in the category of Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group. Get Money, Stay True, Wall's 2007 follow-up, became the rapper's second Top Ten album upon release that April. Similar to the debut in its uncomplicated approach, it included the charting singles "Break 'Em Off" (featuring Lil' Keke) and "I'm Throwed" (featuring Jermaine Dupri), along with "Drive Slow," which originally appeared on Kanye West's The College Dropout. Wall would release two more solo albums for Swishahouse. Fast Life appeared in May 2009 and entered the Billboard 200 at number 15. While it served up plenty of party tracks, it also revealed another side of Wall with the introspective "Daddy Wasn't Home." Just over a year later, Wall was back with the number 58 chart entry Heart of a Champion, half of which was produced by blink-182 drummer Travis Barker. Having set up Paul Wall Music, Wall eased into label independence in 2013 with #Checkseason, and over the next three years continued to churn out solo albums on an annual basis. The Po-Up Poet, a collaboration with producer June "The Jenius" James, was trailed by Slab God, boasting appearances from Snoop Dogg and Devin the Dude, and the Houston Oiler, including featured spots from well-known locals like Z-Ro, Slim Thug, and, naturally, Chamillionaire. The 2018 release Bounce Backs Over Setbacks was Wall's final studio album of the 2010s, a decade in which he also recorded co-billed projects with the likes of Baby Bash and Statik Selektah and further supplemented with a handful of additional mixtapes. The rapper entered the 2020s as a bona fide Houston hip-hop veteran and continued his prolific release rate. Mind Over Matter and Subculture, Wall's 11th and 12th solo studio albums, both landed in 2020, as did Slab Talk, co-billed to Lil' Keke. Solo album 13, Hall of Fame Hustler, was out the next year. In 2022, Wall teamed with Termanology for Start 2 Finish and with Bash for the third volume of their mixtape series The Legalizers. Wall linked again with Termanology for Start Finish Repeat, released in 2023. ~ Andy Kellman, Rovi

name: Jake Hoot
bio: Currently amassing over 10 million Apple Music and Spotify streams, nearly 100K downloads and celebrating his 10th Grand Ole Opry appearance, the future proves bright for this mega talent with a heart of gold who is known by his 6-year-old daughter simply as daddy.

name: Andrea Vasquez
bio: One of country music’s most promising new artists, Andrea Vasquez, blends modern country with her Mexican-American roots. Recognized as a top country artist in Nashville, Andrea’s undeniable stage presence and mainstream quality songs have earned her numerous accolades, including a Billboard feature, the coveted DISCovery Award from renowned music critic Robert K. Oermann of Music Row, and more. With video support from The Country Network and CMT, her “Moving Target” video climbed CMT Music’s 12 Pack Countdown, where she held a spot in the Top 5 for three consecutive weeks.   With continuous performances including appearances at CMA Music Festival, Andrea also performs on her Nashville Hits The Roof Tour as well as with Song Suffragettes in Nashville. With several singles and a full-length album already released, her music has surpassed half a million Spotify streams and features on top playlists like Country Latino and New Music Nashville. Inspired by Carrie Underwood, Shania Twain, and The Chicks, Andrea continues to work on new material and is trailblazing a path for future country artists who share her Latino heritage.

name: Ricky Duran
bio: Ricky Duran garnered international attention with his soulful vocals, fiery guitar playing and compelling performances on NBC’s The Voice. The Season 17 Runner-Up has since released a single charting at No. 1 on iTunes and sold out shows, showing himself to be more than a fleeting show success - he retained fans and amassed more. He is an irrefutable talent and electrifying entertainer making music for the soul. His vulnerable songwriting and ability to capture an audience on and off stage transcends trends, while his musical abilities and influences spanning genres shows his music knows no bounds - he is timeless and a genuine creative that no label can penetrate.   Booking inquiries: Rickyduranbooking@gmail.com

name: David Bisbal
bio: Ganador de 3 Grammy Latino, 3 Billboard Latinos, 3 World Music Award y 2 Premios Ondas, entre los más de 80  galardones nacionales e internacionales que acumula, David Bisbal es reconocido a ambos lados del Atlántico por su  carrera de más de 18 años en los cuales ha conseguido 11 Discos de Diamante por las ventas de sus discos, y vender  más de 5 millones de Tickets de sus más de 1000 conciertos en todo el mundo. David ha actuado en recintos tan míticos, como el Royal Albert Hall, el O2 Arena de Londres, el Carnegie Hall, el  Barclays Center de Nueva York, el Teatro Real de Madrid o el Olympia de Paris y ha colaborado con artistas de la talla  de Alejandro Sanz, Miley Cyrus, Rocio Jurado, Rihanna, Alejandro Fernández, Marco Antonio Solís, Sebastian Yatra,  Juanes, Juan Luis Guerra, Luis Fonsi, Raphael, Juan Gabriel, Plácido Domingo, TINI, Jamie Cullum, Idina Menzel… David Bisbal acumula más de 800 millones de streamings de todas sus canciones, entre las que encontramos sus  últimos éxitos ‘A partir de hoy’ con Sebastian Yatra, 'Perdón' con Greeicy y 'Bésame' con Juan Magán, además de la  recientemente publicada 'Abriré la Puerta' junto a Alejandro Fernandez. Con más de 2 Millones de subscriptores en su canal de Youtube, supera la cifra de 1.2 billones de vistas de sus videos. Además, David Bisbal es uno de los artistas españoles con más fans y seguidores en sus redes sociales, en las que alcanza los 20 millones.

name: Joan Sebastian
bio: Joan Sebastian was recognized by critics and colleagues for his contribution to Mexican culture, getting his lyrics performed by prominent Latin artists. After leaving a local seminary at the age of 17, the young man started to get involved in popular music, dedicating his first composition, called "Juliantla," to his native town. In 1977, José Manuel Figueroa, Sr. decided to call himself Joan Sebastian -- paying tribute to San Sebastian, where he used to work. He embarked on a successful career, having the opportunity to play a role in the Latin series Tú y Yo and receiving the title of King of Jaripeo. In 1999 the popular artist was diagnosed with bone cancer, but he didn't stop working. A year later, Secreto de Amor received awards for song and album of the year in the Regional/Mexican category. Joan Sebastian died in July 2015 at the age of 64. ~ Drago Bonacich, Rovi

name: Río Roma
bio: Formed by Tulancingo, Hidalgo-born siblings José Luis and Raúl Ortega Roma, both of whom found success on their own before joining forces, Latin Grammy-nominated Mexican pop duo Rio Roma released their debut album, Al Fin Te Encontré, in May 2011. Hoy Es un Buen Día followed in 2014. In December 2015, the pre-release single "Te Quiero Mucho Mucho" landed well inside the Latin Songs Top 40. The title track of their album Eres La Persona Correcta en el Momento Equivocado was released the next spring and placed at 16. The full-length, released in April, reached number 10 on the Latin Pop Albums chart. ~ James Christopher Monger, Rovi

name: DannyLux
bio: Since 2019, DannyLux has captivated global listeners with his "Alternative-Sierreño" sound, garnering over  million fans on social media. Born in California to Mexican immigrants, his musical journey started at age 7 with a discarded guitar from his father. Inspired by artists like Ariel Camacho and Eslabon Armado, he penned his first hit, "24:7," at 15, which went viral.   The artist kicked off 2023 with a groundbreaking debut at the Coachella Music Festival, , a hometown glory story told through a billboard which went viral and the bestowal of the keys to his hometown, Desert Hot Springs, by the city’s mayor. Simultaneously his work was recognized with nominations to Premio Lo Nuestro , Latin American Music Awards, and received his first BMI Latin Music Award for his song “Jugaste y Sufri” with Eslabon Amado. The young artist was listed for the 2nd consecutive year in Billboard’s 21 under 21 list and joined Variety’s Young Hollywood Report in 2023. DannyLux made history by being the first Musica Mexicana artist to perform on A Colors Show, and later made his debut on NPR’s Tiny Desk.   DannyLux is ascending as one of the most prominent figures in regional Mexican music. In every note, performance, and milestone, the artist continues to push the boundaries of not only Mexican Music but music in general with his innovative talent, leaving an indelible mark on the industry.

name: Carrie Underwood
bio: Carrie Underwood is a true multi-media superstar. She’s the highest RIAA certified female country artist of all time, with 8 albums certified Multi-Platinum or Platinum by the RIAA & over 95 million total RIAA certifications to date.  All 10 of her albums debuted in the Top 10 on the Billboard Top 200 chart for all genres. She’s won over 100 major awards including 8 GRAMMY®, 16 ACM, 25 CMT, and 7 CMA to name a few. A Grand Ole Opry member since 2008, she received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2018. She built a successful business for health & wellness and launched her new wellness brand HiNote in 2026.  She released herNYT Best Seller FIND YOUR PATH & also launched the fit52 fitness app, both in 2020, which evolved into HiNote Life - Powered by fit52. Her exclusive year-round SiriusXM channel, CARRIE’S COUNTRY began in 2023.  Her REFLECTION: The Las Vegas Residency played to packed houses through April 2025 & is the longest-running Las Vegas residency of any solo female country artist. She has starred in NBC’s Sunday Night Football for 14 consecutive seasons & will return for her 3rd season on the judges panel of American Idol.

name: Miranda Lambert
bio: Acclaimed groundbreaker/songwriter/superstar Miranda Lambert has defined her multi-faceted career as an artist, entertainer, entrepreneur, advocate and businesswoman with an unflinching quest for excellence, honesty and conviction. The most-awarded artist in Academy of Country Music history, including their top honor for Entertainer of the Year, her music has also won three Grammys and 14 Country Music Association Awards. A TIME100 honoree and perennial best of the year list maker at the New York Times, TIME, Rolling Stone, Billboard, Stereogum, People and more, NPR has called her “the most riveting country star of her generation.”  With seven No. 1 solo albums, 10 No. 1 hit radio singles, more than 80 prestigious awards and countless Gold, Platinum and multi-Platinum sales certifications, she’s conquered Las Vegas with her twice-extended Velvet Rodeo residency and blurred genres with Leon Bridges, Enrique Iglesias, the B-52s, Loretta Lynn, Sheryl Crow and Elle King as well as her LGBTQ+ inclusive anthem “Y’All Means All” for Netflix’s “Queer Eye.” She’s taken those standards to become a New York Times bestselling author, and the first and only woman on Lower Broadway with her Tex-Mex cantina Casa Rosa, while expanding her creative reach with her Wanda June Home collection, and her Idyllwind clothing. Driven by her passion for rescue animals, her MuttNation Foundation has raised more than $10 million since inception.

bio: Hi, I’m Ole-Bjørn.   Thanks for listening to my music!   I’m a composer/pianist/keyboardist/producer based in Oslo, Norway. name: J. Alke
bio: For over 15 years, J. Alke, aka Johan Alkenäs has been shaping his career as a songwriter and producer in Sweden. During this time, he has contributed to numerous TV and film projects and collaborated with an impressive array of artists, such as the Jonas Brothers, Miley Cyrus, Ry X, Purple Disco Machine, Enhypen, and Zendaya. Despite his diverse projects, J. Alke has always gravitated back to the piano, recently focusing more on composing original pieces.

name: Waqar Jachin
bio: My love for felted pianos stretches way back. By placing different fabrics and felt between the hammers and strings, the piano transforms into a completely new, ambient instrument. For me, every song is an experiment in texture and timbre—a search to give every composition its unique soul and character.

name: émil caron
bio: émil caron writes quiet piano pieces that linger like memories from his home in Saint-Raphaël. His style is calm, cinematic and full of warmth. His music captures the beauty of still moments, where emotion speaks softly.

name: Farsjön
bio: From the deep forests of Värmland, Sweden, Farsjön is the musical project of Rikard Löfgren. Capturing the melancholy of the Nordic spirit, the melodies are soothing and comforting. The songs are recorded using a variety of old upright pianos, sometimes combined with other instruments such as flugelhorn or ambient textures.

name: Blue George
bio: Blue George His piano speaks in soft confessions— a glance held too long, a love letter never sent.  Blue George composes with the heart wide open, each piece a whispered moment suspended in time. Melodies drift like candlelight on water— fragile, intimate, unforgettable

name: Ella Davies
bio: The countryside on a rainy day, by the fire with a cup of tea, dreaming about life — that is when I am in my element. A powerful urge to write, create, and feel takes hold of me. Sometimes it becomes words, sometimes a melody.

name: Rosenkalla
bio: Melodies for sleepless nights, quiet mornings, and wandering thoughts. With delicate and floating harmonies, the compositions feel like a quiet walk through foggy forests, distant memories and midnight skies. Rosenkalla finds the stillness between every raindrop and as each note echoes you drift past the sunset, beyond the stars and into the quiet night.

name: Sur Coast
bio: Sur Coast is comprised of a dynamic duo who creates serene piano pieces that evoke the calm and beauty of the sea. With each note, listeners are transported to tranquil coastal landscapes, where they can unwind and relax. The music is perfect for moments of quiet reflection, meditation, and peaceful introspection.

name: Les Moray
bio: Les Moray explores the more fragile and introspective side of solo piano. Created by a Swedish composer and conductor, the project moves slowly, often resting in unresolved harmonies and long silences. Les Moray is written for late nights, solitude, and inward listening.

name: Ludwig Bern
bio: Ludwig Bern is a NYC based composer of beautiful, calming neoclassical piano pieces

name: Solvaen
bio: Solvaen is the solo piano project of Massimo Discepoli, a composer of music for film, TV and media. His music explores quietness, intimacy and the beauty of simplicity, creating gentle piano pieces for moments of stillness, reflection and escape.

name: Darkuro
bio: Darkuro's name highlights the nature of his compositions, pieces that are dramatic, yet peaceful, and melodies created to tell stories with mastery.

name: Nascondiglio
bio: Suono quello che canta il mio cuore… 🌸

name: Ben Moldau
bio: Whenever I watch a film that moves me, I feel it — the music, the atmosphere. I often dream that I’m living inside a film. When I walk the streets, I see everything from the outside and hear the music that would bring it to life. That is when I have to sit down at the piano.

name: Mariuga
bio: Belgian pianist and composer with a passion for creating calm, intimate piano pieces that blend minimalism, softness, and storytelling through melody. 🤍

name: Peiskos
bio: Peiskos' music is like a warm blanket for the soul. Specializing in quiet, reflective piano pieces, each composition is carefully crafted to ease tension and provide listeners with a sense of calm. Perfect for slow mornings or restful evenings, Peiskos invites you to breathe deeply and let go.

name: Emmanuel Sapphire
bio: Jamie Safir is an English, London based pianist, composer and producer. Under the name Emmanuel Sapphire Safir releases his beautiful and timeless neoclassical compositions, performed exquisitely on piano.

name: Fredrik Lundberg
bio: Fredrik Lundberg is a composer and pianist living in Stockholm, Sweden. Trained in both classical and jazz piano from early years, his music moves between classical, pop, jazz and electronica. Since 2012 he runs his own studio and record company, Dream Probe Music. He is also behind the electronic one man side project Jupuno. His piano singles like Memories of red, Two birds,  Embrace and many more has together reached over 50 million streams and are listed on several Amazon and Spotify playlist like Peaceful Piano (8 million subscribers). He released his album The Apple Tree in 2024. A 10 track compilation of new and old tracks. New music is coming in 2026, both singles and albums.

name: Francesco Rossi
bio: The piano is a powerful voice. It can tell stories and make you experience something you’ve never felt before. Welcome in to my world.

name: Leo Nocta
bio: What characterises Leo Nocta’s music most is the way he captures fragments of lived experience through his unique sensitivity and humanity. He approaches the piano like a film director would use a typewriter, sitting down and improvising, letting cinematic melodies unfold like poetic sentences.  His universe draws from introspection and dark romanticism, subtly navigating a neo-classical noir aesthetic, where emotion takes precedence over virtuosity.  Alongside his solo work, Leo Nocta is a diamond-certified and multi-platinum producer.

name: Teide
bio: Teide is a neoclassical project by Los-Angeles based Keyboardist and Musical Director and composer Dwight Rivera. Dwight Rivera is a Los Angeles based pianist, composer, and musical director. Originally from New York City, he’s a graduate of Berklee College of Music with a dual Bachelor’s Degree in Film Scoring and Contemporary Writing/Production. Dwight attended Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School, where he joined the school’s New Music Ensemble, a composition collective known as one of the foremost popular music composition seminars in the country. While there he developed a passion for working with and supporting singers. He was also encouraged by teacher Robert Apostle to start composing solo piano music. Since moving to Los Angeles, Dwight has kept up a busy career as a keyboardist, session player, accompanist, and Musical Director. He has played and worked with musicians, singers, and actors such as Joss Stone, Linda Perry, Colin Hay (Men at Work), Sheryl Lee Ralph, Elliot Yamin, Pia Toscano, Tito Puente Jr, world music superstar Khaled, and many others. He has toured as a keyboardist across the country and internationally. In recent years Dwight has added a focus on solo piano and instrumental music. His compositions are enjoyed by millions across the globe daily. Dwight’s piano music focuses on beautiful, elegant melodies accompanied by intimate, peaceful ostinatos that convey a sense of tranquility and nostalgia for anyone who listens.

name: Maxim Slanov
bio: Maxim Slanov (Martin Nevin) is a savant in musical world-building, is appreciated globally for his expressive and serene music. Know for his prolific work in other genres, Nevin enjoys expressing himself in a variety of musical settings.

name: Gia
bio: Piano sketches that hold space for what words can't express

name: John Othmar
bio: Music has always been my way of telling stories and expressing emotion.  I’m a pianist and composer with a background in film and TV music.  Through simple and emotional piano pieces, I hope to create moments of calm and reflection.  Thank you for taking the time to listen.

name: Lunar Lull
bio: Lunar Lull is the peaceful piano project of Swedish composer and pianist Jonny Ek. With a background in jazz piano, Jonny creates intimate, melodic music that blends simplicity and emotional clarity. As Lunar Lull, he composes calm, reflective piano pieces for rest, focus, and quiet moments.

name: Anna Landström
bio: Anna Landström is a Swedish composer, pianist, and vocalist who grew up in Gothenburg with singing and music as a constant backdrop. She trained as a music teacher, specialising in voice and piano, then spent years tutoring and freelancing in Stockholm. Over time the piano stopped being something she taught and became something she wrote with.   Her 2022 debut "Early Memories" opened a run of contemporary classical work that is unhurried and openly emotional - and it has travelled further than solo piano usually does: close to 100 million streams across different streaming platforms, and a catalogue soundtracking billions of views on YouTube and TikTok.

name: Damien Jeunet

name: Alex Laude

name: Robert Gafforelli

name: Alfons Daiminger
bio: Alfons Daimanger is a pseudonym of New York City based, neoclassical and jazz composer and pianist Julian Shore. Shore, a master of musical world-building, is appreciated globally for his beautiful and serene music.

name: Sounds from a Box
bio: Sounds From a Box, created by composer Matthew Reid in 2021, offers original piano music crafted for quiet relaxation and imaginative reflection. Inspired by the subtle beauty of early 20th-century French chamber music, Reid pushes compositional boundaries while maintaining the calming essence of piano relaxation. His work invites listeners to unwind or explore their creativity within soothing, elegant soundscapes.

name: Allard Sidonia
bio: Wherever you are bound, let yourself glide through the open air, effortlessly. My piano music is created to be a gentle breeze under your wings. Enjoy the flight.

name: Richard Sauzal
bio: The rugged beauty of the Atlantic coast is the inspiration for Richard Sauzal. From the morning lights to the quiet moment the sun sinks into the sea. The piano is a canvas where the ocean and the stillness of nature come to life.

name: Stanley Lloyd
bio: Welcome to the world of music made specifically to promote focus.  Piano music to appease your senses, inspire your wits, and overcome your distractions. Settle in for a gentle and relaxing ride, inspiring motivation with the likes you've never seen before.

name: Sam Sapphire
bio: Sam Sapphire is my most everyday piano project. I grew up around music in Sweden and now work as a pianist, composer, and producer. Here I focus on simple pieces, warm chords, and small melodic ideas - recorded closely and quietly as background music for work, calm rooms, and daily life.

name: Zofia Kaczmarek
bio: Zofia Kaczmarek composes like someone watching something fade - slowly, quietly, and with full awareness that it won’t last. Her music is rooted in the fragile beauty of impermanence. Inspired by drying petals, forgotten bouquets, and the subtle decay of time, her piano pieces feel like moments preserved just before they disappear. Notes linger longer than expected, as if hesitating to let go. There’s a softness in her work, but also an underlying weight - a quiet acceptance that everything passes. Each composition unfolds like a pressed flower between pages: delicate, muted, and filled with memory. Zofia doesn’t write to hold on. She writes to remember what it felt like while it was still here.

name: Dylan Charbeneau
bio: 🎹   https://www.frontpagenewsmusic.com/post/a-story-about-dylan-charbeneau

name: Reinhard Krause
bio: With a sensitivity to subtle shifts in mood and tone, Reinhard Krause brings clarity, warmth, and balance to the piano. The music encourages listeners to slow down and remain present.

name: Ever So Blue
bio: Ever So Blue is Gothenburg-based songwriter Jakob Ahlbom's homage to the piano as a solo instrument - where simplicity meets intimacy. The melodies are left pure and uncluttered, with clever subtle nuances creating the perceived variations in dynamics and rhythm. His 2019 debut Fragment found its audience almost overnight, its four sonic chapters amassing over 6 million Spotify streams within a month. The project has since grown to more than 354 million Spotify streams

name: Kisane
bio: Being autodidact pianist, Kisane brings all his passion in every performance, delicate, simple melodies that are touching the heart.

name: Holgar Ingeldson
bio: Holgar is a lifelong pianist and musician who has trained extensively.  Whether a classical concert or recording his focus is on clarity, beauty and musicianship.  As he explores the limitless possibilities of the instrument, he captivates listeners with his artistry and passion

name: Aisen Voight
bio: Aisen Voight, a master of musical world-building, is appreciated globally for his expressive and serene music. The project is a pseudonym of composer Luke Marantz who known for his work in many other genres and enjoys adopting different personas fluent in other genres to best express himself in a variety of musical settings.

name: Muriël Bostdorp
bio: Muriël plays the piano with the beauty of melancholy. Her compositions, inspired by nature and everyday life, move between stillness and intensity. Without words, she invites the listener on a sonic journey to dreamlike, almost cinematic landscapes.  “The chords I hear and use always carry a certain sense of melancholy. I think it’s part of who I am; playing the piano and composing music is for me a way of life”.

name: Patrick Hamilton
bio: Patrick Hamilton is a multi-faceted artist who effortlessly moves between the roles of composer, producer and performer. Signed to Sony Music Masterworks, Hamilton successfully combines his work as a composer in the contemporary classical space with his work in film and TV score composition. Artistically diverse, Patrick Hamilton is rooted in the core classical tradition. Hailing from Bruges in Belgium, he was classically trained at the Royal Conservatoires in Bruges & Ghent before embarking on a hugely successful and varied musical career, spanning many genres.  Hamilton soon became the producer of choice for a range of internationally renowned artists, His production, writing and arranging work for best-selling classical artist, Katherine Jenkins, has seen Patrick oversee a number of Katherine’s albums, all of which reached number 1 on the UK Official Classical Artist Album Chart, including her 12th studio album ‘Cinema Paradiso’ (2022). In addition to his successful career in composition and production, Patrick Hamilton also runs his own studios ‘The Globe Recording Studios’, founded in 2002 as well as operating BROMO Music Publishing, the publishing department of The Globe music company.   Signed to Sony Music Masterworks, Patrick Hamilton is represented for management by Tara Joseph  @ATC Management and for publishing by Decca Publishing (UK) where he was one of their first signings alongside Max Richter.   For more info visit : www.patrickhamiltonmusic.com

name: Elias Kiefer
bio: I´m glad you found your way here.  Two to three times a week, I improvise for  one hour without stopping, regardless of  what I´m playing.  The pieces you find here are not composed,  but rather small parts of these long improvisations.  I hope you enjoy listening.

name: Ren Lockhart
bio: Ren Lockhart is appreciated globally for his beautiful and serene music. A pseudonym of composer Christian Li who is predominantly known in other fields, Li enjoys adopting different personas fluent in other genres to best express himself in a variety of settings.

name: Maxime Verdoni
bio: Maxime Verdoni is a French pianist and composer whose music blends neoclassical, cinematic and romantic influences. Inspired by nature, nostalgia and human emotion, his compositions are defined by expressive melodies and an intimate, personal approach to the piano.  Since beginning his musical journey in 2020, his work has reached an international audience, accumulating over 30 million streams across digital platforms. Beyond streaming, his piano performances and compositions have resonated with millions of people on social media, where he has built a community of over one million followers worldwide.  His compositions, including Winter Waltz in C Minor, Dreamers and Autumn Waltz in C Minor, have found their place in the contemporary piano repertoire, with releases featured in leading editorial playlists on Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon Music.

name: Oscar Mallen
bio: Oscar Mallen is a Spanish pianist and composer. Trained as a classical pianist at the conservatory, he soon began to compose and produce music, also with the help of musical computers. To this day his favorite composer is still Chopin. He is passionate about intimate melodies. Now focused on sharing with the world melodies that awaken feelings and touch the soul through the magic of music.

name: Cherries & Daydreams
bio: Lush guitar based on trippy dreams. Enjoy :s

name: Javier Escudero
bio: Escudero is a neoclassical virtuoso, who crafts compositions with meticulous attention to detail. His music evokes deep emotions, offering a meditative journey with a sense of duality showcasing Escudero's musicianship. Many listeners have embraced Escudero's artistry so far, acknowledging his skill and unique musical identity.

name: Starstrum
bio: Starstrum creates dreamy, meditative ambient music for focus and relaxation. With millions of listeners worldwide, the music offers airy soundscapes that calm the mind and set the perfect atmosphere.

name: The Dawning
bio: The Dawning makes music that asks for nothing except a moment of stillness. Soft guitar swells and patient melodies designed to sit perfectly beneath your thoughts.

name: Rymdklostret
bio: Rymdklostret traces back to Berlin, where guitars, synths and two different musical instincts found their way into the same room.  The idea of making something together stayed around for years. It only became real once Berlin was behind them.  Now split between Brussels and Stockholm, Rymdklostret has become a long-distance meeting point between electric guitars, warm analog textures and synth-driven soundscapes. Ideas move back and forth across Europe, slowly taking shape as spacious, guitar-led instrumentals built around atmosphere and focus.

name: Atlas
bio: I'm a musician from Sweden. Atlas is my dreamy guitar project. Enjoy my tunes!

name: oerra

bio: Nómis creates atmospheric ambient music, often centered around expressive guitar and immersive soundscapes. Each composition is crafted to create moments of stillness, peace, and quiet reflection.

name: Sonic Waves
bio: Sonic Waves captures the quiet beauty of isolation through sound. Warm tape-hiss, patient melodies, and meditative structures tailored to ground you in the present moment.

name: Pete McMurray
bio: Pete McMurray explores ambient music through sounds, textures, and influences from around the world. A journey across borders, blending distant atmospheres into new spaces to drift through.

name: Lumen Atlas
bio: Lumen Atlas creates deep focus music designed to bring calm, clarity, and creativity into your day. With atmospheric textures and gentle melodies, our soundscapes help you concentrate, meditate, and find your flow.

name: Alex Blackwood

name: leony
bio: Leony is an exploration of the quiet architecture of the wilderness—the long shadows of late afternoon filtering through the trees, the rustle of dry leaves, the comfort of open spaces. These pieces are deliberately patient, designed to quiet a racing mind.

name: Under The Zodiac
bio: The vast embodied in music. Under The Zodiac is an escape into the endless. Driven by intergalactic guitar tones—space has never been as near…
