name: Hidden Piano
bio: Hidden Piano is a quiet exploration of what lingers beneath the surface- the moments we don't show, and the pauses that speak more than words.

name: Florentin Davies
bio: Florentin Davies is a piano-based project inspired by landscapes, memory, and slow living.  Created by a Swedish composer who works across classical, choral, and contemporary music, the project focuses on lyrical melodies and gentle harmonic movement. The music is written for reflection, walking, and soft daylight hours.

name: Jeroen Granneman
bio: What started as a hobby in his childhood bedroom grew into a serious musical ambition. Jeroen studied at the conservatory, where he specialized in improvised music. Improvisation has become the common thread in his musical life, both in his compositions and live performances. The freedom to create music on the spot and translate emotions directly into sound is what inspires him most as a pianist.  Alongside his conservatory studies, Jeroen also pursued a degree in Music Management. Despite his musical background, he initially chose a career outside of music and worked as a project manager at a large insurance company. Eventually, he realized that his true passion lay in music and decided to dedicate himself fully to it.  With his neoclassical piano music, Jeroen has reached a broad international audience. His compositions can be heard in major streaming playlists, contributing to his impressive growth as a pianist. Each month, he releases new piano pieces and performs them live at concerts.  www.jeroengranneman.com

name: Vellore
bio: Ambient music that moves slowly and breathes softly.  Minimal textures, warm tones.  Designed for sleep, stillness, and the quiet in between.

name: Deep Vibrations
bio: Deep Vibrations exists in the space between sound and silence. Born from years of composing for film, television, and games, the project turned inward around 2012 - toward instrumental ambient music created for sleep, surrender, and inner quiet. With a minimalist approach, Deep Vibrations unfolds slowly, using restrained harmonies, subtle textures, and open space. The music does not seek attention, but presence-offering a gentle sonic horizon where the mind can rest and the body can let go.

name: Edge Of The Spiral
bio: Edge Of The Spiral is a Stockholm-based ambient project exploring the space between nature, sound, and experimentation. Inspired by time spent outdoors, the project combines field recordings, synthesizers, effects pedals, and found sounds to create atmospheric and immersive music.

name: Angelic Planet
bio: Angelic Planet is a personal project dedicated to calm, presence, and inner space. I am a songwriter and producer from Stockholm who spent many years working with film music before turning fully toward instrumental ambient music around 2012. Through gentle textures, spacious soundscapes, and slow-moving harmonies, Angelic Planet creates music for meditation, relaxation, and deep rest - always with tranquility at the core. Please make sure to follow me if you like my music ❤️

name: Opaline Monarque
bio: Opaline Monarque creates ambient music that feels suspended somewhere between waking and dreaming. Soft textures and distant harmonies unfold slowly and invite the listener to leave the noise of everyday life behind. The music opens a path to a quieter place made for deep rest meditation and sleep.

name: Earthbound
bio: Earthbound explores binaural frequencies for focus and rest, creating minimalist audio for study sessions and quiet nights.

name: Syntropy
bio: Syntropy paints ethereal soundscapes, transcending the boundaries of time and space. With delicate synth whispers and pulsating rhythms, Syntropy's music conjures a realm where thoughts harmonize with the cosmos. Each composition is a journey, a meditation into the unseen, a celestial voyage through the tapestry of existence. As twilight melds with dawn, Syntropy weaves tales of cosmic embrace, a symphony of the universe's heartbeats. In this auditory reverie, find solace, find the sublime, and let the universe's secrets whisper through Syntropy's ambient melodies.

name: Jon Thebur
bio: Jon Thebur is a distinguished German pianist, composer, arranger, and producer. Deeply influenced by the pop music of the 1980s, Jon pursued studies in classical music, jazz, and composition. Throughout his career, he has collaborated with numerous renowned artists in various capacities, including composer, arranger, and producer. Jon's versatility extends to writing for string quartets and orchestras, composing for television and film, and performing as a pianist for diverse projects. His compositions have garnered several awards, reflecting his exceptional talent. Jon Thebur's serene and lyrical piano pieces emphasize melodious and minimalist moments. His work captures the essence of fleeting ideas, themes, and the delicate and contemplative, while also celebrating beauty and promise. Although the piano is his primary instrument, Jon frequently incorporates other instruments such as strings, Sansula, Kalimba, and electronics into his compositions. www.jonthebur.com

Built on layered piano and long reverberant tones, the project takes its orientation from the fixed and the recurring, sounds that return, slightly changed, like something half-remembered. Minimal in structure but generous in feeling, these recordings work as well behind focused work as they do beside late-night quiet.

With music that encourages exploration and self-expression, Rylan’s tracks are a reminder that feelings shouldn’t be boxed in but allowed to flow freely. His soothing yet thought-provoking sound invites you to reflect, release, and expand your emotional boundaries.

name: Cook Daniel
bio: Cook Daniel is the alter ego of Dutch music producer, composer and songwriter Kees Koek. With a background in working for (inter)national artists through his label CJK Music Productions & Publishing, he now focuses on creating music that brings calm, balance and rest.  Under the name Cook Daniel, he produces Lounge Music, New Age, relaxing instrumental music for wellness, meditation, spa and blending ambient textures with subtle piano, soft strings and warm grooves. His music moves between deep-house chillout, lounge, cinematic and deep ambient, always designed to help the listener unwind and reconnect.  For these productions, Cook Daniel collaborates with some of the top musicians from the Dutch music scene. The result is soulful, carefully crafted music that feels both light and deeply rooted.    (Every release is crafted with care by Cook Daniel using musical performance, orchestral libraries and professionally created virtual instruments. The creative process is entirely human, with no AI used in the composition, arrangement or production of these recordings. )  In addition to his relaxing music, Kees also produces epic orchestral and film music under his other pseudonym: Cornel Jacobs Cook, also available on Spotify. Check him out.   🌿 www.cookdaniel.com 🎧 www.cjkmusic.com 📸 Photos by Patricia Steur & Iris Fricke

name: Universal Balance
bio: Universal Balance crafts serene soundscapes that transport listeners to the tranquil forests and fjords of the Nordics. His music is a haven for relaxation, meditation, and restful sleep. Inspired by the vast beauty of Nordic landscapes, Universal Balance creates tracks that calm the mind, ease stress, and promote mindfulness. Ideal for those seeking inner peace or a restful night’s sleep, Universal Balance’s music is your soundtrack to tranquility. Follow on Spotify to explore his growing catalog and let the Nordic-inspired melodies guide you to calm.

The project creates immersive listening experiences that encourage reflection, balance, and a deeper connection to the world around us.

name: Cinthya Garcia
bio: Cinthya Garcia is a Spanish pianist and composer currently based in Miami, US, who focuses on Modern Classical Piano Music.  Classically trained, the story of Cinthya with piano begins at the age of 8 when she gets fascinated by music as a powerful form of expression: she sings, creates, learns piano by ear, and finds in music a new best friend, and a little keyboard becomes her favorite toy from which she never separates.  Then she begins formal lessons, and with time that vocation turns into a profession, graduating years later with honors in classical piano performance and pedagogy. She is happy as a teacher, she loves music and her profession, but somehow, that energy that had captivated her as a child continues to beat strongly inside her.  In 2013 she leaves her country and casually, she starts then to participate in music projects of different genres and styles. That allows her to expand her musical vision.  And then, she begins to compose, and finds in piano again a way to reflect her emotions, to keep her secrets... to tell stories without words. Her first release is Uncertain (Nov. 2017). After this, she has released some albums, eps and singles both independently and also collaborating with music labels. Her music is inspired by her life and personal evolution: melancholy, joy, love, evolution. Her music style seeks the beauty of the melody with influences of minimalism, classical piano, but also pop and electronic music. https://www.cinthyagarcia.com

name: Ryley Moss

name: Akira Kosemura
bio: When Akira Kosemura started making music, it was a kind of therapy during his difficult time in his early 20s. He carried an audio recorder to capture the soundscape he encountered, and those field recordings inspired him to create music with his piano. “My original reason for making it, after all, was to heal myself, a kind of rehabilitation technique and it is still part of my everyday life, or perhaps an extension of it. It’s like breathing for me” he recalls.  Since his record debut in 2007, Kosemura’s compositions have been reflecting his inner voice, and drawing various images silently and beautifully – from quiet nights, four seasons, to some stories about unknown people in unknown world. He garnered attention worldwide, collaborated with notable musicians such as John Legend and Devendra Banhart, and created scores for films/TV drama/video games like the Cannes featured film True Mothers, Hollywood produced drama series Love Is__, the Nintendo Switch game Jack Jeanne, TV anime Honey Lemon Soda, and so many others. Completely self-taught composer/pianist has become one of the most streamed Asian classical artists, has signed Decca Records/Universal Music in 2022, and released diverse records including his renowned solo piano album, SEASONS.  Now in 2025, His new album MIRAI is the highly anticipated new album from Akira Kosemura, One of his most challenging and compelling albums to date, MIRAI is his first-ever vocal project album with 7 notable singers.

name: Cameron Segal
bio: Cameron Segal is an Australian composer and pianist known for intimate neoclassical music centred around mindfulness, reflection and calm. With over 100 million streams and a global community of more than one million followers, his music has connected with listeners around the world.  Built around the warmth of felt piano, Cameron’s compositions blend delicate melodies with subtle ambient textures and influences from the natural world. His music has been supported across Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon Music, alongside multiple broadcasts on Classic FM.  Cameron has released a growing collection of music with Deutsche Grammophon and is currently working on his next project with the label, exploring a more expansive sound through piano, strings and collaboration.  Now based in Australia, Cameron continues to compose, record and perform music designed to create moments of stillness in an increasingly busy world.

name: Christian Lindquist
bio: Christian Lindquist is a Swedish composer, pianist and guitarist. Living on the islands outside Gothenburg on the west coast of Sweden - with its stunning nature it is easy to be creative and find inspiration.   The music is widely used by SPA's and hospitals for meditation and relaxation. The style is quiet, introspective, and deeply personal.   Why   I have always liked the sunrise, the freshness of an early morning. That has also become my time and very often I sit down and play my instruments. I push record and play until the inspiration is out. The choice of keeping a recording is depended on how it makes me feel.      My music is about my feelings, mood and my hunger for expression. Playing in a more or less improvised form is a quest for honesty, where suddenly the tone that was insipid yesterday is inspired today. The instrument has become a way for me to verify my soul and to whittle truth out of my heart. The melodies are therefore a profound mix of pain and of peace.    I hope that my musical expression is a bearer of (e)motion which helps you as a listener to flow in the right direction…     Your Life evolves from Your Thoughts   //Christian Lindquist - www.solopianodiary.com

bio: Lars Florence is a Stockholm-based pianist who has played piano all his life, with a background in both classical and jazz music. The project focuses on intimate piano covers and gentle original compositions, creating a warm and calming sound for quiet moments, relaxation, and slowing down.

name: Davy Burns
bio: When I play the piano, it’s not just about the notes – it’s about the soul of a song.  Taking familiar tracks and giving them a twist: Softer, dreamier.   Whether it’s rock or pop, my goal is the same – to make you feel something new in something you already love. Welcome to my space.

name: Ron Lopata
bio: I make piano music that feels like a movie you’ve lived through — emotional, cinematic, and real. Every piece starts as a feeling I can’t explain, so I let the piano speak for me.  Its where I say the things I can’t in words. If it makes you feel something, that’s all that matters.

name: Steve Dawson
bio: Bassist Steve Dawson played an integral role in the success of British metallers Saxon, which began in 1972 as Son of a Bitch: he got the gigs, drove the van, and sent the demos. However, the band stayed unsigned until 1979, when Carrere Records issued Saxon. Platinum success followed Wheels of Steel (1980), which also broke the band internationally. Dawson's no-frills writing style made itself felt on the title track, "747 Strangers in the Night," "Freeway Mad," and "Street Fighting Gang." He remained a strong contributor on Denim & Leather (1981), Strong Arm of the Law (1982), and Power & the Glory (1983), which is generally considered their finest album. This Is Spinal Tap's wicked sendup of rock clichés brought Dawson's image into the pop-cultural arena, since he's acknowledged as inspiring the character of hapless, diminutive bassist Derek Smalls. Saxon's sound assumed a more commercial sheen on Crusader (1984) and Innocence Is No Excuse (1985), which also marked Dawson's last bow. The band fired him for unexplained reasons in June 1986. Dawson quickly regrouped with guitarist Steve Johnson and former Saxon drummer Nigel Durham for a solo album that went unreleased, for legal reasons; Angel Air reissued their AOR- and hard rock-styled efforts in 2002 as Pandemonium Circus. He and former Saxon guitarist Oliver Dawson also laid claim to their old band's name as Oliver Dawson Saxon, with the intent of recording an album for Angel Air. Vocalist Biff Byford also continued to front a version of the band; further flurries of court action didn't stop either lineup from going about its business. ~ Ralph Heibutzki, Rovi

Fusing smooth rhythms with airy melodies and ambient textures, his tracks create an effortlessly laid-back vibe, perfect for moments of relaxation and reflection. With a focus on atmospheric depth and soulful grooves.

name: Vincent McRae Trio
bio: Vincent McRae Trio is a jazz ensemble crafting a sound that feels both welcoming and quietly melancholic. Blending warmth with subtle introspection, the trio creates music that naturally fills the room with atmosphere and emotion. Through delicate interplay and expressive dynamics, their sound moves between comfort and longing -where melodies linger and harmonies unfold with gentle depth.   Each performance invites the listener into an intimate space, like a conversation carried through tone and silence. At its core, Vincent McRae Trio offers a listening experience that is both close and reflective music that settles in, resonates, and stays with you.

name: Beau Shepherd
bio: Beau Shepherd is an emerging artist with a deep love of holiday music. His work often reflects the warmth and joy of festive seasons, blending traditional tunes with modern, soulful interpretations. From an early age, Beau was captivated by the melodies of Christmas carols and holiday tunes, which inspired him to create art that resonates with the spirit of celebration and nostalgia. Shepherd’s style is marked by a vibrant use of sound and emotion, making his performances a seasonal favorite for audiences seeking both comfort and cheer.

name: Ben Bromfield
bio: Ben Bromfield is an Emmy-nominated composer for film, television, and video games out of Boston, MA. A lifelong jazz pianist, Ben graduated Berklee College of Music in 2010 and has lived in Los Angeles ever since. He is known for his score of the the new Netflix series, Ginny & Georgia (for which he received an Emmy nomination in 2023) and the Dreamworks animated television series, Boss Baby: Back in Business. Ben is an expert in animation scoring, having composed the score for the Dreamworks Where's Waldo? and Netflix's Oddballs, and having contributed music to several other popular animated shows. In film, Ben has made his mark scoring such indies as BOOM!: A Film About The Sonics, a documentary telling the story of one of the most influential 60's rock bands, The Salzburg Story, a romantic comedy which won 'Best Feature Film' at the California International Film Festival, and Borderland, an action/thriller featuring performances by Bruce Dern and Peter Fonda.

name: Piano Relaxium
bio: "Piano Relaxium" is a solo piano project by Belgian composer and pianist Alex De Winter.  It began back in 2020 and has gradually grown into a large catalogue of original piano pieces, alongside piano interpretations of familiar songs (including the Disney songs we all grew up with!).  At heart, though, it is simply piano music for those moments when a little less noise is welcome.  Enjoy!

name: Klaüs
bio: Nazareno also know as klaüs (b. 1999) is a pianist/composer, currently based in Buenos Aires Argentina. "I want to achieve a unique message with my music. Not to be known for one type of musical style, but to be in permanent search and, above all, to achieve my own satisfaction and thus reach people's hearts. That is my goal." He began studying piano when he was 11 years old and was instantly mesmerized by classical music. He was always very curious. Like every romantic child, his first great companion was Chopin. His parents got him a piano and he began to develop a love for the instrument. From then on he began to study music theory very independently, wanting to discover every detail that music had to offer, composing pieces through the sensations he was experiencing and is currently experiencing.. He fell in love with the Ghibli Sound when he saw the movie "Princess Mononoke". From then on he began to study the ambivalent details they generate and the beautiful sensations they project with each sound. He is currently studying Academic Music at the National University of the Arts and at the same time creating music. Immersed in the search for new connections, he got a call for a job to compose music for anime style projects in the web3 and NFT world, he is currently developing his own ideas and building a project for everyone to feel a part of! You can hear a rock version of me at: SIN DATOS :)

name: Rui Fujishiro
bio: A diary, written through the piano 𓇗  Rui Fujishiro sketches her daily thoughts through the piano, writing the stories and worlds she imagines through sound.  Everything begins with improvisation, freely sketched like a diary, and becomes music.  Her works depict what cannot be seen and what cannot be expressed in words.  Composer / Creates music through piano contact : ruifujishiro.mng@gmail.com

name: Matteo Myderwyk
bio: Based in the Netherlands, Myderwyk has made a name for himself by breaking away from classical conventions. After training as a concert pianist, he left behind the works of Debussy and Ravel to follow a freer, more instinctive path — improvising, composing in the moment, and building sound worlds from raw emotion rather than written scores.  His unconventional approach has resonated widely. In recent years, he’s been nominated multiple times for the prestigious Edison Award and has performed in some of the Netherlands’ most iconic venues — including Het Concertgebouw, Paradiso, and TivoliVredenburg. While his studio albums often begin at the piano, his live shows are something else entirely: immersive, unpredictable, and deeply atmospheric. Whether in a concert hall, a club, or a festival tent, Myderwyk’s performances are driven by intuition and curiosity, constantly shifting between textures, tempos, and timbres.  With a growing discography and a sound that appeals to both classical purists and synth lovers, Matteo Myderwyk is carving out a bold new space in the European music scene — where acoustic warmth meets analog grit, and tradition gives way to pure sonic exploration.

name: Dirk Maassen
bio: Dirk Maassen (* 28. February 1970 in Aachen) is an independent german composer and pianist living in Ulm, Germany. Dirk plays piano since the age of 10 and studied a broad variety of musical styles in his early musical career. His compositions and play have deeply touched millions of listeners worldwide and his music has been featured in several film projects so far including the award winning movie "Crossroads " which was introduced at the Cannes Film festival in 2015. More about Dirk at: http://dirkmaassen.com

name: Otto A. Totland
bio: Otto Andreas Totland was born in Porsgrunn, Norway 26. April 1979. Totland's modern compositional elements are also recognized as half of the Norwegian duo Deaf Center, where his melancholic, intricate piano work provides haunting relief to the beds of noise and deep strings from Erik K Skodvin. Other side projects, Nest is the collaborative project of Otto Totland and Huw Roberts (Serein - Hidden Rivers). The two started working together after forging a friendship as former members of the Miasmah label. With 2021's "Companion", Otto A Totland completed his trilogy of personal, sparse piano compositions, following in the footsteps of 2014´s "Pinô" and 2017´s "The Lost". His latest record "Exin" was recorded and co-produced by Nils Frahm at his studio in the German capital’s famed Funkhaus complex in September 2023. The 16-track collection is available on limited edition vinyl as well as via all digital platforms from June 14, 2024. As a self-taught pianist, Otto further determines himself as a timeless composer who follows nothing but his own gut and heart. The outcome is something so pure it’s hard to not be affected. The development of his pieces over the years has grown into something so himself that it’s almost immediately recognizable.

name: Justus Eichhorn
bio: German pianist-composer Justus Eichhorn is one of the most gifted and charismatic artists of his generation.  Still just 16 years old and continuing his standard education as well as his specialist music studies, he has performed in Europe, China and Korea, attracting sell-out audiences to prestigious venues from Hamburg and Zurich to Shenzhen and Seoul.  June 2026 saw the start of a collaboration with Deutsche Grammophon. Eichhorn will make his DG debut with The Source, an album that traces the rich musical history of his birthplace, Weimar, through works by J.S. Bach, Mendelssohn, Liszt, Hindemith, Schubert and R. Strauss. The Source will be released on 4 September 2026.

name: Martin Kohlstedt
bio: Martin Kohlstedt is among the outstanding composers, pianists and producers for instrumental music and electronica. His albums and their respective reworks were rewarded with international recognition and concert tours throughout the whole world.  With his live performances as well as his studio recordings Martin Kohlstedt sets standards on how cutting edge electronica production can intermingle with analogue and acoustic approaches ranging from classical piano and ambient to field recordings and score design in an effortless way. Kohlstedt intuitively combines inspirations and influences from fundamentally different worlds and soundscapes into a unique musical amalgam and forms it into something that feels more like a living body than a list of pieces – be it in form of a spectacular festival show, an introspective piano concert, a multidimensional movie score or an immersive album experience.  He describes his style of work as modular composition; his pieces are always in movement and never resort to a definitive form – even during concerts. Improvisation is an important part of his creative process, and so are the interaction with his audience on equal footing, the courage and sometimes audacity to fail and the interaction with people, space and context.

name: Olexandr Ignatov
bio: Olexandr Ignatov is a neoclassical pianist and composer from Lviv, Ukraine, and one of the country's most-streamed neoclassical artists. His music ranges from intimate solo piano to cinematic orchestral arrangements, always about atmosphere and emotion. Heard worldwide across streaming platforms, his pieces have become a soundtrack for everyday moments and for creators across TikTok, Instagram and YouTube.  What matters most to him is simple: that the music isn't just heard, but truly felt.  Follow him on Instagram: @olexandrignatov

name: Gabriel Albuquerqüe
bio: Gabriel Albuquerque is a 23-year-old film composer, music producer, and multi-instrumentalist born in Brazil. He never had a music teacher or studied theory in a classroom. Everything he knows, he learned by ear. As a child, he would stare at the night sky for hours, captivated by its vastness, by the quiet, by the feeling that something greater was out there, just beyond reach. He didn’t know it yet, but that same wonder would shape the way he made music.  For Gabriel, melodies have never been something to be written down and studied. They appear like constellations in the dark, guiding him toward emotions that words can’t quite capture. Music became his way of understanding the world, of expressing what can’t be seen, only felt.  That same instinct led his compositions to places he never imagined. His music has been featured in events like the Champions League, UFC, Premier League, and La Liga, as well as in dance performances, short films, and documentaries across dozens of countries. Over time, it found its audience, making him the most-streamed Brazilian neoclassical artist in the world and the youngest Brazilian composer in this genre to reach the number one spot in Brazil.  He gained recognition after reaching the 23rd position on the Billboard Top 50 TikTok Chart and the 14th position on the global viral charts. But more than numbers, what matters to him is what music has always been about: a connection that doesn’t need explanation, only feeling.  ig: gabriel_albuq

name: Christian Balvig
bio: The 31 year old Dane, Christian Balvig, is known for his work as composer and arranger for an array of bands and ensembles - Copenhagen Phil, Det Norske Blåsensemble, Love Shop, Lowly, Dreamers Circus and When Saints Go Machine just to name a few. His own records “Music For Humans” and “Associated with Water” has been critically acclaimed internationally.   Christian is working seamlessly across different genres and mediums, and has also been hired as producer, filmscorer and composer-assistant in several occasions. Amongst other documentary movies, can be mentioned: "A Word For Human" (composer) by Mauricio Ananda - Gonzales, “Human Flow” (composer assistant) by Ai Wei Wei and “Gina - Midt I En Drøm” (composer/music producer) by Sofie Lange Jørgensen. With When Saints Go Machine, he just released the score and opening track for the tv - series "Ulven Kommer" on Danish Television (approx 1.000.000 viewers on each episode). Furthermore, Christian has played concerts and festivals all over the world including Japan, India, Vietnam, Gambia, USA and most of Europe, as pianist and keyboardist.   On May 12th, Christian Balvig is set to release his debut solo album Night Poem. The album is an ode to and from the night, a rebellion against constant stimuli, and a meticulous hunt for ghost notes and the almost imperceptible sound of piano keys.  Photography: Michael C. Madsen

name: Branford Marsalis
bio: A virtuoso jazz saxophonist with a wry improvisational sense, Branford Marsalis is a boundary-pushing performer who has explored an array of styles from post-bop and traditional jazz to classical, funk, hip-hop, and rock. Initially emerging in the 1980s to widespread acclaim alongside his brother, trumpeter Wynton Marsalis, Branford drew early comparisons to idols Wayne Shorter, John Coltrane, and Sonny Rollins. Ever creatively restless, he branched out, playing with Sting, Béla Fleck, and Bruce Hornsby, as well as his own genre-bending side project Buckshot LeFonque. He brings the same adventurous, exploratory approach to his recordings, investigating aspects of the blues on 1992's Grammy-winning I Heard You Twice the First Time, leading his harmonically sophisticated quartet on 2000's Grammy-winning Contemporary Jazz, and collaborating with vocalist Kurt Elling for 2016's poetically atmospheric Upward Spiral. He hit the Top Five of the jazz charts with 2019's The Secret Between the Shadow and the Soul, scored the 2020 biopic Ma Rainey's Black Bottom, and continued his classical explorations on 2023's Sound of the Sun. In 2025, he made his Blue Note debut, leading his quartet on Belonging, before marking John Coltrane's centennial with 2026's Dedicated to You, featuring Dianne Reeves. Born in 1969 in Breaux Bridge, Louisiana, Branford Marsalis grew up in a creative musical family the eldest son of pianist and music professor Ellis Marsalis and singer and teacher Dolores. A naturally gifted musician, he learned to play piano at age four, and later took up the clarinet. He was around 15 when he decided to switch over to the saxophone. Although steeped in jazz and classical music in his youth, he also gravitated toward playing in funk bands, often with his brother Wynton. After high school, he studied music at Southern University, where he mentored under legendary New Orleans clarinetist Alvin Batiste. Under Batiste's recommendation, he then transferred to Berklee College of Music in Boston. However, he left Berklee in mid-1980 to tour Europe with a big band led by drummer Art Blakey. More work followed, including stints with Lionel Hampton and Clark Terry. By 1981, Marsalis had become a regular member of Blakey's Jazz Messengers ensemble, playing alongside Wynton. There was also a tour with Herbie Hancock's V.S.O.P. II in 1983 and recordings with Miles Davis, Was (Not Was), and Dizzy Gillespie. In 1984, Marsalis also made his debut as leader with Scenes in the City, playing alongside pianists Mulgrew Miller and Kenny Kirkland, bassists Charnett Moffett and Ron Carter, and drummers Jeff "Tain" Watts and Marvin "Smitty" Smith. From 1981 to 1985, Marsalis was a member of his brother Wynton Marsalis' quintet, appearing on a handful of influential, Grammy-winning albums, including Black Codes from the Underground, Think of One, and Hot House Flowers, all of which found the siblings building upon the modal and post-bop traditions of artists like Miles Davis, Woody Shaw, and John Coltrane. However, Marsalis left the group in 1985 to play in former Police singer Sting's band, which at the time was heavily influenced by jazz, funk, and fusion. The move brought wider recognition to Marsalis, who appeared on Sting's 1984 album Dream of the Blue Turtles and 1986 concert film and recording Bring on the Night. The move also brought other opportunities, including a long association with director Spike Lee, beginning with an appearing in 1987's School Daze. While he enjoyed playing with Sting, the saxophonist was back to leading his own group by 1986, which primarily featured pianist Kirkland, bassist Bob Hurst, and drummer Watts. Signed to Columbia, Marsalis issued inventive albums like 1986's Grammy-nominated Royal Garden Blues, 1988's Grammy-nominated Trio Jeepy, and 1991's The Beautyful Ones Are Not Yet Born. He also experimented with mixing hip-hop, funk, and acid jazz in his Buckshot LeFonque project, and continued his work with Spike Lee, contributing to 1988's Music from Do the Right Thing and 1990's Music from Mo' Better Blues. In 1992, Marsalis released I Heard You Twice the First Time, which found him exploring different expressions of the blues. Along with his brother Wynton, the album featured guest appearances from B.B. King, John Lee Hooker, Russell Malone, and Linda Hopkins. It reached number one Billboard's Top Jazz Albums chart and won the Grammy Award for Best Jazz Instrumental Performance, Individual or Group. That same year, the saxophonist gained even wider attention when he joined Jay Leno's Tonight Show as the musical director. During this period, he also contributed to the Malcolm X soundtrack and appeared on albums by Roy Hargrove, Bobby Hutcherson, Terence Blanchard, and others. After two years with Leno, Marsalis stepped down from The Tonight Show, handing the band over to guitarist Kevin Eubanks. This led to a period of eclectic guest spots on albums with Youssou N'Dour, Béla Fleck, Everette Harp, and Bruce Hornsby. Marsalis earned his second Grammy Award for Best Pop Instrumental Performance for his work on Hornsby's track "Barcelona Mona." He returned to his own genre-bending jazz work with the 1996 trio album The Dark Keys. Requiem (his final album with pianist Kirkland, who died several months after the session) arrived in 1999. In 2000, he finished out his Columbia contract with Contemporary Jazz, his first album with pianist Joey Calderazzo. It won the Grammy for Best Jazz Instrumental Performance, Individual or Group. In 2002, he formed his own label, Marsalis Music. Intended as a true independent label focused on supporting the development of musicians, Marsalis Music began issuing albums by a diverse range of artists including guitarist/vocalist Doug Wamble, pianist/vocalist Harry Connick, Jr., saxophonist Miguel Zenón, and others. Marsalis himself also kept busy releasing a handful of albums on the label including 2002's Footsteps of Our Fathers, which featured his take on the classic John Coltrane composition "A Love Supreme"; 2003's Romare Bearden Revealed; 2004's Eternal; 2006's Braggtown; and 2009's Metamorphosen, which found him paying tribute to the many of his friends and mentors who had passed away, including Alvin Batiste, Michael Brecker, Freddie Hubbard, and others. In 2011, Marsalis and Calderazzo pared down to a duo for Songs of Mirth and Melancholy. In the spring of 2012, the saxophonist's quartet, featuring Calderazzo, bassist Eric Revis, and drummer Justin Faulkner, released Four MF's Playin Tunes. Marsalis also gave a solo saxophone concert in 2012 at San Francisco's Grace Cathedral. Two years later, it was released as In My Solitude: Live at Grace Cathedral by Okeh. In 2016, Marsalis collaborated with vocalist Kurt Elling on the expansive Upward Spiral. He returned to his quartet for 2019's The Secret Between the Shadow and the Soul, which peaked at number three on the Billboard Jazz Albums chart. Also that year, he collaborated with the Ural Philharmonic Orchestra on the classical album Gabriel Prokofiev: Saxophone Concerto; Bass Drum Concerto. In 2020, Marsalis supplied the soundtrack to Ma Rainey's Black Bottom, a biopic on the life of legendary blues singer Ma Rainey starring Viola Davis and Chadwick Boseman. Another classical collaboration, Sound of the Sun, arrived in 2023 and found the saxophonist performing works by Mahler and British composer Sally Beamish alongside conductor Eric Jacobsen and the Virginia Symphony Orchestra. In 2025, Marsalis and his quartet with Calderazzo, Revis, and Faulkner made their Blue Note debut with Belonging, a complete interpretation of Keith Jarrett's 1974 ECM album of the same title featuring his European Quartet. The following year, Marsalis joined forces with vocalist Dianne Reeves for Dedicated to You, an album marking John Coltrane's centennial celebration and which found them interpreting songs off the 1963 classic John Coltrane and Johnny Hartman. ~ Matt Collar, Rovi

name: Verwey
bio: Verwey is the solo piano project of Dutch pianist and composer Erik Verwey. Intimate, cinematic and quietly adventurous, his music moves between contemporary classical, jazz and minimalism.  At the heart of Verwey’s music is the piano in its purest form: close, warm and unpolished. You hear the touch of the keys, the resonance of the instrument, the space between the notes. Melodies appear and disappear like fragments of memories — sometimes melancholic and fragile, sometimes playful, always searching for a sense of movement and hope.  Drawing inspiration from Erik Satie, Bill Evans, Federico Mompou and Philip Glass, Verwey brings together the freedom and harmony of jazz with the stillness and simplicity of modern classical music.  His music has found a home at NPO Klassiek, where Verwey was featured in Keihard Klassiek and invited to perform an hour-long solo piano Nachtsessie. His album Contour was also selected for the NPO Klassiek Top 400.  Rather than telling a fixed story, each piece creates a small world of its own — leaving room for the listener to wander. Music for quiet mornings, late nights, distant memories and everything in between.

name: Dustin O'Halloran
bio: Dustin O’Halloran is an American pianist and composer who has had a lengthy career as a film and TV composer. He is an acclaimed solo musician and is one half of the duo A Winged Victory for the Sullen. With six solo albums released, he has a dedicated following all over the world. His music has been described as ‘subtle, yet powerful.’ His last album, ‘Silfur’ (2021), was released with the renowned classical music label Deutsche Grammophon.  He’s the winner of an Emmy Award for his main title theme to Amazon’s comedy-drama ‘Transparent,’ and he was nominated for an Oscar, a Golden Globe, a BAFTA, and a Critics Choice Award for his score for 2016’s ‘Lion’ – written in collaboration with Volker Bertelmann. His collaborations across film, dance, and art include artists like Sofia Coppola, Ane Brun, Katy Perry, Leonard Cohen, Wayne McGregor, Slater Bradley, and Jóhann Jóhannsson, among others. More recently, he co-composed ‘The Essex Serpent’ with Herdís Stefánsdóttir and scored the ITVX mini-series ‘A Spy Among Friends.’  ‘1 0 0 1,’ his newest release for Deutsche Grammophon, is an album presented in four movements, an exploration of consciousness and the emerging intelligence we’re crafting.  In late 2024, O’Halloran scored two films back-to-back: Bridget Jones Diary: Mad About the Boy (2025), and Scarlett Johansson's directorial debut Eleanor the Great.

name: still fades
bio: Still Fades combines ambient, electronic and neo-classical influences to craft meditative soundscapes that transport listeners into serene, introspective spaces.  As the founder of SoundGhost, he curates and designs ambient content, helping to inspire the sound of the ambient community.

name: Peter Sandberg
bio: “Even the smallest gesture can shift the course of another’s world”; this is the magical truth that the Swedish composer, pianist and multi-instrumentalist Peter Sandberg has instilled in his new album, Temporary Coexistence of Humans. Each of the thirteen original pieces sketches a profound portrait of one of the many distinct forms of connection that we as humans experience in our everyday lives. Some of these focus on interactions with the world around us—a dance with a stranger or a fleeting moment of affection—while others are more intimate ruminations about self-doubt or identity. Performing on solo piano, Peter Sandberg invites us into the chaotic wonder of humanity and what it means to navigate this world of precarious, yet beautiful, chance. As with his previous recordings, Peter Sandberg developed this project from his studio in Uppsala. His compositional style lies somewhere between stage and cinema, blending classical form and neoclassical minimalism with the storytelling and sentiment of contemporary media. Peter Sandberg has written music featured in seasons three and four of the record-breaking Netflix series Stranger Things, as well as commercials for brands including Volvo, Tesla and Vox. His body of work has amassed more than 500 million streams across digital platforms to date. The journey begins in October 2025 with the first single, followed by more tracks leading up to the full album release on May 1, 2026, via Warner Classics.

name: Louise Spencer
bio: Prominent UK musician and composer Louise Spencer is a classical crossover harpist, pianist and singer, exploring ambient and electronic music. Her collaborations include lofi beats, electronic music, ambient harp soundscapes and orchestral music featuring the harp, as well as her own solo piano and solo harp releases. Hailing from Nottingham, she frequently tours the country and showcases her diverse styles spanning classical, electronic, jazz and pop music.

name: Goldbæk
bio: Goldbæk is a European composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist; a collector of melodies and a curator of emotions. With a myriad of instruments, sounds and production techniques to hand, Goldbæk prefers to focus instead on the stripped-back purity of the piano to express their mastery of melody and mood. Goldbæk’s music ranges from atmospheric, stark and introspective to relaxing, optimistic and other-worldly. Drift away to Goldbæk’s unique sound : piano music to soothe the soul.

name: Jóhann Jóhannsson
bio: One of Iceland's most prolifically creative musicians, composer/producer/multi-instrumentalist Jóhann Jóhannsson blurred the lines between genres -- as well as the boundaries between his solo work, collaborations, and commissioned pieces -- with an organic ease and generosity of spirit. The way he blended classical, electronic, and ambient music (along with hints of indie and metal) complemented his innate gift for storytelling and communicating emotions on works as intimate as his 2002 debut Englabörn and as ambitious as 2008's Fordlandia. Similarly, he gave solo albums such as 2016's Orphée as much narrative depth as his Oscar-nominated music for 2014's The Theory of Everything and 2015's Sicario. In turn, his compositions for smaller films like the 2011 documentary The Miner's Hymns were just as rich as any major motion picture score. Jóhannsson's untimely death in 2018 was a huge loss to music, especially since his final score, Mandy, proved he was still finding new ways of combining powerful moods and innovative sounds. Born in Reykjavik, Iceland, Jóhannsson took piano and trombone lessons as a boy, and began making music in the late '80s. His early projects included the band Daisy Hill Puppy Farm, whose noisy brand of indie took inspiration from the Jesus and Mary Chain and won fans such as John Peel and Steve Albini. He became a fixture of Iceland's indie music scene thanks to his work as a guitarist and as a producer for acts such as Unun. In 1999, Jóhannsson founded the Kitchen Motors label and collective (which also included members of Sigur Rós, Múm, and Slowblow). That year also marked the formation of Apparat Organ Quartet, a group of four keyboardists and a drummer who issued a pair of albums (2002's self-titled album and 2010's Pólýfónía) of self-described "machine rock & roll." These collaborative, genre-bending projects informed Jóhannsson's solo career, which launched with 2002's Englabörn. Based on the music he wrote for a play, its bittersweet miniatures paired a string quartet with percussion, keyboards, and electronics. It set the stage for more expansive works such as 2004's Virðulegu Forsetar, an ambient piece scored for brass, organ, keyboards, and electronics that was composed for and recorded in Reykjavik's Hallgrimskirkja Church. For the following year's Dis, Jóhannsson expanded on the pieces he wrote for the film of the same name and collaborated with friends that included members of Singapore Sling and Slowblow as well as Kitchen Motors' Hilmar Jensson and singer Ragnheidur Grondal, resulting in a work that combined Scandinavian indie with more traditional score elements. Jóhannsson moved to 4AD for two of his most ambitious solo albums. The first installment of a planned trilogy of albums about technology and iconic American brands, 2006's IBM 1401, A User's Manual was inspired by the first computer brought to Iceland in 1964 and based on a recording of an IBM computer's electromagnetic emissions that his father -- one of Iceland's first computer programmers -- made on a reel-to-reel tape recorder. A string quartet version of the work was performed as the accompaniment to a dance piece by choreographer Erna Omarsdórtir at the 2002 Dansem Festival. The recorded version of IBM 1401, A User's Manual incorporated vocalizing, electronics, and a 60-piece orchestra along with the original recordings of the IBM computer. Jóhannsson followed it with 2008's Fordlandia, which used Henry Ford's failed rubber plant in Brazil and engineer/occultist Jack Parsons as inspiration for its soaring compositions. During this time, the composer's commissioned works included the music for the Icelandic TV series Svartir Englar and the 2007 film In the Arms of My Enemy. The soundtrack he composed for the animated film Varmints was sold as And in the Endless Pause There Came the Sound of Bees, a limited-edition, tour-only release. The album was given a wider release the following year on Type Records. Soundtrack work dominated Jóhannsson's schedule for most of the 2010s. In 2011, his music for Bill Morrison's documentary The Miner's Hymns combined electronics, a brass band, and pipe organ. The following year, he left Apparat Organ Quartet and issued Copenhagen Dreams, the score to Max Kestner's documentary about the Danish city. In 2013, he first collaborated with Denis Villeneuve, composing the music for the director's acclaimed thriller Prisoners. Jóhannsson achieved another level of success with his emotional score for 2014's Stephen Hawking biopic The Theory of Everything, which won him a Golden Globe and an Oscar nomination for Best Original Score. The following year, he was once again nominated for a Best Original Score Academy Award for Sicario, his second collaboration with Villeneuve. Jóhannsson worked with the director again on 2016's Arrival. During this time, Jóhannsson directed and composed the music for the Antarctica documentary End of Summer, which also featured Icelandic cellist Hildur Guðnadóttir and Lichens' Robert A.A. Lowe. He also premiered Drone Mass, a contemporary oratorio, at New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art in a 2015 performance that featured the American Contemporary Music Ensemble (ACME) and Roomful of Teeth. Jóhannsson reunited with Guðnadóttir for the BBC TV series Trapped, which won the Best Score award at the 2016 Edda Awards in his native Iceland. That year, the composer also signed with Deutsche Grammophon to release his solo projects. The first of these was Orphée, his first solo studio album in six years. Inspired by several versions of the Orpheus myth -- including French director Jean Cocteau's film -- as well as Jóhannsson's move to Berlin, Orphée arrived in September 2016. Around this time, he began work on the score to Villeneuve's Blade Runner sequel Blade Runner 2049, but the director decided that the film needed something different musically and recruited Hans Zimmer and Benjamin Wallfisch to finish the score. Jóhannsson also wrote a score to Darren Aronofsky's 2017 film Mother! that went unused, but he was credited as a music and sound consultant. Shortly after the release of his score to James Marsh's sailing drama The Mercy in February 2018, Jóhannsson died in Berlin from heart failure at age 48. His final scores arrived later that year: Mary Magdalene, another collaboration with Guðnadóttir, appeared in March. The music to Panos Cosmatos' revenge film Mandy, which featured contributions from Sunn O)))'s Stephen O'Malley and producer Randall Dunn, had been recorded at the time of Jóhannsson's death but was assembled into its final form by co-producers Pepijn Caudron and Yair Glotman for its September 2018 release. That year also saw the launch of the Jóhann Jóhannsson Foundation, a non-profit organization dedicated to connecting music students with creators, scholarship grants, and music education programs. ~ Heather Phares, Rovi

name: Jonas Colstrup
bio: At The Crest - album out on 7k!   Jonas Colstrup is a Danish composer and musician. Visit jonascolstrup.com for more info.

name: Goldmund
bio: A Pennsylvanian by birth, Keith Kenniff is an honors graduate of Boston’s esteemed Berklee College of Music, best known as the ambient/electronic practitioner Helios and post-classical piano minimalist music as Goldmund (the latter’s music once described by no less an authority than Ryuichi Sakamoto as “…so, so, so beautiful…”). Together with his wife Hollie, Keith also records as Mint Julep, and the two released their debut album “Save Your Season” which NME coined as “Unquestionably Beautiful”. A succession of albums under those aliases has made Kenniff the darling of discerning critics and his music has been widely used in film, tv and advertising, for clients such as Apple, Facebook, Google, Paramount, MTV and Warner Brothers.  Licensing inquiry? Please visit www.unseen-music.com or email keith@unseen-music.com

bio: A Pennsylvanian by birth, Keith Kenniff is an honors graduate of Boston’s esteemed Berklee College of Music, best known as the brains behind dulcet ambient/electronic practitioner Helios and post-classical piano minimalist music as Goldmund (the latter’s music once described by no less an authority than Ryuichi Sakamoto as “…so, so, so beautiful…”).
