name: SAGES
bio: SAGES are Ólafur Arnalds & Loreen Full EP out now!

name: Ólafur Arnalds
bio: Ólafur Arnalds is a BAFTA-award winning artist and musician from Iceland, celebrated for his haunting musical style, combining ambient, classical and electronic music. Ólafur's five solo albums and his numerous other projects and collaborative albums, including electronic duo Kiasmos with Janus Rasmussen, have garnered immense praise and cemented his place as one of the most influential composers of modern times.   Ólafur’s career is full of milestones, including three Grammy nominations for his 2020 album, some kind of peace. Ólafur has also been praised for his extensive soundtrack work, including the Emmy-nominated main theme for Defending Jacob and Broadchurch, for which he won the 2014 BAFTA for Best Original Music.   Collaboration and exploration play a big role in Ólafur’s work: His extensive work with Nils Frahm; SAGES, a collaborative project with Swedish artist Loreen – and the album A Dawning, a collaboration with the late Irish musician Talos, finished by Ólafur after his passing. Furthermore, Ólafur enforces collaborations through his record label/travelling festival series/community hub, OPIA Community, which serves as a space for curiosity, connection and creativity to thrive.  Ólafur’s live performances are captivating, often unorthodox and have sold out many of the most prestigious live venues in the world, including The Royal Albert Hall, Sydney Opera Hall, Walt Disney Concert Hall and Elbphilharmonie.

name: Loreen
bio: Loreen’s massive breakthrough with Euphoria is still to this day considered as one of the most memorable performances in Eurovision Song Contest history where she single-handedly helped shift the perception of Eurovision. Earlier this year, Loreen once again spellbound viewers around the world, this time with her extraordinary performance of “Tattoo”, making history as the first woman—and only second person ever—to win the Eurovision Song Contest twice.  Besides her artistry, Loreen is known & appreciated around the world for her warm and down-to-earth approach, with messages of love & inclusion shining through everything she does. For her, trusting her intuition is more important than following what's been done before, which leads her down a creative path less traveled, resulting in an artistry infused with spirituality and her nomadic heritage.  Loreen’s sound sphere will take you on a journey, pop inspired by her Berber roots with touches of dance influences that leaves her sound to a truly unique experience.

name: Martin Martyn
bio: "Martin Martyn" is a collective formed by two close friends - Hideyuki Hashimoto & Yuri Kawai, bound together by a deep connection. With a unique blend of the piano, synthesizers, and beats, they craft a powerful sound that evokes a wild, symbiotic relationship with nature. The piano solos are often created as a musical diary of their journeys, while the synths and beats serve as a medium for self-expression and introspection. Based in Japan yet recording across Europe, they continue to share their music with the world. Born out of a year of improvisational sessions, the duo’s shared passion for music naturally led to the creation of this project. With a focus on the beauty of music they both feel deeply, their sound evolves and expands with every new creation.

name: Simon Bächinger
bio: Swiss pianist and composer Simon Bächinger crafts intimate neoclassical and ambient piano music shaped by a uniquely modified Steinway and a deeply personal sonic vision. Blending classical virtuosity with subtle electronics, improvisation and modern production aesthetics, he creates immersive sound worlds for listeners of contemporary post classical music.  His musical path began early. At the age of twelve he performed a Mozart piano concerto with orchestra and received several awards, laying the foundation for his deep connection to the classical tradition.  Working from his own studio equipped with boutique microphones, Bächinger has developed a warm and emotionally close piano sound. Grammy Award winning mastering engineer Bob Katz described one of his recordings as “the most unique piano recording I have ever worked with.” His music often emerges from late night improvisations and explores the fragile boundary between acoustic purity and electronic texture.  Alongside his artistic work, he serves as a lecturer at the Zurich University of the Arts. Releases such as Nana Bianca and Brooklyn Lights place him among a new generation of European neoclassical artists redefining the modern piano landscape.

name: Kenzo Zurzolo
bio: Kenzo Zurzolo is a Paris-based composer whose debut album Hellissandur marks a powerful step into his own voice. After more than a decade of touring and collaborating with other artists, he now turns inward, offering a sound that is both personal and expansive.  Written between the quiet landscapes of southern France and the titular Icelandic town, Hellissandur  blends upright piano, vintage synths, and layered strings into something reflective and atmospheric; It’s music shaped by solitude, nature, and a deep listening practice.  The result is a sound that is rooted in classical tradition but reaching toward something timeless.  For Kenzo, music is a form of mindfulness. His compositions aren’t just meant to be heard - they’re meant to be felt, deeply. Hellissandur invites you to step outside the noise and into a space that is both intimate and euphoric.

name: AAESPO
bio: AAESPO is Aaron Esposito.   Raised in New York, based in Los Angeles.  Aaron Esposito is a multi-instrumentalist who enjoys building diverse soundscapes using minimal instrumentation. As a classically trained trumpet/flugelhorn player, he has developed a unique musical language built on the vocal qualities and fluidity of wind instruments. Inspired by masters of craft, AAESPO cultivates this intentionality through his work; focusing on the pursuit of curiosity and discovery.  Equal parts composer and session musician, Aaron’s influences are diverse. His work can be heard on numerous film scores, tv shows, podcasts, commercials, and albums alike.  aaespo.com

name: Leo Einaudi
bio: Immensely creative across broad musical fields including cinema, theatre, multimedia and live performance, Leo Einaudi follows a lineage stemming from contemporary piano and classical composition and expanding across guitar instrumentals and songwriting as founder of indie folk group Caveleon. From his family home in Milan, Leo developed his skills in collaboration with his father Ludovico Einaudi on a wealth of record-breaking projects while also progressing his own dynamic sound encompassing classical scoring through intimate tones and powerful evolving waves, rock-influenced electronic tone poems and cinematic songscapes with guitar tones and moody vocals. His adaptive style is sometimes reminiscent of Radiohead and Maribou State, sometimes inhabiting the realm of contemporary classical crossover, sometimes with the subtle songwriting influences of The Beatles and sometimes something totally different. A musical polymath: Leo Einaudi.

name: Aldwin
bio: The compositions by Aldwin resonate with an array positive feelings. Meditational; as classical music can force you to step off that proverbial train, but these pieces are also arranged as true songs from head to tail. Recorded with a detailed close mic setup in an acoustically advantageous room; you can hear the smooth crackles of the Steinberg piano and the vibrating strings filling up the space. Proudly part of the Morning Classicallabel; sounds like Challem, Bettiol, and Arundo.

name: Julien Marchal
bio: What emotion does a pianist seek to create? "Ecstasy", answers Julien Marchal. A style that the 38-year-old chisels into his classical compositions with atmospheric variations. As a student, he studied musicology in Bordeaux . There, learning harmony was like an epiphany: "I felt like I was learning to write all over again. As if I had the power to materialize the impalpable." In 2014, he recorded his first original quartet for strings and piano, clearing the neo-classical furrow. The following year, this formed the basis of Insight, the pianist's very first album, followed in 2016 by INSIGHT II.  Since his career started, Julien Marchal has shown an unprecedented eclecticism. He works with renowned electronic music producers such as Robot Koch and Steve Aoki. His music animates American series such as How to Get Away With Murder, Ray Donovan and Blacklist. And with British pop singer Ed Tulett, he composed the duo Lissom, celebrated in particular by multi-platinum singer Billie Eilish. For the forthcoming release of his fifth album, Julien Marchal chose to team up with naïve. "Right from the start, I had the feeling that we were working together as a team. I feel we're listening to my new desires", he stresses. With INSIGHT V, the chord lines that were the lifeblood of his four previous opuses are suddenly deconstructed. But under the felt of INSIGHT V's harmony, one feeling returns again and again: ecstasy.

name: Vulax
bio: Le plus grand pianiste français (1m91).

name: Housman
bio: Housman is a project by British composer Luke Faulkner exclusively for the release of Dark Academia aesthetic piano music. Everyone is welcome to use this music in reels for Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts. Thanks for listening!

name: James Malikey
bio: James Malikey is a pianist, composer and nature photographer. James composes and performs relaxing, emotional and cinematic music. Nature, emotions, imagination and experiences within this society are the most important sources of inspiration for him.   "There are only black and white keys, but the challenge is to play all colors in between."  James started playing the piano at the age of 4. As a classical trained pianist, he won several prizes in piano contests.  But at the age of 15, due to his difficult youth, he discovered his passion for creating his own music, to process and express emotions. In 2019, he won Belgiums Got Talent with his own compositions.  “My music is a key to enter a Different World.”  As much as music helped him, James wants to inspire and help many others with his music. He wants to offer you a Different World, a world where you can calm down and give place to difficulties, but also to beautiful memories, dreams and fantasies. A world of love, light and freedom.  He wants to create that world in this reality too.  In 2022, he made a journey through Europe to connect people at the streets with his music. He also performed at the streets in LA, and for the many homeless people there, giving them water, food, music.   "I cherish the moments they told me my music made their day better, bearable."   James began performing international concerts in 2025 and will continue doing so in 2026, alongside his daily piano livestreams and time in nature.

name: Federico Albanese
bio: Federico Albanese is a genre-defying Italian musician, composer, multi-instrumentalist, and producer. His musical versatility is a natural gift that pushes him to explore music in all its facets. Federico's new album entitled "Blackbirds and the Sun of October" is coming on February 7, 2025, and it will be released by Sony's new innovative, cross-genres label imprint XXIM. Albanese's cinematic instrumental tracks, struck an instant chord for their airy, meditative beauty. Released in February 2014, his highly acclaimed debut solo album The Houseboat and the Moon has been described as “one of the most beautiful modern classical albums of the past years”. Albanese’s sophomore equally acclaimed album The Blue Hour saw the light of the day on January 15, 2016. Albanese’s third full-lenght By the Deep Sea was released on February 23rd, 2018. Albanese's 4th studio album Before And Now Seems Infinite was released on February 25, 2022 by Universal Music Group’s imprint Mercury KX, including collaboration with british artists Ghostpoet and Marika Hackman. Albanese is known internationally for his intense touring activity, that over the years lead him to perform hundreds of solo concerts and festivals across the world including Womad (UK), Montreux Jazz Festival (CH) and the Elbphilarmonie in Hamburg, touching countries such as Australia, Canada and Iran. In 2023, he scored director Sasha Nathwani's debut film "Last Swim", which won the Crystal Bear at the 74th Berlinale.

name: Eleri Morgan
bio: Thank you for listening to my music!!!  My name is Eleri and I'm a composer living on the Isle of Man, a small island in the Irish Sea.  I love to make music that creates moments of calm and also to help unwind ahead of sleep! The piano is my go to instrument for this.  My compositions are neo-classical, and a fusion of electronic and orchestral. Conveying vast soundscapes, compositions are multi-textured and layered to create ambience and timelessness.  Music is a joy to make, and I hope you will enjoy my creations! Eleri  More information about my music:  I'm very grateful to the production teams who have selected my music for BBC radio shows and streams. This has been a highlight of my music career.  Shows my music has been on include: BBC Radio 3 In-Tune in 2021  BBC Radio Lancashire and Cumbria - BBC Introducing BBC Sleeping Forecast BBC Piano Focus BBC 3 Night Tracks BBC Classical Windown BBC Soundwaves BBC 3 Unwind  The local IOM Arts Council commissioned me for music for a dance short film, "Sollys".  Film premiered on 23 March 2023. www.youtube.com/watch?v=izE8bAoFNB0 I provided pro-bono help to the Manx Wildlife Trust, a local charity, with the music and music edit for their soundtrack of their short film 'Wildlife Remembered' This premiered in April 2024. www.youtube.com/watch?v=OjHNTuOdg8M  "Sundays", appears on the 2021 Piano day playlist by Nils Frahm. My arrangement of the "Manx National Anthem" appears on the Manx Music SoundCloud playlist by Culture Vannin.

name: Nora
bio: Nora's music is sentimental and understated, allowing the listener to reflect upon his pieces in their own time. Recorded in a way that makes the pieces even more intimate and delicate, they feel nostalgic.

name: Dalal
bio: Hi, I’m Dalal.   A composer and musician living in Los Angeles. I was born in a small town in Austria, where I started playing piano and violin when I was four and music has been my gentle compass in the world ever since.    My early love for music took me from Vienna’s concert halls to new experiences in London, New York, and Los Angeles—and in each place, I’ve gathered something that stayed with me.   I often experience music in colors. It’s a sort of soft, sensory paintbrush that lets me trace my feelings across soundscapes in a way words can’t touch.  When I’m not lost in my own world of sound, I team up with my brilliant partner-in-music, Maesa Pullman. Together, we score films and TV shows, often adding our own vocals into the mix to give our musical landscapes a very human touch.   My little sonic space here is both personal and shared - and as you wander through my catalogue I hope it offers you a place to feel, breathe, and connect.

name: Justus Rümenapp
bio: Music is my language to express emotions, and I’m truly happy you discovered my work here on Spotify.  I recently released my new album Le Journal Intime together with the wonderful Deutsches Filmorchester Babelsberg. Following my previous album Forest of Memories, the journey through nature continues with my upcoming Album „Symphony For The Future“.  My inspirations come from nature, personal life experiences, and, of course, my beloved Bösendorfer grand piano. Beyond my solo works, I also love composing soundtracks for cinematic films.  For more insights into my music and creative journey, feel free to visit my Instagram or website.  Thank you for listening to my music here @Spotify. Stay safe and stay tuned! 🎹  Justus   Website: www.justus-ruemenapp.de

name: Alexander B. A. Pielsticker
bio: Alexander B. A. Pielsticker is a musical chameleon, composing and producing music in a lot of different styles. At the age of fourteen, Alexander began composing while growing up with classical music on the piano and discovering the freedom of music in jazz and improvised music. Having achieved two Bachelor of Music degrees at the ArtEZ University of the Arts in Arnhem (The Netherlands), he is now following up his studies with the Master of Music program to focus on his unique and individual language as a pianist and composer. At the start of 2024 Alexander had the opportunity to perform with the famous Beethoven Orchester in Bonn. In addition to his solo project, Alexander also performs with his big band at the ArtEZ University of the Arts, having played at the famous North Sea Jazz festival in Rotterdam (The Netherlands). Furthermore he toured with different bands through various countries in Europe and is part of the jazz trio Lanzensticker, experimental international jazz trio 3HOKB and Cologne-based musical collective Lind·Froot, which supports the musical upbringing in low-income countries all over the world.

name: Thomas Gould
bio: Violinist Thomas Gould is a versatile figure who plays electric violin as well as the conventional instrument, and jazz as well as classical music. He is co-leader of the Britten Sinfonia. Gould was born in 1983 in London. His older sister, Clio Gould, 15 years older, is the leader of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra and the London Sinfonietta, and it was she who inspired him to become a violinist. Gould attended the Royal Academy of Music from age 16, studying with György Pauk, and in 2009, he was named an Associate of the school. His name began to spread more widely, and in 2011, he toured with the Australian Chamber Orchestra. He performed with the Aurora Orchestra, playing Nico Muhly's Seeing Is Believing on a six-string electric violin and giving the world premiere recording of the work that year on the Decca label, and he served as director of the Aurora Orchestra in the 2010s. Gould made his debut with the Los Angeles Philharmonic in 2012, in a concert conducted by John Adams, and he has since appeared with major orchestras in Britain, the U.S., and beyond, including the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, the Hallé Orchestra, and the Riga Sinfonietta. He has played chamber music with the Nash Ensemble and other groups. Gould often plays jazz at London's Ronnie Scott's Jazz Club, and he has collaborated with jazz, rock, and pop musicians, including Brad Mehldau, Radiohead, and Rufus Wainwright. For a time, he was a member of the swing quintet Man Overboard. In the early 2010s, Gould became the leader of the Britten Sinfonia; he continues to serve in that position as co-leader with Jacqueline Shave. Gould made his recording debut in 2009, performing the violin concerto of Christopher Ball on the Omnibus album Celtic Twilight. He has recorded for various labels, including Harmonia Mundi, Albion, and Champs Hill, where his 2014 album Bach to Parker reflected the multiplicity of his musical interests. In 2021, Gould appeared on the second of a pair of recordings of folk song-oriented music by Ralph Vaughan Williams on Albion.

name: Matthew Sharp
bio: 'Virtuoso of the arts' (The Times), Matthew Sharp, has performed worldwide as solo cellist, baritone, actor and director - solo appearances with the RPO, LPO, RLPO, CBSO; singing principal roles for Opera North and ROH; acting principal roles at the Young Vic and NT Studio. From Glastonbury to Glyndebourne, he has worked with an extraordinary spectrum of leading artists from Sir John Tavener to Marta Eggert to Dave McKean to Caryl Churchill. His own music and theatre works have toured to major festivals globally. He has given over sixty world premieres and recorded for Sony, EMI, Decca, Naxos, Somm, NMC, Avie and Whirlwind. www.matthewsharp.net

name: Martin Hoper
bio: Bassplayer and composer Martin Höper is based in Stockholm, Sweden and plays frequently with many of the top jazz artists in Sweden.

name: Ivory Soul Trio
bio: Ivory Soul Trio featuring the pianist Axel Mason writes warm, melodic jazz with melodies that stays after the room goes quiet. The music is built for slow mornings, late evenings and the spaces in between.

name: Tiles Square
bio: Deep house in clean geometry. Architectural lines, steady focus, with a pulse. Step in to my sub-bass office.

name: Taki Brano
bio: Taki Brano, aka The Sound Bender has been a professional music producer since 2016.   Worldwide and at any given moment, someone is listening to a Taki Brano song.  His substantial streaming activity across digital platforms reflects the reach of his work. More broadly, his career exists at the intersection of music, community, and digital culture. His practice extends beyond entertainment, using sound as a medium for collaboration, creative exchange, and interpersonal connection.  Find out more at takibrano.com❤️

name: 13pm
bio: Lofi hip hop psychedelic instrumentals.  Boston, MA

name: Lumin
bio: Just a small collective of house lovers making music for house lovers. Whether it’s a late night drink or chilling at the pool, we’ve got you.

name: Theo Juarez
bio: Theo Juarez is a versatile trumpet player/producer forming his own path in the lo-fi scene, taking simple concepts and putting them together with his own brand of soulfulness. With him reaching new milestones, Theo continues to expand on the genre while staying committed to his own sound.   His sounds is derived from listening to jazz legends, modern RnB and hip hop as well as OG’s in the lo-fi scene. The goal for Theo Juarez is very simple. “I want people to listen to my music.”

name: Carlton Ranks
bio: Bel-Air academy proudly presents.

name: makers mask
bio: A refuge in resonance.   Based out of Los Angeles, Makers Mask creates music to comfort, and quiet the mind.   Socials:  https://www.instagram.com/makers.mask https://www.tiktok.com/@makers.mask  Email: makersmaskmusic@gmail.com

name: Hello Papyrus
bio: hello. i like to daydream about sunsets and make house music.

name: Bishop Juice
bio: Harlem, New York. 1992 To Infinity.

name: Far Orange
bio: For composer and multi instrumentalist Gunnar Johnsén, music has been integral to his life for as far back as he can remember. With over 10 years experience playing drums in punk bands, touring internationally, and recording records, Gunnar’s taste and skill shines through his production.   His diverse electronic beats combine feel good melodies and echoing harmonic progressions over chest thumping drums. Contagiously upbeat, Gunnar’s music is uniquely original and transfixing for his nearly quarter million monthly listeners. With several million streams to date, Gunnar is excited to be able to collaborate with other musicians as he continues to release music and grow his international fan base.

name: Faux Facet
bio: The best ideas find me while driving. There’s a rhythm in my car—though, honestly, it probably just needs a service.

name: Annelie
bio: The new album Sunne is out now. Derived from the Old English word for Sun. The theme of the record is deeply connected to being outdoors, traveling, and life on the road, as well as the changing climate. Elements like heat, drought, water, and wind played an important role. At the same time, there is a sense of nostalgia and melancholy—a longing for the past, or certain childhood memories that have influenced the musical identity behind this album. At home, the garden cabin was finally transformed into a functional workspace for writing and recording. For the first time, the process of producing and recording independently became a reality. New synthesizers were acquired, a high-quality microphone was added to the setup, and countless hours—especially during late summer nights—were spent crafting the music. The experience often felt like solving a puzzle, but it offered an extraordinary sense of freedom. Her previous piano solo albums, 'After Midnight' (2018) and 'Hertz' (2021), were widely acclaimed and have nearly reached 50 million streams on Spotify alone. However, on her subsequent EP called 'C', she wanted to showcase more diversity and experiment with electronic elements. After releasing her much anticipated album 'Sunne' in 2025, she's maintaining momentum by releasing stripped down versions of her albumtracks, as well as releasing new work. Stay tuned for new music, and follow This Is Annelie.

name: Gibran Alcocer
bio: Gibran Alcocer, a 22-year-old pianist, composer, and producer hailing from Yucatán, Mexico, has been immersed in music since childhood. He kicked off his musical journey by taking piano lessons, eventually diving into classical music studies. His knack for composition and production emerged at the tender age of 12. In 2021, he hopped onto the TikTok bandwagon, gaining recognition for his piano cover performances. By early 2022, he ventured into crafting instrumental tunes. Come July 2022, he dropped his debut original track "Idea 10", a solo piano piece entirely composed, produced, and performed by himself. It quickly made waves across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.   Gibran Alcocer es un pianista compositor y productor mexicano de 22 años originario de Yucatán, que ha estado inmerso en la música desde pequeño. Comenzó su viaje musical tomando lecciones de piano y finalmente continuo con estudios de música clásica. Su don para la composición y la producción surgió a la edad de 12 años. En 2021 inicio en la plataforma de TikTok donde se hizo conocido por sus interpretaciones de versiones al piano. A principios de 2022 se aventuró a componer música instrumental. En Julio de 2022, lanzó su primera canción original "Idea 10", un solo de piano compuesta, producida e interpretada por el mismo, la cual rápidamente obtuvo un amplio reconocimiento en plataformas como Tiktok, Instagram y YouTube.  Website: www.gibranalcocer.com Contact: music.gibranalcocer@gmail.com

name: Luna Acantha
bio: Born and based in Norway, Luna Acantha is a composer, self-taught pianist, guitarist and clarinet player. Her undying love for not only classical music, but also ancient art, literature and poetry, shapes her work on the piano today. With a versatile and unique style, she tends to make songs sound like an ancient novel. Sometimes heavy and nostalgic, sometimes bright and down-to-earth.   She seamlessly blends diverse dark and mysterious sounds with techniques that can best be described as comfortably airy. Her touch is always genuinely poetic.   Luna grew up in a musical family with her dad being a concert pianist and her mom conducting a pop choir. Luna herself became enamored with the piano at the age of 5 when she first attended one of her dad’s piano concerts. She then relentlessly started to play the piano herself as often as she could.   Sapere aude (Dare to know) is Luna’s guiding principle. Luna finds inspiration in all that’s hidden. In addition to sharing her music, she is also dedicated to finding out as much about the Unknown as possible.

name: Karen LeFrak
bio: A native New Yorker, Karen LeFrak is a prolific and versatile composer and author whose vibrant, moving musical scores have been presented in prestigious concert halls around the world. Highlights of her career include 22 studio albums, which have garnered more than 70 million global streams, a catalog of over 300 works, and worldwide performances by prominent organizations including the New York Philharmonic, National Symphony Orchestra, Shanghai Symphony Orchestra, San Francisco Ballet, and Mariinsky Ballet. She has also received accolades for her children’s books, which are published by Bloomsbury and Crown Books for Young Readers, an imprint of Random House.  In the Moment, Ms. LeFrak’s latest solo instrumental recording, marks the sixteenth release in a series of highly successful solo piano albums, recorded by pianist Jacques van Tuinen. Each album features 10 short, atmospheric piano pieces that have been included in hundreds of curated playlists on Spotify, Pandora, Apple Music, and other streaming services. During the 2026-27 season, Ms. LeFrak will release three notable albums featuring chamber ensembles and solo piano.

name: Juan Arenosa
bio: Juan Arenosa is a 22-year-old pianist and composer born in Santander (Spain). From a very young age, he showed a strong interest in music and the arts. He began studying classical piano at the age of five with his mother and grandmother, and at eight he wrote his first piano composition. From that moment on, Juan never stopped composing and performing. After completing his professional studies at the conservatory, in 2021 he began publishing piano videos on TikTok, where he currently has 1.7 million followers. Recently, he released his piano collaboration with Gibran Alcocer, “Oblivion”.

name: Triosence
bio: „The new faces of German Jazz“  This is how the German magazine stern referred to triosence, the trio formed in 1999 by Bernhard Schüler (piano), Omar Rodriguez Calvo (bass) and Tobias Schulte (drums).  Since their debut album, “First Enchantment”, released in 2002, triosence has been praised by the music press all around the world. The trio has been acclaimed as one of the most successful jazz imports and as “the piano trio that changed our impression of the ‘stiff German jazz’.” ¹   triosence has performed all over the world, with tours in Germany, the United States, Brazil, Japan, Taiwan, Malaysia, France, Spain, Norway, The Netherlands, Turkey, Lebanon, Romania, Albania and many more. Over the years they have created their own fresh and unique style from a combination of Jazz, Fusion, Folk and World Music. Because they emphasize melody and focus on the essence of the song as their trademark, the trio has labeled their music songjazz. The name, triosence (neologism derived from trio-essence) refers to the approach of equality of instruments. The result is music that connects with a variety of audiences, from pure jazz fans to those who haven’t found themselves among jazz listeners before.   1)	Swing Journal Japan

name: John Lenehan
bio: With more than 70 albums to his credit, reflecting an enormous variety of genres and styles, John Lenehan ranks as one of the most versatile pianists on the classical scene today.  As a soloist he has appeared with orchestras such as the London Symphony at the Barbican and the Royal Philharmonic in the Royal Albert Hall.   His many recordings include piano recitals and concertos as well as duo sonatas, chamber music and jazz. A four-disc survey of John Ireland’s piano music received great critical acclaim including a Gramophone award, and other solo recordings include three discs for Sony Classical of minimalist piano works and a disc of Erik Satie (for Classic FM). Most recently he has recorded albums with Tasmin Little and the Rossetti Ensemble as well as concertos by Mozart (K.467) and Beethoven (Emperor) with the National Symphony Orchestra.  John Lenehan also composes, with works published by Faber, Novello and Schotts.   His Fantasy on Tchaikovsky’s Nutcracker has recently been recorded by the Budapest Symphony Orchestra. He has written and arranged for a long list of soloists and orchestras including Nigel Kennedy, Tasmin Little, Nicola Benedetti, Leonidas Kavakos and Yuja Wang, the BBC Concert Orchestra, RPO and Hong Kong Philharmonic and for the Bastille Day celebrations in Paris (Orchestre de Paris) and the last night of the proms (BBC SO) – both in 2021. His most recent work is a piano concerto to be premiered in China in 2022.

name: Maxence Cyrin
bio: French pianist and composer Maxence Cyrin returns with PRESAGE, his new album for Warner Classics, due for release on 26 February 2027, with a first single arriving this autumn.  Built around ten original pieces, PRESAGE brings together solo piano, cello duets, trio and string orchestra. Moving from simple, repetitive motifs to long melodic lines, the album gives the strings an increasingly central role, creating a dialogue in which the piano can lead, recede and re-emerge.  Cyrin first gained international recognition with Novö Piano (2010), an album reimagining iconic songs from pop culture for solo piano. His version of the Pixies’ “Where Is My Mind?” received a triple Diamond export certification in France and was featured in numerous films and television series, including The Leftovers and Mr. Robot.  Since joining Warner Classics with Aurora, Cyrin has increasingly focused on his own compositions, notably with Melancholy Island (2022) and Springsong (2023). With PRESAGE, piano and strings come together on a larger scale, opening a new chapter in his work as a composer.  Contact – Enchanté Records : tastet.christophe@gmail.com

name: Joe Bridges
bio: Joe Bridges is a British composer. He writes music for film and television, and is the ‘BRiDGeS’ half of the music duo GRNBRDGS.

name: Mira
bio: Mira is a French pianist, composer, and content creator signed to Warner Classics. She’s crafting a world that is raw, emotional, and unapologetically honest. Her music isn’t about perfection: it’s about feeling. No distractions, no excess, just melodies that speak, resonate, and heal. Growing up, Mira often felt different, isolated, and misunderstood. The piano became her sanctuary, a place where emotions could take shape through sound. Her music is an open door into that inner world. Intimate and deeply personal, it was born from a need to express what words never could.

name: Jamal Green
bio: Jamal Green is a British composer currently based in the UK. His unique sound finds its way into everything he works on from BAFTA Award Winning TOEM (2021) by Something We Made to Konami Digital Entertainment's flagship release Skelattack (2020)Jamal is a highly praised and celebrated composer, having been selected as a 2022/23 BAFTA Breakthrough and featured in Sony Masterworks & Milan Records BLACK MUSIC MONTH celebration alongside 5 world class composers including Labrinth and Terence Blanchard.His music is also currently featured on 15,000+ playlists including 3 Spotify Editorial playlists (The Most Beautiful Songs in the World, The Wind Down, Lost In The Woods) as well as 5 FILTR (Sony Music Entertainment) playlists from the USA, Germany and France.To tie in with the release of Skelattack's soundtrack Jamal was invited to create a "takeover" playlist to feature on official PlayStation™Music Spotify account - Skelattack: Songs That inspired Jamal Green's Score.Konami Digital Entertainment also partnered with MONDO to create a special edition and standard edition 2xLP Vinyl release for the Soundtrack.

name: George Hart
bio: Born into a musical family, composer/multi instrumentalist George Hart was exposed to an eclectic mix of both live and recorded music almost immediately. With five pianists in the family, it’s no accident that the piano became central to his musical universe. He was making early efforts in composition for the instrument by the time he was six years old. Gravitating towards the drums, this became his first instrument, although the piano was never discarded. Gaining a scholarship entry to the Royal Academy of Music as a jazz drummer, he graduated with first class honours before embarking upon a professional career which still continues. This has garnered him a wealth of experience across many genres, the highlight perhaps being touring the world with Swing Out Sister. He is now resident in London and composing a large body of beautiful new piano works for the Karma Sounds Piano collection.

name: Jøsefine
bio: 🌼🌼🌼  Hi,  I'm better with music than I am with words (or worse with words than I am with music), so I'll keep this one short. Making music behind the piano has been the most essential part of my life for as long as I can remember.    All of this I owe to my wonderful parents, who've stimulated all of their children to follow their passions and never stop dreaming.   I invite you to listen to my dreams here.  I hope they make your days a little brighter and your nights a little warmer.  Much love,  J  🌼🌼🌼

name: Taichi Chishaki
bio: Taichi Chishaki is a composer, pianist from Tokyo, Japan. He started playing the piano at the age of 6. When he was young, he had many opportunities to come into contact with Japanese traditional music through "Noh" (a form of Japanese traditional theater) which his grandfather performed. He started composing classical music at the age of 18 and entered Tokyo University of the Arts. In college, he produced contemporary classical music and was also involved in film music. He can write anything from piano pieces to orchestral pieces. From 2021, he started releasing his own piano pieces on various music platforms. In composing, he places the most importance on simple melodies and sound reverberations, and specializes in works that incorporate classical music composition methods. In 2023, "Harmonism I" was released under the label of "1631 Recordings". He is influenced by L.V.Beethoven, D.Shostakovich, and Ryuichi Sakamoto.  東京出身。作曲家、ピアニスト。6歳からピアノを、18歳の時に作曲を始める。東京藝術大学音楽学部作曲科卒業。小さい頃、祖父が「能」を学んでいたため、日本の伝統音楽を身近に聴きながら育った。18歳からクラシック音楽の作曲を始め、大学時代は現代クラシック音楽を主に制作、映像音楽にも携わっていた。ピアノ作品からオーケストラ作品まで幅広く作曲する。2021年から自身のピアノ曲をリリースし始める。単純な旋律と音の響きを作曲する上での主題にしており、クラシック音楽の作曲法を取り入れた作品を得意とする。2023年、1631Recordingsから「Harmonism Ⅰ」を発表。影響を受けた作曲家はベートーベン、ショスタコービッチ、坂本龍一である。

name: Oliver Davis
bio: Composer Oliver Davis has parlayed a long record as a composer of film and television scores into a successful career as a composer of orchestral scores that, in performance, have attracted top-notch London orchestras and soloists. He has also been active as a composer of ballet and has released highly successful albums under his own name. Davis was born in the U.K. in 1972. He attended the Royal Academy of Music, studying composition with Justin Connolly and graduating in 1994. Among Davis' extensive television credits is one for a sequence in the "Diggs" episode of season 25 of The Simpsons, a riff on the series' venerable couch gag that has been viewed on a streaming video service more than six million times. He has written 12 television series soundtracks and music for 15 short films, two major British films for television, and soundtracks for feature films in Britain (The Ringer) and the U.S. (An Unkindness of Ravens and Sleepwalk with Me). Davis has also written songs, including one called Song for Malala, both for and independently of dramatic productions. His ballet scores, executed as part of collaborations with choreographer Erico Montes, include the well-reviewed Within the Hours. Davis began to gain widespread exposure in 2015 with the release of the album Flight, featuring his music as recorded by violinist Kerenza Peacock and the London Symphony Orchestra. The release was named Featured Album of the Week on Britain's popular Classic FM radio network, gained wide radio airplay in many countries, and cracked top levels on both British and U.S. classical sales charts. A selection of pieces from the album, which does not fit easily into the categories of crossover, minimalist, or neo-Romantic, was made into the ballet Flight of Fancy and performed in 2016 by the Tulsa Ballet in the state of Oklahoma. The album spawned the equally successful Seasons, which includes songs based on the sonnets depicted by Vivaldi's Four Seasons violin concertos. A third album in the series, Liberty, appeared in early 2018. Davis has continued to issue albums under his own name, mostly with the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, on the Signum Classics label. These have included Arcadia (2019), Solace (2021, with the Budapest Scoring Orchestra), Air (2022), and Blue (2023). ~ James Manheim, Rovi

name: Fabrizio Paterlini
bio: Fabrizio Paterlini (born in 1973) is an Italian pianist and composer from Mantua, a small and nice town in Italy, where he lives with his family. He released his first album for piano solo back in 2007 (Viaggi in aeromobile) and since then, his music started to travel around the globe. After exploring the piano solo with several works (Viandanze in 2008, Fragments Found in 2010, Autumn Stories in 2012 and The Art of the Piano in 2014). In 2013 he released "Now", his first attempt to combine piano with electronics and in 2017 he published his latest Secret Book, his most composite album so far. Piano, strings and electronics blend together in a new and interesting formula that brings Fabrizio's music to new unexplored paths. In February 2018, he released his first piano solo album, since four years: Winter Stories, presented to the audience by recording and streaming on all his social channels one song per day during the week from Feb 12th to Feb 17th. In 2020, he released his "Transitions" trilogy project which consist in three EP with songs lasting around 1 minute long. In February 2021, he released "Life", followed by "LifeBlood" in April, his latest full album released so far. On Oct 6th, 2023 he released "Riverscape", a collaborative project between Fabrizio and the Dutch photographer Kristel Schneider. On November 14th 2025, he released "Layers" a joint project between Fabrizio and the string duo LoopArc.

name: Jacob Mühlrad
bio: JACOB MÜHLRAD is a celebrated Swedish art music composer, born 1991, who has rapidly emerged as one of the most recognizable composers in Europe. Mühlrad's debut album on Deutsche Grammophon, Time, received a 5-star BBC Music Magazine review. He’s been described as "one of the world's  most imaginative orchestral composers".  Mühlrad has collaborated with musicians such as Martin Fröst, Olga Neuwirth, Matthias Pintscher, and Pablo Heras-Casado, and has received major commissions and been performed by institutions including Radio France, the Swedish Radio Symphony Orchestra, and the Tokyo Symphony Orchestra.  He works fluidly across genres, collaborating with Swedish House Mafia, Anyma, and 070 Shake. His track One Symphony with Swedish House Mafia shook both electronic and classical music circles. In 2024, he collaborated with Anyma on an immersive multimedia show at the Sphere in Las Vegas. That same year, he co-wrote, co-produced, and played piano on two tracks from 070 Shake’s album Petrichor: “Sin”and “Blood on Your Hands”.  Mühlrad has written extensively for chamber ensembles and orchestras, as well as for theatre and film.  Through choral music, he has been able to achieve a unique expression of the mystical aspect of Jewish tradition. Kaddish holds a deeply personal connection to the composer; it tells the story of his grandfather's survival of the Holocaust.

name: Marta Cascales Alimbau
bio: Marta Cascales Alimbau, a Barcelona-born pianist and composer, creates music that blends classical roots with a contemporary, minimalist, and poetic essence, reminiscent of @Ólafur Arnalds, Max Richter, and Hania Rani. Her peaceful and intimate compositions offer a calming refuge. Her discography includes the EP Light-House (2018) the LP Anoche (2020), and singles released through New York label Sonder House and Prisma Music. Marta's track Almost Here has been featured on Spotify Editorial Playlists like @Piano in the Background1 and Coffee and Piano, reaching 2M streams. She also appears on the Official Piano Day Album compilation released via Nils Frahm's label LEITER, alongside artists as @Yann Tiersen and @Liam Mour. It’s also remarkable her parallel project with singer-songwriter Grauwi , featuring their acclaimed debut album Contradictions, and the invitation by legendary label Deutsche Grammophon to be part of the album 'Fragments'. She has performed at notable festivals and venues such as Trans Musicales (FR), Piano City Milano Festival (IT), Kosmoskonzerte Berlin (GE), and Rockwood Music Hall (New York). On stage she exudes raw emotion and charisma while dazzling fans with her exquisite piano playing. She studied composition and piano at the Royal Conservatoire of Antwerp and Taller de Músics Barcelona, and has been a resident artist in San Francisco, Florence, and Tokyo. Marta is one of five emerging artists supported by Creative Europe of the European Union.

name: Dardust
bio: Dardust, aka Dario Faini, is one of the most acclaimed pianists and composers of his generation. His music has featured at global events including the Olympics, the Super Bowl, the NBA All-Star Game and an Apple Product Launch Keynote. As an exceptional songwriter and producer, he has scored numerous Italian hits, earning over 100 Platinum records and two victories at the Sanremo Festival.  He has released five albums blending piano and electronics: 7, Birth, S.A.D. Storm and Drugs, Duality and Urban Impressionism (2024), developing a distinctive style that challenges the boundaries between classical and contemporary music.  His music has reached international audiences, from Eurovision to major festivals, where he has opened for Lana Del Rey and Dua Lipa. In 2026, he composed Fantasia Italiana, the official soundtrack of the Milano Cortina Winter Olympic Games, celebrating Italian musical tradition and the iconic locations hosting the event.  In May 2026, he unveiled SommersiVo, an immersive sound installation at the Venice Pavilion for the 61st International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, merging music, artificial intelligence and an underwater environment.  Since late 2024, Dardust has toured with Urban Impressionism, a live project merging music and brutalist architecture. With over 80 concerts across Italy and Europe, the tour has also featured eight sold-out performances of Piano Concerto N.1, his first original composition for piano and orchestra.

name: Lambert
bio: Lambert is a Berlin-based pianist, composer and producer from Hamburg.  Lambert’s sixth album False is where everything changes for the genre-defying pianist. He first emerged with 2014’s self-titled album, which ignited the world of contemporary classical music – largely because it showed Lambert was a talent too broad to be pigeonholed as “contemporary classical pianist”.   In the five years since, Lambert released an album a year, also working with English folk singer Brookln Dekker of Rue Royale on the acclaimed album We Share Phenomena and fellow German visionary Stimming on the magical EP Exodus. He also composed several wonderful soundtracks. Live shows became an essential event, evenings of mystique and wonder as the dazzling musicianship of Lambert’s trio was conveyed while wearing matching horned Sardinian masks. Never seen without his mask as his music became yet more accomplished, speculation naturally intensified as to Lambert’s identity. Rumours grew that Lambert had opened a camp where he trained promising musicians how to “become Lambert”. In exploring the meanings of identity, Lambert’s 2019 album was called True. Calling his new album False seems a natural next step – and it’s a stunning record, where Lambert explodes all the known truths of Lambert’s Universe, or the Lambiverse, if you will.

name: Bea Boethius
bio: I change what I cannot accept.  I accept what I cannot change.  Within this paradigm, my music lives and breathes and shapes itself. And when it leaves a footprint, I capture it. For me.  For you.  Here is my heart.

name: Jeremy Hababou
bio: Jeremy Hababou, born in 1989, is a pianist and composer with a unique style. His music invites introspection, inner journeys, and daydreaming.  As a jazz-trained pianist, Jeremy Hababou has released two albums, "Run Away" and "Nuances," which received positive acclaim from both the media and festivals, as well as the public.  He is also a composer and performer of film music, including the renowned film "Eiffel" with Romain Duris and Emma Mackey, as well as "L’empereur de Paris," where he performed Marco Beltrami's music with a grand orchestra.  Additionally, Jeremy Hababou has ventured into theater, collaborating with notable figures such as Laure Calamy (César Award winner for Best Actress in 2021) and Michel Vuillermoz of the Comédie Française.  In 2023, Jeremy Hababou released his album "Il était une fois" on the naïve label. Currently, the artist is releasing a series of ten singles under the project "Fragments" and performs a show titled "Unorthodox Pianist."

name: Brad Kella
bio: When Brad Kella won Channel 4’s The Piano, a national televised talent show, he knew his life would change forever. And so it has proved. From being homeless and playing street pianos to make ends meet, he’s now living out his childhood dream of performing his own music to audiences of thousands in the world’s greatest concert halls. ‘It’s been the best feeling in the entire world,’ he says from his Liverpool home, where he lives with his partner and two young children. ‘If I could put that feeling from those shows into a bottle and sell it, I’d be a billionaire.’  One of music’s most extraordinary, inspiring and freethinking talents, Brad’s career has taken off since he was named the winner by superstar pianists Lang Lang and Mika. He has signed with the independent record label Modern Sky, appeared at Classic FM Live at the Royal Albert Hall and performed his own sell-out show at Liverpool’s famed Philharmonic Hall – a real pinch-me moment.

name: Evgeny Grinko
bio: Artist website: https://evgenygrinko.net  Born in Zukhovsky, Russia in 1985, Evgeny Grinko's early exposure to music came from films and cartoons. Fascinated by Russian rockabilly and surf music, he received his first guitar as a teenager, inspired by Western bands like Prodigy and Nirvana. At 16, Evgeny began playing guitar seriously and later switched to drums, joining indie noise bands in Moscow. A pivotal moment occurred when he discovered the piano, teaching himself to play. His composition "Valse" went viral on Facebook in 2010, propelling him into the contemporary classical music scene.  Evgeny has since released four albums and six EPs, with his work often incorporating cinematic elements and a mix of humour, sadness, and longing. His music has gained widespread popularity, with over 400 million streams on Spotify and 200 million views on YouTube. In 2022, after opposing the invasion of Ukraine, Evgeny left Russia and eventually settled in Berlin. Despite these challenges, he continues to create music, with his latest EP, "Outtakes II," released in 2024, and a new album set for release in 2025.

name: Nitin Sawhney
bio: One of the most talented and recognized producers and songwriters in the British electronic and fusion music scene, Nitin Sawhney is also a respected actor, writer, and scriptwriter. Conceiving daring theme combinations of electronica-style beats with gleaming pieces of Asian influences driven within trip-hop and jazzy styles, Sawhney delivers exclusive and overwhelming sound pieces, enlightened by his indubitable creative insight. Following an education in the Kent region of England, obscured by the militant presence of racist organizations, Sawhney finally turned to music, therefore aiming to overcome ruling and disquieting racial boundaries. During subsequent years, he went on to study law at Liverpool University before moving to London. It was there that, alongside Sanjeev Bhaskar, he created The Secret Asians, a radio show that eventually evolved into an award-winning TV series. Although he dedicated most of his time to the TV business, Sawhney never neglected his musical dream. He first joined James Taylor, with whom he played a series of dates across the U.K. alongside Taylor's quartet. Following the experience, Sawhney decided to form his own band, the Jazztones, by that time playing on concerts headlined by DJs like Gilles Peterson. After yet another collaboration, by then with Talvin Singh (with whom he assembled the Tihai Trio), the British creator decided to make it on his own, releasing his debut album, Spirit Dance, on his own label in 1993. A few months later, he signed a contract with Outcaste Records, for which he released one of his most acclaimed recordings, Migration, in 1995. Following a year of incessant work, the album Displacing the Priest arrived in record stores, again demonstrating his exceptional creative skills. During this period, Sawhney continued to dedicate part of his time to writing soundtracks for acclaimed TV series and theater plays, and remixing works for artists like Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan. During the following months, Sawhney recorded his long-awaited fourth album, Beyond Skin, released in late 1999. Coming after an extensive touring season across the U.K. and Europe alongside artists including Sting, Sawhney recorded his fifth studio record. Prophesy arrived in 2001, again earning glowing reviews from the media. Sawhney remained busy throughout the 2000s, releasing works such as Human, Philtre, Love Undersound, and One Zero, as well as mix albums like In the Mind of Nitin Sawhney and Fabriclive.15. By 2015 Sawhney had received numerous awards, including four honorary doctorates, two Ivor Novello nominations, and two U.K. Asian Music Awards; 2015 also marked the release of Sawhney's tenth studio album, Dystopian Dream. Two years later, he received a lifetime achievement Award from the Ivor Novello Awards, released Live at Ronnie Scott's, and provided the score for the Andy Serkis-directed Breathe. His twelfth studio album, Immigrants, arrived in 2021; positioned as a sequel to his 1999 album Beyond Skin, the record celebrated immigration worldwide. ~ Mario Mesquita Borges, Rovi

name: George Winston
bio: George Winston is undeniably a household name. He’s inspired fans and musicians alike with his singular solo acoustic piano songs for more than 40 years while selling 15 million albums. A tireless road warrior, live performance for Winston is akin to breathing. Winston’s music is evocative, offering us all a chance to take a step back from our perpetually busy lives and let our minds adventurously wander. His latest album, “NIGHT,” is where things truly come alive for Winston. Whether on a performance stage, in a midnight recording session, practicing late at night, driving solo through urban city spaces, or witnessing nature grow under the moonlight, Winston celebrates his renowned 50-year career with this interstellar new recording.  George Winston’s classic albums, Autumn and December, are perennial favorites, along with Winter into Spring, Summer, 2017’s Spring Carousel – A Cancer Research Benefit, as well as two volumes of the compositions of Vince Guaraldi, two volumes of benefit albums for the Gulf Coast disasters, and six other solo piano albums. He recently released his 17th solo piano album, "Beloved: A Celebration of Professor Longhair", via Dancing Cat Records/Valley Entertainment. The album is available now at GeorgeWinston.com.

name: Marco Velocci
bio: Ciao a tutti, sono Marco Velocci. Il pianoforte è il mio respiro. Sono un pianista che ama spaziare tra classica, contemporanea, jazz e pop, ma c'è qualcosa di più profondo che mi spinge a suonare: il bisogno di condividere. Scelgo di eseguire le musiche che più mi emozionano, quelle che mi toccano l’anima, perché sento che non posso tenerle solo per me. Se non le condividessi con voi, scoppierei di emozione. Ogni nota è un pezzo del mio cuore che spero possa vibrare anche nel vostro. Se sei qui, probabilmente hai ascoltato la mia ultima release I'm Not the Only One (Soft Felt Piano) o la mia playlist Musica Pop Italiana - Piano Version. La mia musica è il risultato di una ricerca artistica costante e di un amore incondizionato per il pianoforte. Vi invito a viaggiare con me in questo fantastico mondo. FOLLOW ME ON THE BEST MUSIC STREAMING PLATFORMS: https://linktr.ee/marco.velocci FOLLOW ME ON SOCIAL MEDIA: https://lnk.bio/marco.velocci Collaborate with BabuZzle s.a.s. and Giovanni Valle Edizioni Musicali s.a.s. My Favorite Song: Spring Waltz My Album: Marco Velocci: The Beat "La vita imita l'arte molto più di quanto l'arte imiti la vita." (Oscar Wilde) Seguimi per non perdere il prossimo viaggio.

name: Cécile Seraud
bio: Cécile Seraud is a French pianist & composer. Inspired by composers/artists like Chopin, Sigur Rós or Yann Tiersen, the pianist from Brittany (France) feels comfortable with her piano as much as her surfboard. Cécile Seraud's debut album is an intimate recording which will touch the heart of the listener. "Shoden"makes its way between the joyful and yet misty melancholy of the attractive Brittany,and the intimate musical atmospheres of the icy lands of the frozen North. It' s like a contemplative journey which leads with a delicate touch to the deepest part of the heart."

name: Pêtr Aleksänder
bio: Pêtr Aleksänder create a considered sound, controlled in its execution, by way of purposefully limiting the instruments at their disposal to piano and strings, but never at the expense of the raw, emotional impact that a simple yet incisive sound can deliver. Early recordings such as Sans Souci quickly caught the attention of streaming services, the wider public and in turn, renowned indie label Nettwerk, who offered the band a record deal which was signed in December 2017. The band released a music video for “Bells” in September 2017, featuring aspiring dancer Jacob Lang, a finalist in the contemporary dance category of BBC Young Dancer 2017. A support tour with Norwegian singer Susanne Sundfør in October 2017 saw the band perform across the UK and in Sweden. The live show consisted of the looping of various instruments and the re-imagining of arrangements, all before a backdrop of visuals created by the band themselves. The band's debut album "Closer, Still" is out now

name: Yulianna Avdeeva
bio: Described by the Financial Times as an artist who is "able to let the music breathe", Yulianna Avdeeva, who gained international recognition when she won First Prize in the Chopin Competition in 2010, is always uncompromisingly and profoundly devoted purely to the music itself. Conjuring an impeccable combination of clarity, energy and elegance, she wins audiences with compelling honesty, wit and musical judgement.

name: Tony Ann
bio: Tony Ann is a virtuoso solo pianist who seamlessly blends contemporary and classical styles. A harmony connoisseur, he pushes the boundaries of neoclassical and popular music, creating emotionally rich compositions using the full range of the piano’s 88 keys. With over 1 billion views, 300 million streams, and more than 6 million followers on social media, Tony has captivated a global audience and inspired a new generation through his viral “#playthatword” series and his acclaimed debut album EMOTIONS (Deluxe) released with Decca Records France (Universal Music Group). Tony’s world tour continues to sell out venues across the globe, from Helsinki to Kuala Lumpur, Chicago to Melbourne, São Paulo to Bilbao. In 2024, he received multiple standing ovations at sold-out concerts in prestigious venues such as the Olympia in Paris and the Barbican in London. Tony’s critically acclaimed album 360° showcases the emotional and stylistic range that defines his artistry. Following this, he will release a collaborative orchestral project with genre-defying duo ARKAI, reimagining Tony’s most beloved compositions through additional instrumentation. His single ICARUS was recently certified diamond, with over 50 million streams (excluding France), affirming his global impact. Praised by the press, Tony was named “the new piano star” by Les Échos. His recognition continues to grow across the music industry, with increasing support from media and fellow artists alike.

name: Ophelia Wilde
bio: hey, my name is ophelia, and i don't really exist outside your imagination, but i play the piano and romanticize my life as much as possible anyway. i love reading, secret romance and haunted libraries,  where the scent of aged books and the faint echoes of forgotten stories linger in the air.  when i’m not lost in daydreams of distant realities, you'll most likely find me sitting in the quiet corner of the college library. as exam season draws near, i’ll be sitting amidst towering bookshelves, diligently studying, my mind alight with the pursuit of knowledge.  while i can only share my piano music here, i invite you to join my fictional life on my socials, where i reveal more about my captivating dark academia existence <3 yours, ophelia

name: Peter Gregson
bio: When an artist with a well-established career, successful past recordings, and a large global following releases a self-titled album, it usually points to a creative high point, a stylistic breakthrough, or even a back-to-basics moment. When Peter Gregson chose to self-title his newest album, he had that kind of significance in mind. The award-winning Scottish cellist and composer says Peter Gregson, a collection of nine contemporary songs without words for cello and synthesizer due April 11th on Decca Records US, is “the closest to what I hear in my head that I’ve ever reached.”

name: Luna
bio: From tranquil to more complex solo arrangements, the story of Luna is about serenity and the passion to reflect the colorful aspects of nature in the most minimalistic way. The eccentric and calm vibe of Luna is cached perfectly by the French choreographer. In reciprocity with the dance and audio, visual artist Jesse Bom made several videos reflecting the purity of nature. Luna is proudly part of the roster of the Neo-Classical label Morning Classical (with artists like Challem, and Ruben Gerards). Listen here to all of the compositions in one playlist: Luna - Full Discography

name: Yana
bio: Based in Gdańsk, Poland, YANA (Joanna Bieńkowska) is a violinist, pianist and composer whose music brings together classical instrumentation, piano, strings and electronic textures. Her work moves between intimate, minimalist compositions and more expansive arrangements, reflecting an ongoing exploration of sound, texture and emotional expression. YANA’s third album, Quiet Rebellion, is out on 19 February 2027 via OPIA Community.  On Quiet Rebellion, YANA turns inward in response to a world that feels increasingly loud, fractured and difficult to process. The album was born from anger, sadness and resentment in the face of violence, social unrest and the erosion of basic ethical values. Rather than reproducing the noise around her, YANA transforms it into something personal: an inner rebellion expressed through music, rooted in the belief that art can become a voice for change.  Pre-save album: https://yana.lnk.to/QuietRebellion

name: Ben Laver
bio: Ben Laver is a British composer and contemporary classical solo artist, known for his emotionally resonant piano compositions. His work has garnered over 50 million streams and secured more than 100 editorial playlist placements across major platforms. As the co-founder of Box of Toys Audio, Ben has created music for leading global brands such as Gucci, LEGO, EA Games, and Christian Louboutin, specializing in scoring for television, film, and branding.  Ben’s love for music began at the age of four, watching his father play the piano. He learned by ear, exploring how harmonies, melodies, and rhythms could evoke emotion. These formative experiences shaped his belief that music is a language that communicates beyond words. After graduating from The Guildhall School of Music and Drama, Ben immersed himself in the world of media composition, where his classical training and passion for sound experimentation allowed him to develop a distinctive voice as both a composer and sonic architect.  Ben’s approach to music is driven by a desire to break free from traditional rules, blending classical instrumentation with textures, electronics, and reverbs to create emotionally compelling soundscapes. His work continues to challenge conventions, whether in his solo piano pieces or his scores for visual media, always aiming to communicate through sound in innovative and deeply personal ways.

name: Alex North
bio: American composer Alex North hardly needed films to enhance his reputation. A graduate of Julliard and the pupil of such musical heavyweights as Ernst Toch and Aaron Copland, North was responsible for the incidental music in several major Broadway productions of the 1940s, notably Death of a Salesman. He also composed for the ballet, for symphony orchestra, and even for Benny Goodman. North's earliest film work consisted of the scores for documentary films, an activity he engaged in from 1937 through the early 1950s. His first feature-film score was for 20th Century-Fox's The 13th Letter; he followed this with a steady parade of scores for such memorable pictures as Viva Zapata (1952), The Rose Tattoo (1955), The Bad Seed (1956), Spartacus (1960), Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf (1967), Under the Volcano (1984) and Prizzi's Honor (1985). His most popular composition, "Unchained Melody" (for the 1955 prison picture Unchanged), received a whole new lease on life in 1990 thanks to the runaway hit film Ghost. Yet despite so impressive a resume, Alex North never received an Oscar in any of his 15 nominations. Finally, in 1986, the Academy threw him that guilt-absolving bone, the "Lifetime Achievement Award." Perhaps Alex North's most ambitious film score was the one nobody heard -- he was engaged by Stanley Kubrick to write the music for 2001: A Space Odyssey, only to have Kubrick rudely pull the rug from under him by substituting such classical pieces as "Thus Spake Zarathustra" and "The Blue Danube Waltz." With teeth clenched, Alex North wrote a terse article describing his frustration for Jerome Agel's 1969 compendium The Making of Kubrick's 2001.

name: ARSHA KAVIANI
bio: Arsha Kaviani is one of the most uniquely versatile pianists around. Born in the Middle East, Arsha grew up immersed in diverse musical genres, from Bach to Nirvana. This eclectic background shaped his imaginative and independent artistry.  Coming to the UK at the age of 15 and completing his classical training at Chetham's, Royal Northern College of Music, & the Royal College of Music whilst mentored by luminaries such as Sir Stephen Hough, Daniel Barenboim, Lang Lang, and Peter Donohoe, he received numerous accolades as BBC Music & ClassicFM's Rising Star, and one of International Piano's 30 Under 30 Best Pianists in The World.  Arsha's career features acclaimed performances with orchestras like the Tonhalle Zurich and The Royal Liverpool Philharmonic, and solo recitals in venues from London's Royal Albert Hall to recital halls in Moscow & Tokyo. His innovative approach challenges classical conventions, incorporating original compositions and audience-prompted improvisations into his performances.  Committed to making classical music accessible, Arsha is praised for his engaging and charismatic presentation. He frequently includes his own compositions in his programs and is sought after as a composer through his production company, Maison Musique Kaviani.  In Arsha’s musical world, classical repertoire intertwines with pop, jazz & Persian music, creating performances and compositions of exceptional wit and originality; one language spoken in different accents.
